provenance: Derived from public disease reference pages. Summaries, symptom lists, urgency and prevalence were generated by a language model and are estimates, not clinical data.

diseases.name: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
diseases.summary: A slow-growing bulge in the lower main artery of the belly can often go unnoticed for years, and some never burst. When symptoms do appear, they tend to involve deep belly or back discomfort and a pulsing sensation, and sudden severe pain signals a possible rupture that needs emergency care.

diseases.name: Absence seizure
diseases.summary: Absence seizures are brief episodes where a person suddenly loses awareness and stares into space for a few seconds, then recovers quickly. They occur mostly in school-age children, and many outgrow them in adolescence. Medication usually keeps them under control.

diseases.name: Acanthosis nigricans
diseases.summary: This skin condition causes areas in skin folds to turn darker and thicken, often taking on a soft, velvety texture. It is frequently linked to insulin resistance and excess body weight, though it can occasionally signal an internal disease that needs medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Achalasia
diseases.summary: This is a disorder of the gullet's movement, where the muscular tube fails to push food and drink down into the stomach. Material can pile up in the tube and sometimes come back up, often with a sour or bitter taste. Although the underlying damage can't be reversed, procedures through a scope, minimally invasive options, or surgery usually keep symptoms under control.

diseases.name: Achilles tendinitis
diseases.summary: Achilles tendinitis is inflammation of the tendon that connects the calf muscles to the heel bone, usually caused by overuse or repetitive strain. It typically produces pain and stiffness along the back of the ankle and lower leg, especially with activity. Symptoms often start gradually and may worsen if the tendon is ignored.

diseases.name: Achilles tendon rupture
diseases.summary: A tear in the strong tendon that links the calf muscles to the heel can happen when it is overstretched, most often during jumping or stop-and-go sports. Many people feel a pop and then sharp pain behind the ankle, and walking or pushing off on that foot becomes difficult. Surgery or non-surgical treatment can both work, so prompt medical evaluation is important.

diseases.name: ACL injury
diseases.summary: A torn or sprained ligament in the knee, usually caused by sudden stops, jumps, or quick changes of direction, often during sports. Many people feel or hear a pop at the time, followed by quick swelling and a sense that the knee may give way. Prompt medical evaluation is advised because nearby cartilage and other ligaments are often hurt too.

diseases.name: Acne
diseases.summary: Acne is a common skin problem in which pores become clogged, leading to a mix of blemishes that often appear on the face, chest, and upper back. It is especially frequent in teenagers but can occur at any age and tends to recur over time. Treatment is effective, and starting it early lowers the chance of lasting marks or emotional strain.

diseases.name: Acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma)
diseases.summary: This slow-growing, non-cancerous tumor forms on the nerve that carries hearing and balance signals from the inner ear to the brain. It typically affects one ear and often develops so gradually that early signs are overlooked. Its only confirmed risk factor is a parent with a specific inherited genetic condition.

diseases.name: Acromegaly
diseases.summary: A hormone imbalance in adults, usually from a benign pituitary growth, slowly enlarges the hands, feet, face and internal tissues over years. Because the changes creep in gradually, they are often missed for a long time. Early diagnosis matters because untreated cases can lead to diabetes, high blood pressure and sleep apnea.

diseases.name: Actinic keratosis
diseases.summary: A common, harmless-looking growth of the outer skin that appears on areas repeatedly exposed to sunlight, mostly in older adults with fair skin. Most patches stay small and do not spread quickly, but a minority can slowly change into a type of skin cancer, so they are worth having checked.

diseases.name: Acute coronary syndrome
diseases.summary: A sudden blockage in the blood supply to the heart muscle starves part of it of oxygen, and this spectrum ranges from a full heart attack to a milder form of reduced flow. It is a medical emergency, and symptoms often begin abruptly, most typically as pressure or discomfort in the chest. Women, older adults, and people with diabetes may experience it without obvious chest pain.

diseases.name: Acute flaccid myelitis (AFM)
diseases.summary: A rare condition that affects the nerve cells controlling muscles in the spinal cord, mostly in children. It tends to appear suddenly, often a few days after a cold-like or stomach illness, and can leave limbs weak or floppy. Because weakness can spread quickly and occasionally reach the breathing muscles, prompt medical assessment is important.

diseases.name: Acute kidney injury
diseases.summary: When the kidneys abruptly lose their ability to clean waste and excess fluid from the blood, dangerous substances and chemical imbalances can build up quickly. It is most often seen in hospitalized patients, especially those in intensive care, and it can frequently be reversed if recognized and treated promptly. Because it is usually triggered by another illness or event, the condition often needs urgent medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Acute liver failure
diseases.summary: A rapid loss of liver function that unfolds over days to weeks in someone without earlier liver disease. It is usually triggered by a viral hepatitis infection or a medication overdose, and it is a medical emergency that needs hospital care, sometimes ending in a transplant.

diseases.name: Acute lymphocytic leukemia
diseases.summary: A blood and bone marrow cancer in which the marrow produces large numbers of immature white cells instead of healthy mature ones, progressing quickly. It is the most frequent childhood cancer and is usually curable in children, though outcomes are considerably worse in adults. Symptoms mostly stem from crowding out normal blood cells, leading to bleeding, infections, anemia and enlarged lymph nodes.

diseases.name: Acute myelogenous leukemia
diseases.summary: A fast-moving blood and bone marrow cancer that starts in the myeloid cell line, which normally matures into red cells, white cells, and platelets. It is the most frequent acute leukemia in adults and becomes much more likely with age. Symptoms often overlap with everyday infections, so clinicians usually rule those out first.

diseases.name: Acute sinusitis
diseases.summary: Acute sinusitis is a short-term swelling of the air-filled cavities behind the nose and cheeks, often following a cold, that traps mucus and causes stuffiness and facial discomfort. Most cases settle on their own within a couple of weeks, though a minority involve a bacterial infection that needs treatment. Warning signs such as eye swelling, high fever, or vision changes call for prompt medical review.

diseases.name: Adamantinoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer of the long bones, most often in the shinbone, that tends to grow slowly but can return after treatment or spread. Early signs are usually lasting pain, swelling, or a lump over the affected bone, sometimes with limping or a fracture. Diagnosis requires imaging and a biopsy because these symptoms overlap with many more common causes.

diseases.name: Addison's disease
diseases.summary: A long-term disorder in which damage to the adrenal glands leads to low output of cortisol and often aldosterone. Its warning signs tend to creep in gradually and are easy to dismiss at first. Without hormone replacement, a serious illness or injury can trigger a dangerous collapse.

diseases.name: Adenomyosis
diseases.summary: A condition in which cells that normally line the uterus grow into its muscular wall, causing the womb to thicken and often enlarge. It mainly affects women in their 40s and 50s and tends to cause heavy, painful periods and pelvic discomfort. Symptoms often ease after menopause.

diseases.name: Adjustment disorders
diseases.summary: Adjustment disorder is an outsized emotional and behavioral response to a identifiable life stressor, such as a job loss, move, or relationship strain. Symptoms usually appear within three months of the event and often fade within about six months after the stress ends, though they can persist when the stressor continues. Because it can disrupt work, school, and relationships and may carry a risk of suicidal thinking, getting professional support is worthwhile.

diseases.name: Adnexal tumors and masses
diseases.summary: Abnormal growths that develop on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or the supporting tissue beside the uterus are usually non-cancerous, though a minority are malignant. Many cause no noticeable signs and are discovered during an unrelated exam, while others produce pelvic discomfort, digestive or urinary changes, or unusual bleeding. Doctors typically confirm them through physical examination, imaging, and blood tests, and the approach depends on size and underlying cause.

diseases.name: Adrenal cancer
diseases.summary: Adrenal cancer is a rare tumor that begins in the small glands sitting atop the kidneys, which produce hormones governing metabolism, blood pressure, and immune function. When caught early it may be curable, but once it has spread the aim shifts toward slowing progression. Many affected people have excess hormone effects, most often from cortisol, that show up as physical changes.

diseases.name: Adrenoleukodystrophy
diseases.summary: This is a rare inherited disorder in which the body cannot break down certain fats, so they accumulate and damage the protective covering of nerve fibers, mainly in the brain and spinal cord. It also can impair the adrenal glands and cause hormone shortage. It mostly affects boys, appearing as a fast-moving childhood form or a slower adult form.

diseases.name: Adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)
diseases.summary: Adult ADHD is a long-lasting condition in which attention, impulse control, and activity levels cause ongoing trouble at work, at school, and in relationships. Its roots go back to childhood, though it is often not recognized until adulthood. Treatment usually combines medication, counseling, and care for any coexisting mental health conditions.

diseases.name: Adult Still disease
diseases.summary: This autoimmune-type inflammatory arthritis brings recurring high fevers, a body rash, and painful, swollen joints, sometimes with a sore throat. Symptoms can come and go, and the disease may appear once and resolve, persist, or relapse. Joint damage, especially in the wrists, is a concern, so prompt medical evaluation is advised.

diseases.name: Age spots (liver spots)
diseases.summary: Dark, flat or slightly raised patches on sun-exposed skin that appear gradually with age and cumulative sun exposure. They are harmless in most people, though a doctor should check any spot that changes shape, color, or size.

diseases.name: Agoraphobia
diseases.summary: Agoraphobia is an anxiety condition in which a person becomes so afraid of situations where escape or help might feel hard to reach that they start steering clear of public places, crowds, or even leaving home. The fear often grows out of earlier panic episodes and can narrow daily life considerably. Treatment, typically talk-based therapy combined with medication, tends to work well.

diseases.name: Airplane ear
diseases.summary: A pressure imbalance between the middle ear and the surrounding air, most often during plane descent, causes discomfort and a sense of blockage in the ear. The condition usually resolves on its own once the pressure equalizes. Persistent pain, bleeding, or lasting hearing changes call for medical evaluation.

diseases.name: AL amyloidosis
diseases.summary: This is a rare, serious disorder in which misfolded antibody fragments deposit as an abnormal protein throughout the body and gradually impair vital organs. Because the symptoms overlap with many everyday illnesses, it is often recognized late, and it most often appears in people in their sixties. Early medical review can help prevent further organ injury.

diseases.name: Albinism
diseases.summary: A inherited condition in which the body makes little or no melanin, leading to very pale skin, hair and eyes along with significant vision difficulties. Affected people are highly sensitive to sunlight and need protection for their skin and eyes, though the condition itself cannot be cured.

diseases.name: Alcohol intolerance
diseases.summary: A reduced ability to break down alcohol causes a buildup of its byproduct, acetaldehyde, after drinking. Most people notice a rapid reaction with flushing and stuffiness, and some also feel sick or have a racing heartbeat. The reaction is usually harmless but unpleasant, and it is most common in people of East Asian ancestry.

diseases.name: Alcohol poisoning
diseases.summary: Alcohol poisoning happens when a large amount of alcohol is consumed quickly, disrupting vital functions such as breathing, heart rate, temperature, and the gag reflex. It can progress to unconsciousness or death, so any suspicion of it calls for immediate emergency care rather than waiting it out.

diseases.name: Alcohol use disorder
diseases.summary: Alcohol use disorder is a condition where a person loses control over drinking, keeps drinking despite harm to health, work, or relationships, and may need more alcohol to feel its effect or experience withdrawal when stopping. It ranges from mild to severe and can be treated, and getting help early tends to prevent escalation into serious problems.

diseases.name: Alcoholic hepatitis (Alcohol-associated hepatitis)
diseases.summary: Alcohol-associated hepatitis is inflammation that injures liver cells, typically in people who have drunk heavily for years or who binge drink. Stopping alcohol and restoring nutrition are the core treatments, since continued drinking sharply raises the chance of liver failure and death. Warning signs include yellowing of the skin and eyes, digestive upset, and pain under the right ribs.

diseases.name: Allergies
diseases.summary: Allergies occur when the body's defense system overreacts to a harmless substance, tagging it as a threat and triggering inflammation in the skin, nose, airways, or gut. Reactions range from mild irritation to a dangerous, whole-body emergency. Most allergies cannot be cured, but medications and other treatments can ease symptoms.

diseases.name: Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency
diseases.summary: A genetic disorder in which the body produces too little of a protective lung protein, or a malformed version of it, allowing damage to the lungs, liver, skin, and blood vessels. Many people who carry it never develop problems, while others may show lung or liver disease, often starting in adulthood. Early detection and proper management can slow the damage and improve daily life.

diseases.name: Alpha-gal syndrome
diseases.summary: Alpha-gal syndrome is an allergy to meat and other animal-derived products, often acquired after a tick bite. Reactions usually surface a few hours after eating, and can range from mild skin symptoms to dangerous breathing problems. Avoiding the triggering foods is currently the main way to manage it, so anyone with suspicious reactions should see a clinician.

diseases.name: Alzheimer's disease
diseases.summary: Alzheimer's is the leading cause of dementia, driven by abnormal protein deposits that gradually destroy brain cells and shrink the brain. It starts with trouble recalling recent events and progresses to broader losses in thinking, judgment, behavior, and daily functioning. There is currently no cure, though some medications can ease symptoms or slow decline.

diseases.name: Ameloblastoma
diseases.summary: This is a slow-growing, non-spreading growth in the jaw, usually near the back teeth, that often produces no noticeable signs at first. When it does cause problems, it typically shows up as swelling or discomfort in the jaw, and it can gradually push teeth out of place if it goes untreated. Diagnosis and removal are usually handled by a dentist or oral surgeon.

diseases.name: Amenorrhea
diseases.summary: Amenorrhea means a person's periods are absent, either because they have never started or because they have stopped for several cycles after having been regular. Pregnancy is the usual reason in the second case, while hormone imbalances and differences in reproductive anatomy account for many others. Anyone who has missed three cycles in a row, or who has not started menstruating by a certain age, should speak with a clinician.

diseases.name: Amnesia
diseases.summary: This condition involves losing the ability to store and recall information, most noticeably new experiences, while older, deeply learned knowledge often survives. It usually follows damage to brain regions that handle memory, such as from head injury, stroke, seizures, or heavy long-term drinking. Because it can be lasting, any unexplained memory problem or confusion calls for prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Ampullary cancer
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer that begins in the small opening where the bile duct and pancreatic duct meet the small intestine. It is more often found in older adults, and some inherited gene changes raise the risk. Treatment usually centers on surgical removal, sometimes combined with radiation or chemotherapy.

diseases.name: Amyloidosis
diseases.summary: This is a group of uncommon conditions in which abnormal protein deposits gradually accumulate in tissues and interfere with organ function. Which symptoms appear depends on the organs involved, and while some forms respond to treatment, others can progress to serious organ damage.

diseases.name: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)
diseases.summary: A progressive disease of the nerve cells controlling movement, where muscle weakness spreads and worsens over the years and eventually affects speaking, swallowing, and breathing. It usually starts in a limb or with changes in speech or swallowing, and it is not curable at present. Most cases have no identified inherited cause, and risk climbs with age.

diseases.name: Anal cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that forms in the short passage at the lower end of the rectum, usually following a long-lasting infection with a high-risk strain of HPV. It may cause no warning signs at first, and its symptoms are easy to confuse with hemorrhoids. Diagnosis depends on an exam and a tissue sample, and treatment often combines medication, radiation, and sometimes surgery.

diseases.name: Anal fissure
diseases.summary: A small tear in the moist lining of the anus, usually triggered by hard stools or straining, tends to hurt during and after bowel movements and may leave traces of blood. Most cases settle with dietary fiber, warm soaks, and sometimes medication, with surgery reserved for persistent cases. Anyone with rectal pain or blood after a bowel movement should have it checked by a clinician.

diseases.name: Anal fistula
diseases.summary: A tunnel forms between the inner anal canal and the skin around the anus, usually after an infected gland produces an abscess that drains and leaves a channel behind. The channel stays open and tends to leak fluid, and it generally needs surgical repair. The condition is more frequent in men and in people around 40, particularly those with Crohn's disease.

diseases.name: Anal itching
diseases.summary: Itching around the anus is a frequent complaint that can be uncomfortable and embarrassing. It can stem from infections, hemorrhoids, ongoing loose stools, or skin irritation, and it often gets worse at night or in warm, damp weather. Most people recover fully once the underlying trigger is identified and treated.

diseases.name: Anaphylaxis
diseases.summary: Anaphylaxis is a sudden, whole-body allergic reaction that can progress within minutes and may block breathing or drop blood pressure. It is treated as a medical emergency and requires immediate epinephrine and emergency care.

diseases.name: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare, slow-growing cancer of the immune system's T cells that often appears as swollen lymph nodes and can also involve the skin, breast implant tissue, or abdomen. Its features differ by subtype, and some forms show up only years after a breast implant is placed. Anyone with worrying lumps, persistent fevers, or unexplained weight loss should see a clinician.

diseases.name: Anemia
diseases.summary: Low red blood cell or hemoglobin levels leave tissues short of oxygen, so the body tends to show fatigue, breathlessness and pallor first. Many people with mild cases feel nothing until the drop becomes larger, and sometimes it is found incidentally during a routine test or blood donation. Persistent unexplained tiredness or breathlessness is a reason to book a medical visit.

diseases.name: Aneurysms
diseases.summary: Aneurysms are weak, enlarged spots in an artery wall that can form in the brain, chest, belly, or limbs. Many cause no noticeable signs, but when one grows or ruptures, it can produce pain, neurological changes, or sudden life-threatening bleeding.

diseases.name: Angelman syndrome
diseases.summary: Angelman syndrome is a rare inherited disorder that affects brain and nerve function, caused by a problem with a gene passed down from the mother. It usually becomes noticeable in infancy through slowed development, then brings speech difficulties, movement and balance problems, and often seizures. Affected children are frequently cheerful and easily excited, and while the condition is lifelong, therapies can help with development and communication.

diseases.name: Angina
diseases.summary: Angina is chest discomfort caused by the heart muscle receiving less blood than it needs, usually because of coronary artery disease. It is a common reason for doctor visits, and it can look like heartburn, so unexplained chest pain should always be checked promptly. Chest pain that lingers beyond a few minutes or fails to ease with rest or medication needs emergency help.

diseases.name: Angiosarcoma
diseases.summary: Angiosarcoma is an uncommon, aggressive cancer that starts in the cells lining blood or lymph vessels. It most often appears in the skin, scalp, breast, or in limbs previously treated with radiation. Patients usually first notice a changing skin mark or a swelling that does not go away.

diseases.name: Ankylosing spondylitis
diseases.summary: A long-lasting inflammatory condition that mainly affects the lower spine and the joints linking the spine to the pelvis, usually starting in early adulthood. Over time it can stiffen and limit movement in the back and sometimes involve other joints, tendons, and the eyes. Symptoms often feel worse after rest and ease with activity.

diseases.name: Anorexia nervosa
diseases.summary: This is an eating disorder in which a person's body weight is kept well below what is healthy for them, driven by a strong dread of gaining weight and tight control over food. Malnutrition can blunt a person's awareness of how sick they are, so affected people often do not seek help on their own. Although it is treatable, it carries a high risk of serious physical harm, so prompt care matters.

diseases.name: Anorgasmia in women
diseases.summary: Some women find they reach orgasm later than expected, less often, or with weaker intensity, even with adequate arousal, and feel bothered by it. Whether this matters depends on personal distress, since orgasm patterns vary widely and change over time. Contributing factors can include emotional or relationship issues, medical conditions, or medications, and many treatment options exist.

diseases.name: Anterior vaginal prolapse (cystocele)
diseases.summary: A bladder that sags downward into the front wall of the vagina, typically because the tissues holding it in place have loosened over time. Many women with a mild case never notice anything, while others feel pressure, a bulge, or trouble with urination. Management ranges from monitoring and pelvic exercises to a support device or surgery for bothersome cases.

diseases.name: Anthrax
diseases.summary: Anthrax is a serious infection caused by a spore-forming bacterium that gets into the body through broken skin, the airways, or the gut. The skin form often begins as an itchy bump that becomes a painless sore with a dark center, while the inhaled and digestive forms can start like a mild flu and then worsen fast. Because it can become fatal quickly, any suspected exposure or compatible symptoms call for immediate medical attention.

diseases.name: Antibiotic associated diarrhea
diseases.summary: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea is loose or watery stools that begin during or shortly after a course of antibiotics, caused by disruption of the normal gut bacteria. Most cases are mild and resolve after the medicine is stopped, but a more serious bowel infection can occur and needs prompt evaluation.

diseases.name: Antiphospholipid syndrome
diseases.summary: An autoimmune disorder in which the immune system produces antibodies that make blood more prone to forming clots. Clots can block veins or arteries and may also cause pregnancy complications. Symptoms depend mostly on where clots form, so they can range from a swollen leg to breathing trouble or a stroke-like event.

diseases.name: Antisocial personality disorder
diseases.summary: This personality disorder involves a long-standing disregard for others' rights and feelings, often showing up as deceit, manipulation, and rule-breaking that begins in childhood. It is generally considered lifelong, though some harmful behaviors may lessen with age. People with it rarely seek help themselves, so a clinician usually needs to be involved.

diseases.name: Anxiety disorders
diseases.summary: Anxiety disorders involve intense, lasting worry or fear that go beyond what a situation warrants and can include sudden peaks of panic. These feelings can disrupt work, relationships, and daily routines, and people often start avoiding triggers. Treatment is effective, and seeking care early generally leads to better outcomes.

diseases.name: Aortic aneurysm
diseases.summary: Aortic aneurysms are abnormal swellings of the body's largest artery, most often in the belly or chest. Many stay silent for years and are discovered by chance during imaging. The main danger is that the swelling splits or ruptures, which can cause sudden, life-threatening internal bleeding.

diseases.name: Aortic dissection
diseases.summary: This is a life-threatening emergency in which the inner lining of the body's largest artery splits, and blood forces its way between the wall layers. It is most often linked to long-standing high blood pressure or weakened artery walls, and it can block branch vessels or rupture the aorta. Anyone with these symptoms needs emergency care right away.

diseases.name: Aortic valve disease
diseases.summary: Narrowing or stiffening of the aortic valve, or leaking backward through it, limits how well blood leaves the heart for the rest of the body. Many people feel nothing for years, and symptoms that do appear often reflect strain on the heart or heart failure. Chest discomfort, fainting, or sudden breathlessness calls for urgent care.

diseases.name: Aortic valve regurgitation
diseases.summary: A leaky aortic valve lets blood slip backward from the main artery into the heart's main pumping chamber each beat, so the heart has to work harder to keep the body supplied. It often builds slowly over years with no warning, but it can also strike quickly, usually after an infection. Symptoms tend to appear once the leak is significant and frequently reflect heart failure.

diseases.name: Aortic valve stenosis
diseases.summary: A narrowing of the valve that sits between the heart's main pumping chamber and the body's largest artery means less blood gets pushed out to the body. Many people feel nothing for years, while others notice chest tightness, breathlessness, or fainting during exertion. Left untreated, the strain can progress to heart failure, so a doctor's evaluation is important when symptoms appear.

diseases.name: Aphasia
diseases.summary: Aphasia is a language disorder in which a person loses some ability to speak, understand, read, or write, usually because of damage to the brain's language areas. Stroke causes most cases, though head injury, tumors, and infections can also lead to it. How much each language skill is affected varies from person to person.

diseases.name: Aplastic anemia
diseases.summary: A rare bone marrow failure disorder in which the marrow stops producing enough red cells, white cells, and platelets. Because all three blood cell types drop together, people often feel tired and short of breath, bruise or bleed easily, and get infections more often than usual.

diseases.name: Appendicitis
diseases.summary: Appendicitis is swelling and infection of the small pouch attached to the large intestine, typically starting as pain near the navel that migrates to the lower right abdomen. It most often affects people in their teens through early thirties and usually requires antibiotics and removal of the appendix. Severe abdominal pain warrants immediate medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Appendix cancer
diseases.summary: An exceptionally uncommon malignancy arising from the small pouch at the start of the large bowel. It is frequently discovered by chance during an operation performed for suspected appendicitis, because early signs are faint or absent. Prognosis depends heavily on the tumor's type and stage, and slow-growing forms are often curable with surgery alone.

diseases.name: ARDS
diseases.summary: When the lungs' tiny air sacs fill with fluid after inflammation damages their lining, breathing becomes insufficient and oxygen fails to reach the blood in adequate amounts. This typically strikes people already hospitalized with serious illness or trauma, and it can be fatal, though survivors may recover fully or keep lasting lung damage. Anyone with these symptoms outside a medical setting needs emergency care immediately.

diseases.name: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
diseases.summary: This is a rare inherited disorder in which the heart muscle is gradually replaced by fat and scar tissue, disrupting normal rhythm and pumping strength. It can start in childhood or adulthood and may cause dangerous irregular heartbeats or lead to heart failure. Many affected people feel fine at first, and some are only diagnosed incidentally.

diseases.name: Arteriosclerosis / atherosclerosis
diseases.summary: Atherosclerosis is a form of artery hardening caused by plaque, a mix of fat and cholesterol, building up inside vessel walls. It often causes no signs early on, but as arteries narrow or clot, it can starve organs of blood and bring on heart or brain problems. Early checkups and lifestyle changes can slow or prevent serious outcomes.

diseases.name: Arteriovenous fistula
diseases.summary: An abnormal direct connection forms between an artery and a vein, skipping the small vessels that normally sit between them. It may be present from birth, follow an injury, or be created on purpose to give access for dialysis. Some people feel nothing, while others notice a buzzing sensation, swelling, or changes in the limb.

diseases.name: Arteriovenous malformation
diseases.summary: A tangled knot of abnormal vessels lets blood shortcut directly from arteries into veins, starving nearby tissue of oxygen. Many cases cause no symptoms and are discovered incidentally, but when the fragile vessels rupture, bleeding in the brain can produce headaches, seizures, and neurological decline. Any sudden or progressive neurological change warrants prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Arthritis
diseases.summary: Arthritis is an umbrella term for many joint conditions that cause pain, swelling, and reduced movement. The two most common forms are wear-and-tear cartilage loss and an autoimmune attack on the joint lining. Symptoms are usually managed with treatments aimed at easing discomfort and preserving daily function.

diseases.name: Asbestosis
diseases.summary: A long-term lung condition that develops after breathing in asbestos fibers, which slowly inflames and stiffens the lung tissue over years. It usually appears decades after the exposure and tends to worsen gradually, with breathing trouble and a persistent cough as the main complaints.

diseases.name: Ascariasis
diseases.summary: Ascariasis is an intestinal infection caused by a large roundworm that spreads when people swallow microscopic eggs found in soil, food, or water contaminated with human feces. Many infected people carry only a few worms and notice nothing. Heavier infections can cause digestive upset, and the larvae's journey through the lungs can produce coughing or wheezing.

diseases.name: Ascites
diseases.summary: Fluid gathering in the abdominal cavity can make the belly look puffed out and feel heavy or tight, and it often signals serious liver disease, though heart failure, some cancers, and pancreas problems can also cause it. Small amounts may be unnoticed, while larger buildups can crowd the diaphragm and make breathing harder. Persistent swelling of this kind usually needs medical evaluation and treatment aimed at the underlying cause.

diseases.name: Aspergillosis
diseases.summary: A fungal infection caused by molds in the Aspergillus genus, usually breathed in from the environment. It most often affects the lungs and sinuses, and it can spread through the body in people with weakened immune systems or underlying lung disease. Symptoms range from mild, long-lasting breathing problems to serious, fast-moving illness.

diseases.name: Asthma
diseases.summary: Asthma is a long-term condition where the airways in the lungs tighten, swell, and fill with extra mucus, making breathing hard. It cannot be cured, but with ongoing medical care and medication the symptoms can usually be kept under control. Attacks can occasionally become life-threatening, so worsening breathlessness needs prompt attention.

diseases.name: Asthma attack
diseases.summary: A sudden flare of asthma that makes it hard to pull air into the lungs, usually signaled by breathlessness, chest squeezing, coughing and a whistling sound on breathing out. Warning signs appear on a home peak flow meter and in how the person can talk, and it can turn dangerous quickly, so timely treatment matters.

diseases.name: Astigmatism
diseases.summary: Astigmatism is a very common eye condition in which the front surface of the eye or the lens is shaped unevenly, so light fails to meet at a single point on the retina. The result is vision that looks smeared or stretched at any distance. It is typically present from childhood and is usually corrected with glasses, contact lenses, or refractive surgery.

diseases.name: Astrocytoma
diseases.summary: A slow-growing or fast-growing tumor arising from star-shaped support cells in the brain or spinal cord, with the type of symptoms depending on where it sits. Early signs are often subtle and can include new seizures or mild headaches, while later signs reflect pressure buildup. Anyone with worsening or persistent neurological symptoms should see a clinician promptly.

diseases.name: Ataxia
diseases.summary: Ataxia is a loss of muscle coordination that makes movements clumsy, most often from damage to the cerebellum or its connections. It can also arise from damaged nerves in the limbs or spinal cord. Sudden onset calls for emergency evaluation because it can signal a stroke.

diseases.name: Atelectasis
diseases.summary: A lung, or a section of one, can deflate when the tiny air sacs inside it lose their air. This often follows surgery or general anesthesia, and it can also accompany lung disease, chest injury, fluid buildup, or weak breathing muscles. Breathing may become difficult, so anyone with trouble breathing should seek prompt medical care.

diseases.name: Athlete's foot
diseases.summary: A fungal skin infection that usually begins between the toes, typically after feet stay warm and damp inside closed shoes. It tends to cause an itchy, flaking rash and can return even after treatment. It spreads easily through shared towels, footwear, and floors.

diseases.name: Atopic dermatitis (eczema)
diseases.summary: This is a persistent inflammatory skin condition that usually starts in early childhood and often coexists with allergic problems such as hay fever or asthma. Symptoms tend to come and go in episodes, and routine moisturizing along with prescribed topical medications can keep it under control.

diseases.name: Atrial fibrillation
diseases.summary: Atrial fibrillation is a heart rhythm disorder in which the upper chambers quiver out of step with the lower chambers, producing a pulse that is irregular and often fast. Many people feel fluttering, breathlessness, or lightheadedness, while others notice nothing at all. Because it raises the risk of clots and stroke, it needs a medical evaluation and ongoing management.

diseases.name: Atrial flutter
diseases.summary: An irregular, overly organized fast rhythm in the heart's upper chambers can run quietly for a long time or announce itself with pounding, chest discomfort, or fainting. It resembles atrial fibrillation but follows a more regular pattern. Older adults and people with heart, lung, or recent cardiac surgery history are more likely to develop it.

diseases.name: Atrial septal defect (ASD)
diseases.summary: A hole between the two upper chambers of the heart is present from birth and can range from tiny and harmless to large enough to strain the lungs and heart over time. Many small ones never cause trouble, while larger ones may need surgical repair. Symptoms often appear only in adulthood, with breathlessness and fatigue during activity being the typical early signs.

diseases.name: Atrial tachycardia
diseases.summary: A condition where the upper chambers of the heart fire off rapid beats, pushing the heart rate above 100 per minute during episodes before it settles back to a normal range. Episodes can come on gradually or abruptly and may bring racing, fluttering, lightheadedness, or fainting. It is fairly common and is often linked to heart disease, thyroid or lung problems, stimulants, and alcohol.

diseases.name: Atrioventricular heart block
diseases.summary: The heart's electrical timing signal sometimes slows or fails to pass from the upper chambers to the lower chambers. The mildest form, first-degree, often causes no problems at all, while more advanced forms can drop the heart rate enough to reduce blood flow and need prompt care or a pacemaker. Some cases are present from birth.

diseases.name: Atrioventricular nodal reentry tachycardia (AVNRT)
diseases.summary: This heart rhythm disorder causes the heart to suddenly race, often above 100 beats a minute, because of an extra electrical loop in the area where the upper and lower heart chambers connect. It is the most common form of supraventricular tachycardia and is seen more often in young women, though anyone can develop it. Many people never need treatment, while others may be helped by specific maneuvers, medicines, or a catheter-based procedure.

diseases.name: Atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD)
diseases.summary: This is a heart malformation present from birth, in which the central wall and valve tissue that divide the heart's chambers develop incorrectly, leaving openings that let blood mix between sides. The extra blood flow strains the heart and lungs, so infants often show breathing and feeding trouble early on. Many affected children have an associated chromosomal condition, and repair is usually done surgically in infancy.

diseases.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children
diseases.summary: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a lifelong condition in many people that shows up as trouble focusing, restlessness, and acting before thinking. It usually becomes noticeable before age 12 and is seen more often in boys, who tend to show more hyperactivity while girls often show quiet inattention. Symptoms can be eased substantially with education, medication, and behavioral therapy, and an evaluation by a pediatrician is advised to rule out other causes.

diseases.name: Atypical genitalia
diseases.summary: Some babies are born with genitals that do not clearly look male or female, which can reflect differences in how sex organs developed before birth. Doctors usually notice this right after delivery and then investigate the underlying cause. Families often receive counseling to help them make decisions about care.

diseases.name: Atypical hyperplasia of the breast
diseases.summary: This is a breast finding in which some cells lining the milk ducts or lobules look abnormal under the microscope but are not yet cancer. It usually causes no noticeable signs and is typically discovered when tissue is sampled for another reason. It mainly matters because it raises the chance of developing breast cancer later, so it is managed with closer screening and sometimes preventive medication.

diseases.name: Atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor (ATRT)
diseases.summary: This aggressive malignant tumor of the central nervous system is extremely uncommon and mostly affects children under three, though older children and, very rarely, adults can develop it. Symptoms depend on where the growth sits and how large it becomes, and they often appear quickly. Prognosis depends heavily on the patient's age and whether the tumor has spread at diagnosis.

diseases.name: Auditory processing disorder (APD)
diseases.summary: A hearing-processing condition in which the ears and hearing tests look normal, yet the brain struggles to interpret sounds, especially speech in noise or quick speech. It can occur in children and adults, often alongside attention or developmental conditions, and while it has no cure, targeted therapies can improve day-to-day function.

diseases.name: Autism spectrum disorder
diseases.summary: Autism spectrum disorder is a neurodevelopmental difference that appears in early childhood and shapes how a person communicates, relates to others, and moves through daily routines. Its effects vary widely from mild to severe, and it includes several presentations that were once classified as separate conditions. There is no cure, but support started in the preschool years often leads to meaningful gains.

diseases.name: Autoimmune encephalitis
diseases.summary: A group of immune-driven conditions in which the body's defenses inflame the brain, often after an infection or cancer. It can bring on mental changes, memory trouble, and seizures, and it can become dangerous quickly without treatment. Many patients recover fully with prompt therapy, though some keep lasting problems.

diseases.name: Autoimmune epilepsy
aliases: Acute symptomatic seizures secondary to autoimmune encephalitis
diseases.summary: Autoimmune epilepsy is a seizure disorder driven by the body's own antibodies attacking receptors in the brain, which leads to brain swelling and seizures. It often follows a feverish illness and typically responds poorly to standard seizure medications, so early immune-suppressing treatment is central to care. Seizures in this condition are sudden and serious, and people with other autoimmune diseases or a family history of them are more likely to be affected.

diseases.name: Autoimmune hepatitis
diseases.summary: A condition in which the immune system mistakenly inflames and injures the liver, and which can scar the organ or progress to failure if left alone. Medications that dampen immunity usually keep it in check when caught early. Women are affected far more often than men, and a family tendency and other autoimmune illnesses raise the chance of developing it.

diseases.name: Autoimmune pancreatitis
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon type of pancreatic swelling caused by the body's own defenses mistakenly targeting the organ. It has two forms, and one can involve several other organs as well. Because its signs closely resemble pancreatic cancer while treatment differs, it needs careful evaluation, and many people have no noticeable symptoms at all.

diseases.name: Autonomic neuropathy
diseases.summary: Autonomic neuropathy is nerve damage affecting the body's automatic control systems, including blood pressure regulation, digestion, bladder function, sweating, and sexual response. Because different systems can be affected to different degrees, symptoms vary widely between people and often develop gradually. It is most often associated with long-standing diabetes, though other causes exist.

diseases.name: Avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis)
diseases.summary: Avascular necrosis is a condition where bone tissue dies because its blood supply is interrupted, most often in the hip, knee, shoulder, or ankle. Early on it may cause little discomfort, but as the bone weakens and collapses, pain and loss of movement usually follow. It is typically treated by orthopedic specialists, and earlier detection generally leads to better outcomes.

diseases.name: B-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: B-cell lymphomas are a group of blood cancers that start in one kind of white blood cell and can spread to lymph nodes, bone marrow, and other organs. They vary widely in how fast they progress, and some people have no symptoms at all. Swollen glands and systemic signs such as fever, sweating at night, and weight loss are the most typical warning signs.

diseases.name: Baby acne
diseases.summary: A common, harmless skin condition that affects many newborns and young infants, usually appearing a few weeks after birth. It causes small bumps and pimples, mostly on the face, and typically clears on its own within a few months without scarring.

diseases.name: Back pain
diseases.summary: Back pain is a very widespread complaint that often eases on its own with rest, gentle activity, and self-care over a few weeks. Certain red flags, such as nerve symptoms in the legs, fever, bladder or bowel changes, or pain following an injury, call for prompt medical evaluation. Serious underlying causes are uncommon.

diseases.name: Bacterial vaginosis
diseases.summary: A common vaginal condition where the normal balance of bacteria shifts, letting certain germs multiply. It is most often seen during the years when hormones fluctuate and is linked to new or multiple sexual partners and rinsing the vagina. Many affected people notice no symptoms at all.

diseases.name: Bad breath
diseases.summary: Bad breath is an odor from the mouth that can be caused by bacteria trapped on the tongue, certain foods, dry mouth, smoking, or other health problems. Many cases improve with better daily cleaning of the teeth, tongue, and gums, and staying hydrated. If the odor persists despite these steps, a dentist or other clinician should check for an underlying cause.

diseases.name: Bags under eyes
diseases.summary: Under-eye puffiness is a mostly cosmetic change that tends to appear with age, as the supporting tissues loosen and fat or fluid collects below the eyes. It is usually harmless, and cool compresses or, for stubborn cases, eyelid surgery can help. A medical check is worthwhile if vision changes, irritation, headaches, or a skin rash accompany it.

diseases.name: Baker cyst
diseases.summary: A fluid-filled bulge that forms behind the knee when joint fluid collects in a nearby sac, usually because of an underlying knee problem such as arthritis or a cartilage tear. It is often harmless and may cause no symptoms at all, though it can cause tightness and discomfort. Pain and swelling behind the knee should be checked promptly, since a blood clot in the leg can look similar.

diseases.name: Balance problems
diseases.summary: Balance problems usually come from the inner ear's balance system, though muscles, nerves, eyes, and heart can also play a part. They tend to cause a spinning or floating feeling, unsteadiness, and lightheadedness, and they can occur whether lying, sitting, or standing. Most cases are manageable, but persistent or worsening symptoms warrant a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS)
diseases.summary: A rare inherited genetic disorder that can affect many body systems at once, often showing up in early childhood. Its signs vary widely from person to person, so some people have only mild features while others have many. Care usually requires several kinds of specialists working together, since there is no cure but early treatment of related problems can improve quality of life.

diseases.name: Barrett's esophagus
diseases.summary: This is a change in the lining of the lower food pipe, often caused by years of stomach acid backing up from the stomach. The altered tissue carries a small added risk of cancer, so people with long-term reflux are usually advised to get periodic monitoring. Many affected people have few or no noticeable symptoms.

diseases.name: Bartholin's cyst
diseases.summary: A Bartholin's cyst forms when the gland on either side of the vaginal opening becomes blocked, so fluid collects and swells into a lump. It is often painless at first, but it can grow large and become infected, causing an abscess. Most people notice a tender or swollen lump near the vaginal opening.

diseases.name: Basal cell carcinoma
diseases.summary: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common type of skin cancer, arising from the cells in the lower layer of the epidermis. It usually appears on sun-exposed areas as a slow-growing lesion that rarely spreads but can cause local damage if left untreated. Most patients notice a changing or non-healing spot, bump, or sore on the skin.

diseases.name: Bed-wetting
diseases.summary: Bed-wetting is passing urine unintentionally during sleep past the age when nighttime dryness is usually expected. It is very common in young children, is more frequent in boys, and typically resolves without treatment. Medical review is worth considering if it persists past age 7, starts again after a dry period, or comes with other warning signs.

diseases.name: Bedbugs
diseases.summary: Bedbugs are tiny, flat, wingless insects that hide in bedding and furniture during the day and feed on people at night. Their bites tend to be itchy and often appear in lines or clusters, and most resolve on their own within a couple of weeks. Some people react strongly, so a doctor should be seen if a bite reaction becomes severe.

diseases.name: Bedsores (pressure ulcers)
diseases.summary: Bedsores are wounds that form when pressure cuts off blood supply to skin and the tissue beneath it, usually over bony spots. They tend to affect people who cannot shift position easily or who spend long periods in bed or a chair. Many heal with prompt repositioning and care, though some persist.

diseases.name: Bee sting
diseases.summary: Stings from bees usually cause immediate sharp pain, a raised welt, and localized swelling that fade within hours for most people. A minority experience a stronger reaction that lasts days, and a small number develop a rapid, dangerous allergic reaction that needs emergency treatment. Many people sting by multiple bees may feel generally unwell.

diseases.name: Behcet disease
diseases.summary: Behcet disease is an uncommon, long-term disorder in which the body's blood vessels become inflamed in many places at once. Its signs can look unrelated and may involve the mouth, skin, eyes, joints, genitals, or internal organs. Because it can threaten eyesight and blood vessels, it calls for prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Bell's palsy
diseases.summary: A quick-onset, one-sided loss of facial movement that usually fades over weeks to months, most often with full recovery. It is thought to stem from inflammation of the nerve that powers the face, frequently after a viral illness. Because it can look like a stroke, a prompt medical check is important.

diseases.name: Benign adrenal tumors
diseases.summary: Most growths on the adrenal glands that are not cancerous cause no noticeable problems and need no treatment. When one does release excess hormones, it can lead to weight gain, bruising, high blood pressure, or changes in mood and energy. Tumors arising from the outer layer or the inner core of the gland produce different patterns of symptoms.

diseases.name: Benign brain tumor
diseases.summary: Most benign brain growths are slow-moving and do not spread, yet they can still cause trouble by pressing on nearby brain tissue, nerves, blood vessels, or fluid pathways. Many are found by chance on imaging and need only monitoring, while others are managed with surgery, radiation, or medication depending on type and location. Symptoms depend on where the growth sits and how quickly it enlarges.

diseases.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)
diseases.summary: This inner-ear balance disorder causes brief spells of spinning sensation that are typically triggered by specific head movements, such as rolling over in bed or looking upward. Although unsettling, it is seldom dangerous on its own, though it can make falls more likely. A clinician can often resolve it with a simple in-office maneuver.

diseases.name: Benign peripheral nerve tumor
diseases.summary: A benign peripheral nerve tumor is a non-cancerous growth on a nerve outside the brain and spinal cord. It can sit inside the nerve or press on it from outside, and symptoms depend on which nerve is involved. Although these growths are usually harmless in themselves, they can still damage nerves and affect movement, so a medical evaluation is worthwhile.

diseases.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)
diseases.summary: An enlarged prostate is a very common change in older men, and it often causes urinary problems that tend to worsen slowly over time. Some people have marked symptoms with only a slightly enlarged gland, while others have none at all. Because similar urinary complaints can come from infections, stones, or certain medicines, a doctor should evaluate them, and urgent care is needed if urine cannot be passed.

diseases.name: Bile reflux
diseases.summary: Bile reflux happens when digestive fluid from the small intestine flows back up into the stomach and sometimes the esophagus. It often causes burning discomfort in the upper belly or chest, along with nausea and a bitter taste. Symptoms can worsen after meals or when lying down.

diseases.name: Biliary atresia
diseases.summary: A rare disorder in newborns and infants in which the tubes that drain bile from the liver are blocked or never fully form, causing slow liver injury. Babies usually look well at birth, then develop lasting yellowing and pale stools within the first weeks of life. Early surgery can relieve the blockage and delay the need for a liver transplant, but it does not cure the disease.

diseases.name: Binge-eating disorder
diseases.summary: Binge-eating disorder is a mental health condition in which a person repeatedly loses a sense of control over eating, often consuming far more food than typical within a short window. Feelings of shame and distress usually follow these episodes, and attempts to strictly cut back can make the cycle worse. Effective treatment can help people regain a steadier and more balanced relationship with food.

diseases.name: Bipolar disorder
diseases.summary: A lifelong brain-based condition marked by shifts between emotional highs and lows that affect energy, sleep, and judgment. Episodes of each typically last several days and can be managed with ongoing treatment, usually medication plus talk therapy. Getting professional help early matters because the condition does not resolve on its own.

diseases.name: Bird flu (avian influenza)
diseases.summary: This infection spreads from birds to people only rarely, usually through close work with live poultry or contact with an animal's droppings or bedding. Its early signs look like ordinary flu, but breathing trouble, pink eye, and stomach symptoms can set it apart. Anyone with a possible exposure and matching symptoms should contact a clinician promptly for testing.

diseases.name: Black hairy tongue
diseases.summary: A harmless, usually short-lived tongue change occurs when tiny taste-bump projections grow longer and trap stains from food, drinks, tobacco, or microbes, giving the tongue a dark, furry appearance. It is typically painless and resolves once the underlying triggers are addressed and the mouth and tongue are cleaned regularly. Anyone who does not improve despite twice-daily brushing of teeth and tongue should see a clinician or dentist.

diseases.name: Bladder cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins in the cells lining the inside of the bladder, usually found early when it is most treatable. Blood in the urine is the signal most often noticed, and urinary irritation can also show up early. Smoking, older age, and male sex raise the chance of developing it.

diseases.name: Bladder exstrophy
diseases.summary: A rare birth defect in which the bladder develops outside the body wall, so it cannot hold urine and the baby leaks urine from birth. It can also involve the genitals, abdominal muscles, pelvic bones, and bowel, and usually requires surgical repair in infancy.

diseases.name: Bladder stones
diseases.summary: Bladder stones are hard mineral deposits that form inside the bladder, often when urine does not fully empty and crystals settle and clump together. They mainly cause irritation of the bladder lining and can block the urine flow. Most people notice urinary discomfort, changes in how they pass urine, or blood in the urine.

diseases.name: Blastocystis hominis
diseases.summary: Blastocystis hominis is a single-celled organism that lives in the human intestine and is detected in stool samples. Many people who carry it feel no effects at all, while others notice digestive discomfort. Whether it causes illness on its own is still debated among clinicians.

diseases.name: Blepharitis
diseases.summary: Blepharitis is a long-lasting or recurring inflammation along the edges of the eyelids, where the lashes grow. It usually stems from oil-gland problems or skin bacteria and tends to flare and settle over time. Most cases are manageable with routine eyelid hygiene, but persistent symptoms or any vision change should be checked by an eye doctor.

diseases.name: Blocked tear duct
diseases.summary: A nasal lacrimal duct that fails to drain properly causes tears to pool and overflow, most often in infants and older adults. The main effects are watery eyes and a sticky, mucus-like discharge, sometimes with swelling near the inner corner of the eye.

diseases.name: Blood in urine (hematuria)
diseases.summary: Seeing red, pink, or cola-tinted urine can be alarming, and it is often caused by something harmless such as certain foods or medicines. Still, actual blood in the urine can point to infection, kidney or bladder problems, or in some cases cancer, so it deserves a medical evaluation. Blood may be visible to the eye or only detectable under a lab microscope.

diseases.name: Body dysmorphic disorder
diseases.summary: Body dysmorphic disorder is a mental health condition in which a person becomes fixated on a supposed flaw in their looks that others either cannot see or consider trivial. The fixation drives repeated checking, grooming, and requests for reassurance, and often leads to pulling back from social life and seeking cosmetic treatments that bring only brief relief. Talk therapy and sometimes medication are the usual treatments, and the condition tends not to improve without them.

diseases.name: Body lice
diseases.summary: Body lice are tiny insects that live in clothing and bedding and feed on human blood, mainly at night. Most people notice itching and skin irritation from bites, and the lice are typically found in seams of clothing rather than on the body itself. Infestation is strongly linked to poor hygiene, crowding, and infrequent clothing or bedding changes.

diseases.name: Boils and carbuncles
diseases.summary: Boils and carbuncles are painful, pus-filled skin lumps caused by bacterial infection of a hair follicle or oil gland. A carbuncle is a cluster of connected boils that forms deeper in the skin. They usually appear on areas with friction or sweating, such as the neck, armpits, buttocks, and thighs.

diseases.name: Bone cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins inside a bone rather than spreading there from elsewhere in the body. It most often forms in the long bone of the upper leg and can appear in children or adults, and it is uncommon overall. Pain and swelling near the affected bone are the usual early warning signs, and anyone with persistent symptoms should see a clinician.

diseases.name: Bone metastasis
diseases.summary: This is cancer that has spread from its original site into the skeleton. It commonly causes ache or pain in the affected bones and can weaken them so they break more easily. When it presses on the spinal cord or raises calcium in the blood, it can also cause nerve symptoms or general illness.

diseases.name: Bone spurs
diseases.summary: Bony outgrowths that develop at the edges of bones, most often where bones meet in joints or along the spine, and usually linked to wear-and-tear arthritis. Many people never notice them, but when they press on nearby structures they can cause joint pain, stiffness, or nerve-related weakness or numbness.

diseases.name: Borderline personality disorder
diseases.summary: This is a long-term mental health condition that shapes how a person views themselves and how they connect with others, often causing unstable relationships and strong emotional swings. Intense fear of being left alone can drive impulsive choices and self-harm. Symptoms tend to be most intense in early adulthood and often ease with age, though self-image and relationship struggles may persist, and many people improve substantially with treatment.

diseases.name: Botulism
diseases.summary: Botulism is a rare illness in which a nerve-attacking toxin, made by a bacterium, disrupts normal nerve signaling and can cause paralysis and breathing trouble. It can reach the body through contaminated food, a wound, or the intestines in infants, and it is never spread from person to person. Because it can be fatal, anyone who suspects it needs immediate emergency care.

diseases.name: Brachial plexus injury
diseases.summary: A brachial plexus injury affects the network of nerves linking the spinal cord to the shoulder, arm, and hand, usually after stretching, compression, or tearing. Mild cases are frequent in contact sports, while severe cases from high-speed crashes can cause lasting weakness or paralysis. Prompt evaluation matters, and surgery can help some serious injuries.

diseases.name: Bradycardia
diseases.summary: A heart rate under 60 beats per minute can deprive the brain and organs of enough oxygen, leading to dizziness, fatigue, or fainting. Many people with a slow pulse feel fine, especially athletes and those asleep. Medical attention is needed when slowness brings on worrying symptoms, and severe cases may require a pacemaker.

diseases.name: Brain aneurysm
diseases.summary: A brain aneurysm is a swelling in an artery inside the head that often causes no noticeable signs and is frequently discovered by accident during unrelated scans. If it bursts, it bleeds into the space around the brain and typically brings on an abrupt, intense headache that needs immediate treatment. A larger unburst swelling can press on nearby nerves and tissue, leading to eye pain or changes in vision.

diseases.name: Brain AVM (arteriovenous malformation)
diseases.summary: A tangle of abnormal vessels in the brain lets arterial blood flow straight into veins, bypassing normal capillaries and disrupting circulation. Many affected people have no warning signs until the malformation ruptures, though others notice seizures, head pain, or neurological deficits. Because these lesions are uncommon and often first appear in early adulthood, prompt medical evaluation is important.

diseases.name: Brain metastases
diseases.summary: Cancer that began in another organ can travel to the brain and form one or several growths there. These growths press on nearby brain tissue, so the resulting problems depend on which region is affected rather than on where the original cancer started. Anyone with a cancer history who develops new nerve-related symptoms should be evaluated promptly.

diseases.name: Brain tumor
diseases.summary: A brain tumor is a mass of abnormal cells that forms inside the brain or nearby structures, and it may be non-cancerous or cancerous, with cancers that spread from elsewhere also possible. Symptoms depend on where the growth sits and how fast it grows: slow-growing benign tumors usually cause subtle changes over months, while malignant ones produce symptoms that worsen within days or weeks. Persistent, worrying symptoms such as recurring headaches, vision changes, or seizures warrant prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Brainstem tumor
diseases.summary: A growth in the midbrain, pons, or medulla can disrupt the brain's control over movement, balance, eye alignment, facial muscles, speech, and swallowing. Most of these growths are gliomas, and they are more often found in children than in adults. Symptoms often build gradually, and sudden worsening calls for prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Breast cancer
diseases.summary: Breast cancer begins in the cells of breast tissue, most often in the milk ducts and less often in the milk-producing lobules, and it can affect people of any sex. Early disease frequently causes no symptoms and is often found on screening imaging, while advanced disease can bring bone pain, fatigue, and weight loss. Any new breast or nipple change warrants a prompt medical visit rather than waiting for the next mammogram.

diseases.name: Breast cysts
diseases.summary: Breast cysts are small, fluid-filled pockets within the breast tissue that are almost always harmless. They often feel like a smooth, movable bump and can swell or ache around the menstrual cycle. Most people never need treatment unless a cyst becomes large or uncomfortable, though any new or changing lump should still be checked by a clinician.

diseases.name: Breast pain
diseases.summary: Breast discomfort can take many forms, from aching or throbbing to sharp or burning, and it may be constant, brief, or intermittent. It is often tied to the menstrual cycle, but it can also arise without any hormonal pattern, and it is usually caused by a benign condition rather than cancer. Large breast size, prior surgery, and smoking are factors that can make it more likely.

diseases.name: Broken ankle
diseases.summary: A broken ankle means one or more of the bones around the ankle joint has cracked or separated, usually from a fall, twist, or impact. It typically causes immediate pain, swelling, and difficulty putting weight on the leg, and it needs prompt medical assessment with imaging to confirm the injury and guide treatment.

diseases.name: Broken arm
diseases.summary: A fracture in the upper arm bone or one of the two forearm bones can be spotted by visible deformity, intense movement-related pain, and trouble using the arm or rotating the forearm. Prompt medical evaluation matters because delayed care can impair healing, and any numbness, color change, or skin breach needs emergency attention. Falls onto an outstretched hand and contact sports are typical causes.

diseases.name: Broken collarbone
diseases.summary: A cracked or fully split clavicle, the long bone running from the breastbone to the shoulder, typically follows a fall, sports collision, or car crash. Pain and swelling at the fracture site are the hallmark, and the arm often cannot be used normally. Most cases heal with sling support and time, though some need surgical fixation, and prompt medical evaluation prevents poor healing.

diseases.name: Broken foot
diseases.summary: A broken foot happens when one or more small bones in the foot crack or snap, usually after a fall, a crushing blow, or a sports injury. Injuries range from hairline cracks to multiple breaks, and some break through the skin. Anyone who can't comfortably bear weight after an injury should get checked, since some fractures still allow walking.

diseases.name: Broken hand
diseases.summary: A broken hand is a crack or full break in one of the small bones of the hand or fingers, most often caused by a fall, a direct blow, or a crush injury. It usually causes localized pain, swelling, and trouble using the hand, and a clinician needs to examine it and usually order imaging to confirm the break and check alignment.

diseases.name: Broken heart syndrome
diseases.summary: A temporary weakening of the heart muscle that can follow intense emotional stress, a serious illness, or surgery. Its symptoms can closely resemble a heart attack, so it needs urgent evaluation. Most people recover, though some feel unwell for a while after the heart has recovered.

diseases.name: Broken leg
diseases.summary: A cracked or fully broken bone in the lower body, most often from a fall, vehicle crash, or sports injury. Pain, swelling, and inability to bear weight are typical, and a thighbone fracture is an emergency that needs immediate care. Treatment ranges from a cast or splint for milder breaks to surgical hardware for severe ones.

diseases.name: Broken nose
diseases.summary: A broken nose is a fracture of the bones or cartilage that form the nasal structure, usually caused by a blow to the face. It typically produces pain, swelling, and bleeding, and it can change how the nose looks or how air moves through it. Medical evaluation is generally advised to check alignment and rule out complications.

diseases.name: Broken ribs
diseases.summary: A rib fracture is a crack or break in one of the bones of the chest cage, most often from a fall, vehicle crash, or contact sport. Simple cracks are painful but usually not dangerous, while several adjacent broken ribs can leave a loose section of chest wall that interferes with breathing and needs urgent care. Most fractures knit back together on their own within roughly six weeks, with good pain control helping the person keep breathing deeply.

diseases.name: Broken toe
diseases.summary: A cracked or fractured toe is a frequent minor injury, typically caused by a heavy object landing on the foot or by hitting the toe against something hard. Most heal on their own within several weeks, though lingering soreness and puffiness can persist for months. Medical attention is worth seeking if symptoms do not ease within a few days or if walking or fitting into shoes becomes difficult.

diseases.name: Broken wrist
diseases.summary: A wrist fracture is a crack or break in one of the small bones of the wrist or the forearm bones near it, most often caused by falling onto an outstretched hand. Pain that gets worse with gripping, swelling, bruising, and visible deformity are typical signs. Because delayed care can lead to poor healing and lasting loss of strength, it should be evaluated by a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Bronchiolitis
diseases.summary: A common respiratory infection in infants and toddlers, it inflames and clogs the tiniest breathing tubes in the lungs, usually after a virus. It typically begins looking like a cold and may progress to labored breathing and whistling sounds over one to two weeks. Most children recover at home, though a minority need hospital care, and very young infants or those with heart, lung, or immune problems are at greater risk.

diseases.name: Bronchitis
diseases.summary: Inflammation of the airway tubes that carry air to and from the lungs, usually triggered by a viral infection and typically clearing within a couple of weeks, though a lingering cough may persist longer. A longer-term form, most often linked to smoking, involves ongoing irritation and can be part of COPD and warrants medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Brucellosis
diseases.summary: Brucellosis is a bacterial infection usually picked up from unpasteurized dairy products or contact with infected animals. It tends to cause a long-lasting, undulating fever along with aches and tiredness, and it can settle into joints, organs, or other tissues if left untreated. Treatment requires a multi-week course of antibiotics prescribed by a physician.

diseases.name: Brugada syndrome
diseases.summary: Brugada syndrome is an inherited heart rhythm disorder caused mainly by changes in genes that control sodium flow in heart cells. Many people with it never have symptoms, but it can trigger dangerous fast heart rhythms that may cause fainting or sudden death, often at rest or during sleep. It is usually identified through a characteristic ECG pattern, followed by clinical and genetic evaluation.

diseases.name: Buerger disease
diseases.summary: A rare inflammatory disorder that narrows and clogs small arteries and veins in the hands and feet, mainly in people who smoke. Reduced circulation gradually injures the skin, which can lead to open wounds and tissue death. Stopping all tobacco use is the main way to halt progression.

diseases.name: Bulimia nervosa
diseases.summary: Bulimia is an eating disorder marked by repeated episodes of eating far more than usual in a short span, often with a sense of being unable to stop, followed by attempts to cancel out the food through vomiting, laxatives, or intense exercise. It is closely tied to how a person views their body and self-worth, and it can damage physical health and mental wellbeing if left untreated. Professional medical and psychological care can help people recover.

diseases.name: Bullous pemphigoid
diseases.summary: An uncommon skin disorder in which the body's defenses target the outer skin layers, producing tense, fluid-filled bumps that tend to show up in body folds. It mostly affects adults past their sixties and frequently begins with intense itching before any blisters appear. Many cases resolve over months to several years with appropriate treatment.

diseases.name: Bundle branch block
diseases.summary: A bundle branch block is a delay or interruption in the heart's electrical wiring that carries signals to the lower chambers, so they contract slightly out of step. It is usually discovered on an electrocardiogram and often causes no noticeable problems. When symptoms do occur, they tend to reflect an underlying heart condition or reduced pumping efficiency.

diseases.name: Bunions
diseases.summary: A bunion is a bony bump that develops at the joint where the big toe meets the foot, as the toe gradually angles toward the other toes. It tends to progress slowly and is commonly linked to footwear and foot shape. Many people manage it with better-fitting shoes and padding, and see a clinician if pain or stiffness starts limiting daily activities.

diseases.name: Burkitt lymphoma
diseases.summary: Burkitt lymphoma is a fast-growing blood cancer that starts in immune B cells and most often shows up as a quickly enlarging mass or painless lumps. It is aggressive but often curable when caught and treated promptly. Children and people with weakened immune systems are at higher risk.

diseases.name: Burning mouth syndrome
diseases.summary: Burning mouth syndrome is a long-lasting scalding or stinging feeling in the mouth that has no clear source. It most often affects the tongue but can involve the lips, gums, palate, or the whole mouth. It tends to persist for months or years, and a doctor or dentist can help look for contributing factors and plan treatment.

diseases.name: Burns
diseases.summary: Burns are injuries to the skin caused by heat, flames, chemicals, electricity, or strong sunlight. Minor ones often heal with simple home care, while deep or large burns, or those caused by chemicals or electricity, need prompt medical attention. How a burn looks and feels depends mainly on how many layers of skin it reaches.

diseases.name: Bursitis
diseases.summary: Bursitis is a painful inflammation of the small fluid-filled sacs that cushion joints where bone, tendon, and muscle meet. It most often affects the shoulder, knee, elbow, heel, and hip, and it becomes more likely with age and repetitive pressure or motion. Pain and swelling typically worsen with movement or touch.

diseases.name: C. difficile infection
diseases.summary: A gut infection caused by a bacterium that can inflame the large intestine, usually appearing during or after a course of antibiotics. It is most often seen in older adults in hospitals or long-term care, though others can catch it. Mild cases bring watery diarrhea and cramps, while severe cases can lead to dehydration and serious complications.

diseases.name: Calciphylaxis
diseases.summary: A rare, serious condition in which calcium accumulates in small blood vessels of fat and skin, most often in people with advanced kidney disease. It produces painful skin lesions that can break down into sores, and those sores carry a real risk of life-threatening infection.

diseases.name: Cancer
diseases.summary: Cancer is an umbrella term for many illnesses in which cells grow out of control and invade nearby tissue, sometimes travelling to distant parts of the body. It is a leading cause of death worldwide, though outcomes have been getting better as screening and treatment advance. Because the signs depend on where the disease sits, symptoms are often vague and shared with many other conditions.

diseases.name: Canker sore
diseases.summary: A small, painful sore that forms inside the mouth, usually on soft tissue such as the cheeks, lips, or tongue, is a common, self-limiting problem that tends to clear within a couple of weeks. It often begins with a tingling or burning sensation before the sore is visible. Seek dental or medical advice if sores are unusually large, persistent, spreading, or accompanied by high fever.

diseases.name: Carbon monoxide poisoning
diseases.summary: Poisoning from this odorless, colorless gas occurs when it displaces oxygen in the blood, and it can damage the brain and heart quickly. Early signs often resemble flu without a fever, and the danger is greater for people who are asleep or intoxicated. Anyone with suspected exposure should move to fresh air and get emergency medical help without delay.

diseases.name: Carcinoid syndrome
diseases.summary: Carcinoid syndrome is a set of flushing, diarrhea and related symptoms caused by hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tumors, most often in the small intestine or lung that have spread to the liver. The hormones released, mainly serotonin, reach the body beyond the liver and trigger the characteristic episodes. Symptoms tend to come in attacks and can be managed once the underlying tumor is identified and treated.

diseases.name: Carcinoid tumors
diseases.summary: Carcinoid tumors are slow-growing growths that most often start in the digestive tract or lungs, and many cause no noticeable problems until they are advanced. When they do cause trouble, it is often through hormones they release, which can lead to flushing or diarrhea. Symptoms vary with where the tumor sits, and persistent complaints warrant a doctor's visit.
