diseases.name: Carcinoma of unknown primary
diseases.summary: This is an advanced cancer where tumor cells are found in the body, usually in lymph nodes or distant organs, but doctors cannot locate the original site where it began. Identifying that origin matters because it guides treatment choices, so the care team works to pin it down. It mostly affects adults over 60 and is often linked with smoking or a family history of cancer.

diseases.name: Cardiac amyloidosis
diseases.summary: This is a stiffening disease of the heart muscle caused by abnormal protein deposits building up in the heart walls, which makes it hard for the heart to fill and pump blood properly. Early signs are easy to mistake for other heart or general health problems. Treatments can slow progression and relieve symptoms, though the underlying damage often cannot be reversed.

diseases.name: Cardiogenic shock
diseases.summary: Cardiogenic shock is a life-threatening state in which the heart suddenly cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs, most often after a major heart attack. Organs become starved of oxygen, causing low blood pressure, confusion, and cold, pale skin. It requires immediate hospital treatment.

diseases.name: Cardiomyopathy
diseases.summary: A condition where the heart muscle weakens or thickens, making it harder for the heart to pump blood around the body. Many people have no noticeable signs at first, but symptoms that resemble heart failure tend to develop and worsen over time without treatment. Some forms can run in families, and anyone with symptoms should see a clinician promptly.

diseases.name: Carotid artery disease
diseases.summary: Fatty buildup in the two large neck arteries that carry blood to the brain narrows them over time. It often causes no noticeable problems until it triggers a stroke or a brief warning episode. Any sudden stroke-like symptom needs emergency care, even if it passes.

diseases.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
diseases.summary: This condition involves pressure on a nerve running through a narrow wrist passage, leading to hand symptoms that often come and go and can disturb sleep. It is more often seen in women, and it usually responds well to timely treatment, though untreated cases can lead to lasting nerve and muscle harm.

diseases.name: Castleman disease
diseases.summary: Castleman disease is an uncommon group of disorders in which lymph nodes enlarge and the body can react with wide-ranging illness. The single-node form often causes no noticeable problems and is found incidentally, while the multi-site forms can bring on fever, weight loss, fatigue, and organ or blood abnormalities. Diagnosis relies on imaging, lab tests, and sometimes a tissue sample.

diseases.name: Cataracts
diseases.summary: A cataract is a gradual clouding of the eye's normally clear lens that makes vision look foggy or washed out. It usually develops slowly and is most common in older adults. Early on it can often be managed with brighter light and new glasses, while surgery is considered once daily activities are affected.

diseases.name: Cavernous malformations
diseases.summary: Most abnormal vessel clusters in the brain or spinal cord of this type never produce noticeable problems and are found by chance. When they do cause trouble, it is usually because they have leaked blood, which can bring on seizures, sudden neurological deficits, or severe headaches. Repeated small bleeds can worsen symptoms over time, so any seizure or sudden brain-related symptom needs prompt emergency evaluation.

diseases.name: Cavities and tooth decay
diseases.summary: Tooth decay creates small holes in the hard outer layer of teeth and is one of the most widespread dental problems worldwide, affecting children, teens, older adults, and even babies. Early decay often causes no noticeable signs, while larger cavities bring sensitivity, visible pits, staining, and pain, and untreated decay can progress to infection or tooth loss.

diseases.name: Celiac disease
diseases.summary: Celiac disease is an immune-driven reaction to gluten that gradually injures the lining of the small intestine and hampers nutrient uptake. Its effects range from stomach complaints like diarrhea and bloating to wider problems such as anemia, fatigue, and bone or nerve changes. Strict avoidance of gluten is the main management approach for most people.

diseases.name: Cellulite
diseases.summary: Cellulite is a harmless, extremely widespread change in skin texture that makes the surface look dimpled or uneven, mostly on the thighs, hips, buttocks, and belly. It happens when fat pushes against the skin while fibrous bands beneath pull downward. Treatment is optional and usually sought only for cosmetic reasons.

diseases.name: Cellulitis
diseases.summary: A bacterial infection of the deeper layers of the skin and the fatty tissue beneath it, usually entering through a break in the skin such as a cut, scrape, or insect bite. The inflamed area can spread quickly if it goes untreated, so it generally needs prompt medical assessment and antibiotics.

diseases.name: Central nervous system (CNS) lymphoma
diseases.summary: A cancer of the immune lymphocytes that develops inside the brain, spinal cord, their surrounding fluid, or sometimes the eyes. It usually forms as one or more growing masses and tends to show up as headaches, confusion or personality shifts, and problems with movement or vision. Treatment is available, and outcomes depend on general health and how far the disease has spread.

diseases.name: Central nervous system vascular malformations
diseases.summary: These are abnormal blood vessel formations in the brain, spinal cord, or the membranes that cover them. Several types exist, and some never cause problems and are discovered only by chance on imaging. When they do cause symptoms, the usual problems are bleeding, seizures, headaches, or nerve-related difficulties that slowly worsen.

diseases.name: Central sleep apnea
diseases.summary: Central sleep apnea is a sleep-related breathing problem where breathing briefly halts and resumes through the night because the brain's signals to breathing muscles are unreliable. It is distinct from blockage-based apnea and often accompanies heart failure, stroke, or time spent at high elevation. Treating the underlying condition, using a breathing device, or supplemental oxygen may help.

diseases.name: Cerebral palsy
diseases.summary: This condition is a group of lifelong disorders that disturb movement, posture and balance, arising from injury to the developing brain, usually before birth. Signs typically emerge in infancy or the preschool years and vary widely, from mild motor differences to involvement of the whole body. Although there is no cure, therapies can improve daily function, and the underlying problem does not progressively worsen.

diseases.name: Cervical cancer
diseases.summary: Cervical cancer develops when cells lining the lower part of the uterus begin to change abnormally and multiply without control. Infection with human papillomavirus is the main driver, and routine screening with Pap tests has made it far more treatable when caught early. Early cases often cause no noticeable signs, so bleeding or pelvic discomfort prompts a medical visit.

diseases.name: Cervical dystonia
diseases.summary: Cervical dystonia is a movement disorder in which the neck muscles contract involuntarily, pulling the head into abnormal positions. The pulls are often repetitive and can be painful, and they tend to get worse under stress or when the person is tired. It is typically managed by a neurologist with treatments such as botulinum toxin injections.

diseases.name: Cervical spondylosis
diseases.summary: Cervical spondylosis is age-related wear and tear of the bones, discs, and joints in the neck. Over time this can narrow the space around the spinal cord or nerve roots, leading to neck stiffness and pain that may spread into the shoulders, arms, or hands.

diseases.name: Cervicitis
diseases.summary: A frequent problem in women where the lower part of the womb becomes inflamed, often without any noticeable signs. It is sometimes found during a routine pelvic exam, and it can be triggered by sexually transmitted germs or by other causes that may not need treatment. Infections linked to sexual activity should be checked and treated.

diseases.name: Chagas disease
diseases.summary: Chagas disease is a long-term infection caused by a parasite spread mainly by triatomine insects in Latin America. It often begins with few or no noticeable signs, then may later affect the heart and digestive tract. Symptoms range from mild early illness to serious heart rhythm problems or heart failure years later.

diseases.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
diseases.summary: This is a group of inherited disorders that damage the nerves running from the brain and spinal cord to the limbs. Over time the nerves that control muscles and carry touch sensation to the feet and hands weaken and degenerate, so symptoms usually begin in the lower legs and spread slowly. Onset typically occurs in childhood or early adulthood, and progression is gradual.

diseases.name: Chemo brain
diseases.summary: Chemo brain describes memory and concentration difficulties that some people notice during or after cancer treatment, especially chemotherapy. Its exact causes are not fully understood and are thought to involve several factors. Although it can be frustrating, it is a recognized side effect that researchers are actively studying.

diseases.name: Chest pain
diseases.summary: Chest discomfort has many possible causes, and the most dangerous ones involve the heart or lungs, so it needs prompt medical evaluation rather than guesswork. Heart-related pain often comes with pressure, arm or jaw spread, breathlessness, and sweating, while pain that worsens with breathing, coughing, or position changes tends to point elsewhere. Any sudden or unexplained chest pain warrants emergency help right away.

diseases.name: Chest wall tumors
diseases.summary: Chest wall tumors are growths arising in the structures that form the outer chest, such as ribs, breastbone, cartilage, muscle, and fat. They can be harmless or cancerous, and they may begin there or spread or grow in from nearby areas. Most people notice a slowly enlarging lump, with pain or swelling possible, and large ones can affect breathing.

diseases.name: Chiari malformation
diseases.summary: This is a structural problem where lower brain tissue extends into the spinal canal because the skull is misshapen or small, and it occurs in four types. Many affected people never notice it, while the most common type tends to surface in later childhood or adulthood with headaches triggered by coughing or straining. Symptoms can be varied, and because many overlap with other conditions, a full medical evaluation is needed.

diseases.name: Chickenpox
diseases.summary: A virus infection that begins with a few days of fever, poor appetite, and tiredness before an itchy, blister-filled rash spreads across the body. Most cases are mild in healthy children, though the rash can be widespread and can affect the mouth, eyes, or genital areas in some people. Vaccination is highly protective, and anyone who suspects they have it should contact a doctor's office ahead of arriving.

diseases.name: Chilblains
diseases.summary: A skin reaction that develops after time spent in cold, damp air, though not freezing, causing red, swollen, painful or itchy patches on the extremities. It typically resolves within a few weeks and tends to return each cold season, usually without lasting damage. Medical advice is worth seeking if symptoms persist, worsen, or may involve infection or frostbite.

diseases.name: Child abuse
diseases.summary: Child abuse covers harm done to a minor through physical force, emotional mistreatment, sexual contact, or failure to provide basic care. Signs often appear as unexplained injuries, shifts in mood or behavior, and changes in sleep, appetite, or school performance, though none of these alone proves abuse. Anyone who suspects a child is being harmed should contact a doctor, child protective services, or local emergency services.

diseases.name: Childhood apraxia of speech
diseases.summary: A rare speech condition in which the brain has difficulty directing the mouth, jaw, and tongue to form sounds and words in the correct order and at a normal pace, even though the muscles themselves are not weak. It is usually noticed in toddlers and young children, and speech therapy with a speech-language pathologist is the main treatment.

diseases.name: Childhood asthma
diseases.summary: Childhood asthma is a long-term condition in which the airways of a child become swollen and narrowed, making breathing difficult at times. Symptoms often come and go and may be set off by colds, exercise, allergens, or cold air. Many children manage it well with daily controller medicine and rescue inhalers.

diseases.name: Childhood obesity
diseases.summary: Childhood obesity means a child carries more body fat than is healthy for their age, and it can set the stage for diabetes, high blood pressure, and emotional struggles. Visible size alone is an unreliable clue, so clinicians rely on growth charts and BMI compared against peers of the same age and sex. Family eating and activity habits play a large role in both prevention and management.

diseases.name: Childhood schizophrenia
diseases.summary: A rare but serious psychiatric illness that begins in childhood or the teen years, where a young person's sense of what is real becomes distorted. It affects thinking, behavior and emotions, and often needs lifelong care. Starting treatment early tends to help the long-term outcome.

diseases.name: Chlamydia trachomatis
diseases.summary: Chlamydia is a bacterial infection passed on through sexual contact that frequently causes no noticeable signs. When symptoms do show up, they are usually subtle and can affect the genitals, rectum, throat, or eyes. Left untreated, it can lead to more serious health problems, so testing and antibiotic treatment are important.

diseases.name: Cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer)
diseases.summary: Bile duct cancer arises in the thin tubes that carry digestive fluid from the liver and gallbladder to the small intestine. It mostly affects adults over 50 and is often found at an advanced stage, which makes treatment harder. Yellowing of the skin and eyes, itching, and pale stools are among its more recognizable warning signs.

diseases.name: Cholecystitis
diseases.summary: Inflammation of the gallbladder usually begins when gallstones block its outlet, causing bile to back up and irritate the organ. Pain often follows a meal, especially a large or greasy one, and can radiate toward the shoulder or back. Untreated cases can progress to serious complications, so prompt medical evaluation is important.

diseases.name: Cholera
diseases.summary: Cholera is an intestinal infection caused by swallowing contaminated water or food, and it can trigger a very fast loss of fluids. The illness typically starts with sudden, watery bowel movements and vomiting, which can quickly lead to severe dehydration if not treated. Because it can become life-threatening within hours, it requires prompt medical attention and rehydration.

diseases.name: Cholestasis of pregnancy
diseases.summary: A liver-related pregnancy condition in which bile flow slows, typically appearing in the third trimester and causing intense itching that often worsens at night. It usually resolves within days after delivery, but it can carry risks for the baby, so prompt medical follow-up is important.

diseases.name: Chondrosarcoma
diseases.summary: A rare bone cancer that typically begins in cartilage-forming cells inside bone, most often in the pelvis, thigh, or upper arm. Some forms grow slowly while others are aggressive and can travel to the lungs. Surgical removal is the mainstay of treatment and can be curative when the whole tumor is taken out.

diseases.name: Chordoma
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon, slow-growing tumor that develops from remnants of embryonic tissue along the spine, most often at the skull base, the mid-spine, or the tailbone. Because it presses on nearby nerves and structures, its warning signs depend on where it sits. It is seen most often in middle-aged adults and affects men somewhat more than women.

diseases.name: Choroid plexus carcinoma
diseases.summary: A very uncommon cancer of the tissue that makes brain fluid, mostly seen in young children. As it grows, it can cause fluid to build up inside the skull, which produces pressure-related complaints. Treatment outcomes depend on the tumor's size, location, spread, and the patient's age and overall health.

diseases.name: Chronic cough
diseases.summary: A cough that persists for two months or more in adults, or four weeks in children, can wear down sleep and energy even though it is usually not dangerous on its own. Tobacco use and asthma are the leading triggers, while mucus dripping down the throat and stomach acid creeping upward are also frequent culprits. Once the underlying cause is identified and treated, the cough generally resolves.

diseases.name: Chronic daily headaches
diseases.summary: Headaches that happen on most days for several months make up this group, which includes several distinct subtypes rather than one single kind of headache. Because the pain is nearly constant, it tends to be quite disabling, though early treatment and ongoing management can often reduce how much pain and how many headaches a person has.

diseases.name: Chronic exertional compartment syndrome
diseases.summary: A condition in which pressure builds inside a muscle compartment of the lower leg during physical activity, reducing blood flow and irritating nerves. Symptoms typically appear with exercise and ease with rest, and they tend to recur in the same pattern. Most people are active adults, such as runners, and the condition is uncommon.

diseases.name: Chronic granulomatous disease
diseases.summary: This inherited immune disorder leaves the white blood cells that normally destroy germs unable to do their job, so affected people repeatedly suffer serious infections from bacteria and fungi. Lung infections, including pneumonia, are especially typical, and infections of the skin, liver, and gut also occur. Symptoms are usually first noticed in childhood, though some people are not diagnosed until adulthood.

diseases.name: Chronic hives
diseases.summary: Long-lasting hives are itchy, raised welts that come and go across the skin for more than six weeks, often recurring for months or years without a clear trigger. They can disrupt sleep and daily life, though antihistamines help many people. Most cases are not predictable, but some are linked to infections, thyroid disease, allergies, cancer, or inflammation of blood vessels.

diseases.name: Chronic kidney disease
diseases.summary: Chronic kidney disease is a long-term condition in which the kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter blood and perform their regular jobs. It often goes unnoticed for years because early signs are subtle, and it is commonly tied to conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure. Doctors track it with a blood test measuring filtration rate and staging it from mild to kidney failure.

diseases.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia
diseases.summary: This blood cancer slowly thickens the blood with excess immune cells that are slow to progress and often cause no early signs. When symptoms arise they tend to be lymph node swelling, night sweats, tiredness, and frequent infections. It mostly affects older adults and is managed with monitoring, drugs, or transplant depending on the stage.

diseases.name: Chronic myelogenous leukemia
diseases.summary: This blood cancer begins in the bone marrow, where it causes too many white blood cells to build up. It often progresses slowly and is frequently found incidentally on routine blood work, and many patients now achieve remission and live for years with modern treatment. It mostly affects older adults and is only occasionally seen in children.

diseases.name: Chronic pelvic pain
diseases.summary: Long-lasting discomfort in the lower abdomen and pelvis, persisting for six months or more, can stem from one or several underlying problems, and sometimes no clear cause is found. Treatment often targets the underlying condition when one is identified, and otherwise focuses on easing pain and improving daily function. Seek medical evaluation when the discomfort interferes with everyday activities or keeps getting worse.

diseases.name: Chronic sinusitis
diseases.summary: Chronic sinusitis is a long-running inflammation of the sinus cavities that lasts at least three months even with treatment. It is often driven by ongoing infection, nasal polyps, or swollen sinus lining, and it commonly leaves the nose blocked and the face around the eyes and cheeks tender. Ongoing exposure to smoke or pollution and dental or fungal infections raise the chance of developing it.

diseases.name: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy
diseases.summary: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy is a degenerative brain disorder linked to many head impacts over time, most often seen in contact sports and military blast exposure. Its signs typically surface years or decades after the injuries and can involve thinking, mood, behavior, and movement. It can only be confirmed through examination of the brain after death.

diseases.name: Cirrhosis
diseases.summary: Cirrhosis is long-term scarring of the liver that builds up after repeated damage, usually from hepatitis infection or heavy drinking. Because the scar tissue steadily reduces how well the liver works, early damage often causes no noticeable signs. Symptoms that do appear tend to reflect the liver failing to clear toxins, process nutrients, and regulate fluid.

diseases.name: Claudication
diseases.summary: Claudication is a pattern of muscle discomfort in the legs that appears during walking or other exertion and fades after a short rest. It happens when narrowed leg arteries cannot deliver enough blood to working muscles. It is usually a sign of peripheral artery disease and warrants a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Cleft lip and cleft palate
diseases.summary: A gap in the lip, the roof of the mouth, or both, forms while a baby is developing before birth, and it is among the most frequent birth differences. It is usually visible at birth or on a prenatal scan, and surgical repair over several procedures typically restores normal function with minimal visible scarring. A less obvious version involving only the soft palate muscles may go unnoticed until feeding, speech, or ear problems appear.

diseases.name: Clubfoot
diseases.summary: A condition present from birth in which a baby's foot is turned inward and downward, often with a raised arch and an inward-turned heel. It is fairly common and will not resolve on its own, but it responds well to a specific series of casts started in the first weeks of life, often with a small procedure on the heel tendon.

diseases.name: Cluster headache
diseases.summary: Cluster headaches are a rare form of head pain that hits in brief, very intense bouts, often clustered over weeks or months and sometimes at the same time each year. Attacks typically strike around one eye or one side of the head and frequently wake people at night. Because the pain can mimic other conditions, a clinician should evaluate new cases to rule out other causes.

diseases.name: Coarctation of the aorta
diseases.summary: A narrowing in the body's largest artery forces the heart to pump harder to push blood through. It is usually present from birth, though it can sometimes first appear later in life. Many affected people have no symptoms, while infants with a severe narrowing can become quite ill soon after birth.

diseases.name: Cold sore
diseases.summary: A small cluster of fluid-filled blisters, usually on or around the lips, caused by a widespread virus that most adults carry. It often begins with tingling or itching, then blisters burst and crust before healing on its own over a few weeks.

diseases.name: Cold urticaria
diseases.summary: Cold urticaria is a skin reaction where hives and itchy welts appear after the skin is exposed to cold air, cold water, or cold objects. Symptoms usually fade as the skin warms, though in severe cases the reaction can involve swelling of deeper tissues or a whole-body response. It is an uncommon condition that is typically managed with antihistamines and avoidance of triggers.

diseases.name: Colic
diseases.summary: Colic describes intense, repetitive crying and fussiness in an otherwise healthy infant who seems to be in discomfort, usually without a clear medical cause. It typically appears in the first few weeks or months of life and tends to fade on its own by around three to four months. Its exact mechanism is not fully understood, and the main concern is ruling out other causes of crying.

diseases.name: Colon cancer symptoms & causes
diseases.summary: Colon cancer is a malignancy of the large intestine that often grows silently at first. As it progresses, it commonly changes bowel function, causes bleeding, and can lead to anemia and general decline.

diseases.name: Colon polyps
diseases.summary: Colon polyps are small growths on the inner wall of the large intestine that usually cause no noticeable problems. Some types can gradually develop into bowel cancer, which is why doctors commonly find and remove them during routine screening. Most people learn they have them only through a test rather than from symptoms.

diseases.name: Color blindness
diseases.summary: This is a condition in which the eyes struggle to separate certain hues, most often reds from greens. It is usually inherited and appears more often in males, while seeing the world only in grayscale is extremely unusual. Some illnesses and medications can also trigger it, and an eye exam with color testing is the way to confirm it.

diseases.name: Coma
diseases.summary: A coma is a deep, lasting state in which a person cannot be roused and has no awareness of their environment. It can follow head trauma, stroke, bleeding in the brain, a tumor, poisoning, intoxication, or a systemic illness such as infection or dangerously abnormal blood sugar. Because it threatens life and brain function, it calls for immediate emergency evaluation, typically with blood tests and brain imaging to identify the cause.

diseases.name: Common cold
diseases.summary: A very widespread, self-limiting infection of the upper airways, usually caused by one of many viruses. It tends to clear up without treatment within about a week or so, though people who smoke may be ill for longer. Medical review is generally only needed if symptoms persist, worsen, or involve high fever or breathing trouble.

diseases.name: Common cold in babies
diseases.summary: A mild viral infection of the upper airways that affects infants and very young children. Babies often show stuffy nose, sneezing, and fussiness, and they can have trouble feeding or sleeping when congestion makes breathing harder. Most cases clear up on their own within a week or two, but young infants warrant prompt medical attention if breathing or feeding worsens.

diseases.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
diseases.summary: This immune disorder leaves the body with too little of the protein-based defenses that fight infection, so affected people get repeated illnesses, especially in the sinuses, ears, and lungs. Signs often start in childhood or adolescence, though many people are not diagnosed until adulthood. The condition can also raise the chance of digestive, autoimmune, blood, and some cancers, and it can run in families.

diseases.name: Common warts
diseases.summary: Harmless, rough, grainy growths caused by a virus usually appear on the hands or fingers and often contain tiny dark specks. They can take months to show up after contact and frequently fade without treatment, though many people remove them for cosmetic or comfort reasons. Medical advice is worth seeking if they hurt, spread, or affect people with weakened immunity.

diseases.name: Complex regional pain syndrome
diseases.summary: This is a long-lasting pain disorder that most often involves one arm or leg, typically starting after an injury, surgery, or minor event. The nervous system seems to overreact, producing pain far greater than the original trigger along with changes in skin, temperature, swelling, and movement. Early diagnosis and physical therapy generally lead to better outcomes.

diseases.name: Complicated grief
diseases.summary: Grief that stays intense and keeps a person from resuming daily life, instead of easing over months, is a recognized condition that often calls for professional support. It tends to appear more often in women and older adults, especially after sudden deaths, the loss of a child, or when someone has little social support. Help is available, and therapy can make it possible to accept the loss and feel peace again.

diseases.name: Compulsive gambling
diseases.summary: Gambling disorder is a behavioral addiction in which a person repeatedly loses control over betting, keeps chasing losses, and continues despite mounting financial and personal harm. Symptoms are mostly psychological and behavioral, often including preoccupation with gambling and restlessness when trying to cut back. Treatment usually combines counseling, support groups, and sometimes medication.

diseases.name: Compulsive sexual behavior
diseases.summary: Compulsive sexual behavior is an intense, hard-to-control focus on sexual thoughts, urges, or actions that causes distress and disrupts health, work, or relationships. It is often used as a way to cope with loneliness, low mood, or stress. Treatment and self-help can help people regain control.

diseases.name: Concussion
diseases.summary: Concussion is a mild brain injury that disrupts how the brain works, usually from a blow to the head or body, and most often from falls. Symptoms can appear immediately or emerge over the following days, and most people recover fully, though recovery can take weeks. Any head injury warrants prompt medical evaluation, and some warning signs require emergency care.

diseases.name: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia
diseases.summary: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is an inherited group of disorders in which the adrenal glands cannot produce one of the enzymes needed to make cortisol, aldosterone, or sex hormones. The resulting hormone imbalance can show up as early genital differences or a life-threatening crisis in infants, or as early puberty, rapid growth, and fertility problems later on. It is manageable with ongoing treatment, though it has no cure.

diseases.name: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH)
diseases.summary: A structural defect in the baby's chest-abdomen divider forms during early pregnancy, letting abdominal organs push into the chest. This crowds and underdevelops the lungs, which can make breathing very hard right after birth, and it is often spotted on a routine prenatal scan. Severity ranges from barely noticeable to life-threatening.

diseases.name: Congenital heart defects in children
diseases.summary: Heart structure problems present from birth affect a meaningful number of newborns each year. Many are minor and need no intervention, while complex ones may require surgery at several points during childhood. Serious forms usually show up in infancy, whereas milder ones can stay hidden until a child is older.

diseases.name: Congenital heart disease in adults
diseases.summary: Heart structure problems present from birth can alter how blood circulates, and in adults they may first surface later in life or return after earlier treatment. Typical clues include unusual heart rhythms, bluish discoloration from low oxygen, breathlessness, fatigue during routine activity, and fluid swelling. Ongoing specialist follow-up is important even when a person feels well.

diseases.name: Congenital myasthenic syndromes
diseases.summary: This is an inherited group of rare neuromuscular disorders that appear when a child receives two faulty copies of a responsible gene, usually noticed at birth or in early childhood. Weakness in voluntary muscles tends to build with activity and can involve the eyes, face, swallowing, breathing and limbs. Although there is no cure, medications targeted to the specific gene involved usually ease the weakness, and some very mild cases need no treatment.

diseases.name: Conjoined twins
diseases.summary: Conjoined twins are identical babies that form when a single early embryo incompletely divides, leaving them joined, most often at the chest, belly, or pelvis, sometimes with shared organs. Ultrasound can usually detect them during pregnancy, and survival and the feasibility of separation depend on the joining site, the shared organs, and the surgical team's experience. The condition has no symptoms specific to it, so it is typically found through routine prenatal imaging.

diseases.name: Constipation
diseases.summary: Constipation means having trouble moving stool, usually fewer than three bowel movements in a week or stools that are hard to pass. It is a frequent complaint and is often tied to low fiber, low fluid intake, or too little movement, though medications and other illnesses can also be responsible. Most cases improve with lifestyle adjustments or over-the-counter remedies, but persistent cases or ones with warning signs like blood in the stool need medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Constipation in children
diseases.summary: Constipation in children means passing stool less often than usual or having difficulty and discomfort when passing it, often because the stool has become hard and dry. It is common in childhood and is usually managed with diet, fluids, and bowel habit changes, though it can occasionally lead to other problems.

diseases.name: Contact dermatitis
diseases.summary: A skin reaction that produces an itchy patch after the skin touches something that irritates it or triggers an allergy. It is not spread from person to person, and it usually fades within a few weeks once the trigger is removed. Symptoms can look different depending on skin tone, and the rash tends to appear where the skin met the trigger.

diseases.name: COPD
diseases.summary: COPD is a long-lasting lung disease in which damaged airways and tiny air sacs make it hard to move air in and out. Most cases trace back to years of breathing in smoke or other irritants. It tends to worsen gradually, but good treatment and avoiding exposures can keep it under control.

diseases.name: Corns and calluses
diseases.summary: Corns and calluses are areas of thickened skin that form as a protective response to repeated rubbing or pressure, most often on the feet and toes or on the hands. Corns are small with a hard central core, while calluses are broader and usually painless. Removing the cause of the friction typically makes them go away, but people with diabetes or poor circulation should see a clinician before treating them themselves.

diseases.name: Coronary artery disease
diseases.summary: Narrowing of the heart's blood vessels from fatty plaque build-up reduces oxygen delivery to the heart muscle, and it tends to progress slowly over years. Its main warning signs are chest discomfort and breathlessness that often appear during exertion, while a full blockage can trigger a heart attack that requires emergency treatment.

diseases.name: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)
diseases.summary: COVID-19 is a respiratory infection caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus and passes mainly through tiny airborne droplets during close contact. Many infected people have only mild symptoms or none, but older adults and people with other health problems face a higher risk of severe disease. Symptoms usually appear within about two weeks of exposure and often resemble a cold or flu.

diseases.name: Corticobasal degeneration
diseases.summary: A rare, progressive neurological disorder in which an abnormal build-up of tau protein damages nerve cells and shrinks parts of the brain. It can cause a mix of thinking, language, behavior, and movement problems, often starting on one side of the body. No cure exists yet, but medicines and therapies can help manage symptoms.

diseases.name: Costochondritis
diseases.summary: Costochondritis is an inflammation of the cartilage that connects the ribs to the breastbone, causing localized chest wall tenderness. It is usually benign and tends to resolve on its own over weeks to months, though its pain can closely mimic heart problems, so a medical evaluation is advisable to rule out serious causes.

diseases.name: Cough headaches
diseases.summary: A cough headache is a brief, pounding pain that comes on when a person coughs, sneezes, laughs, or strains. Most cases are harmless primary headaches, but a doctor should check new or unusual ones to rule out a serious underlying cause.

diseases.name: Cradle cap
diseases.summary: A common, harmless scalp condition in infants that causes greasy, yellowish flaky patches and usually fades by itself within a few months. Gentle daily washing with a mild shampoo helps loosen the scales, and a doctor should be consulted if home care fails or the patches spread.

diseases.name: Craniopharyngioma
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon, slow-growing benign growth near the pituitary gland at the base of the brain, found most often in children and older adults. Because it presses on nearby brain structures, it tends to produce vision changes, headaches, and hormone-related effects like frequent urination or slowed growth in kids. Its symptoms develop gradually, so they are often mistaken for other problems.

diseases.name: Craniosynostosis
diseases.summary: A birth condition in which one or more of the flexible seams between a baby's skull bones fuse too early, so the head grows in a lopsided or unusual shape. Signs are usually visible at birth and become clearer over the first few months, and surgery to reshape the skull is the usual treatment.

diseases.name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
diseases.summary: A rare, fast-moving brain disease caused by misfolded prion proteins that gradually destroy brain tissue. It brings worsening memory and thinking problems, along with sudden muscle jerks and loss of coordination. It is almost always fatal, usually within about a year of the first symptoms.

diseases.name: Crohn's disease
diseases.summary: Crohn's disease is a long-term condition in which the digestive tract becomes swollen and irritated, most often in the small intestine and colon. It tends to alternate between periods of flare-ups and calmer stretches, with symptoms like stomach pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. It has no cure, but treatment can usually keep it well controlled.

diseases.name: Croup
diseases.summary: Croup is a childhood viral infection that swells the upper airway around the voice box and windpipe, usually striking children between about six months and three years old. It typically produces a barking cough, hoarse voice, and noisy breathing, and symptoms often worsen at night. Most cases are mild and resolve within several days, but noisy breathing at rest or trouble breathing needs urgent medical attention.

diseases.name: Cryoglobulinemia
diseases.summary: Cryoglobulinemia is an unusual immune-related disorder in which certain blood proteins behave abnormally in the cold, sometimes provoking vessel-wall irritation. Many people with it never notice anything, while others develop skin, joint, nerve, or kidney problems that can flare and fade. It is often tied to hepatitis C, autoimmune conditions, or certain blood cancers, and treatment is guided by the underlying cause.

diseases.name: CSF leak (Cerebrospinal fluid leak)
diseases.summary: A CSF leak happens when a tear or opening in the membrane wrapping the brain and spinal cord lets some of the protective cushioning fluid escape. Spinal leaks typically cause a headache that eases when lying flat and returns when upright, while cranial leaks often show up as clear fluid draining from the nose or ear. Some cases resolve with rest, while others need a patch or surgical repair.

diseases.name: Cushing syndrome
diseases.summary: This hormonal disorder develops when the body is exposed to excess cortisol over an extended period, whether produced internally or introduced through steroid medications. It often changes body shape, skin, and mood, and can raise blood pressure, weaken bones, and occasionally lead to diabetes. Earlier treatment to bring cortisol down generally leads to better outcomes.

diseases.name: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: A slow-to-moderate skin cancer arising from B-type immune cells, where the lymphoma stays confined to the skin. It typically shows up as firm bumps or patches, most often on the head, trunk, or legs depending on the subtype. Some variants grow quickly or spread, so anyone with persistent or changing skin lumps should get them checked.

diseases.name: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare group of blood cancers that start in T lymphocytes and settle in the skin, where they can look like eczema or psoriasis at first. Symptoms often come and go for a long time before the disease becomes more obvious or stops responding to treatment. Lymph node enlargement and persistent itchy patches are the main reasons people see a doctor.

diseases.name: Cyclic vomiting syndrome
diseases.summary: This is a condition where a person has repeated, sudden bouts of intense nausea and vomiting that follow the same pattern each time, with normal health in between. Attacks can last from hours to several days and often leave the person worn out and dehydrated. Doctors usually diagnose it after ruling out other causes of recurring vomiting.

diseases.name: Cyclosporiasis (cyclospora parasite)
diseases.summary: This intestinal infection comes from a microscopic parasite that spreads through food or water contaminated with stool. Symptoms typically appear about a week after exposure and can wax and wane over weeks or longer. Most healthy adults recover without prescription drugs, while people with weakened immunity may need specific antibiotic treatment.

diseases.name: Cyclothymia (cyclothymic disorder)
diseases.summary: This long-term mood condition involves repeated swings between energized, elevated periods and milder low periods, with steadier stretches in between. The shifts are less intense than in bipolar disorder but can still disrupt work, relationships, and routines, and it often begins in the teens or early adulthood. Because it rarely resolves without care and can progress to bipolar disorder, ongoing professional evaluation and follow-up are important.

diseases.name: Cystic fibrosis
diseases.summary: A lifelong inherited disorder that thickens mucus and other body secretions, mainly clogging the lungs and digestive tract. Many people now get identified early through newborn screening, and while there is no cure, treatment has improved survival and daily living considerably. Ongoing care with a specialist and regular check-ups is central to managing it.

diseases.name: Cystitis
diseases.summary: Cystitis is swelling and irritation of the bladder, most often triggered by a bacterial urinary tract infection. It typically causes urinary urgency, burning, and frequent small voids, and it can occasionally be set off by medications, radiation, irritating products, or another illness. Antibiotics are the usual treatment when bacteria are the cause, and back pain, fever with chills, or vomiting suggest a kidney infection that needs prompt care.

diseases.name: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection
diseases.summary: Cytomegalovirus is a herpes-family virus that many people pick up during their lives and then carry without noticing any problems. When it does cause symptoms in otherwise healthy people, they usually look like a flu-like or mono-like illness. The infection can be dangerous for newborns, pregnant people, and those with weakened immune systems.

diseases.name: Dandruff
diseases.summary: Flaky, itchy scalp is a mild, long-lasting skin problem that is harmless and not contagious, though it can be hard to clear. Gentle routine washing often helps, and a medicated shampoo may be needed if it does not. It tends to flare in dry weather or during stress, and it cannot be fully cured but can usually be kept under control.

diseases.name: De Quervain tenosynovitis
diseases.summary: A painful inflammation of the tendons running along the thumb side of the wrist, typically brought on or worsened by repetitive gripping, lifting, or wrist motions. Discomfort tends to show up near the base of the thumb and can radiate into the forearm if left alone. Most people improve with rest and basic home measures, though persistent symptoms warrant a clinical look.

diseases.name: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
diseases.summary: A blood clot forms in a deep vein, most often in a leg, and can partly or fully block blood flow. The problem often shows up as one swollen, tender, warm limb, sometimes with discoloration. The main danger is that a piece of the clot can break loose and travel to the lungs.

diseases.name: Dehydration
diseases.summary: Dehydration happens when the body loses more water than it takes in, leaving less fluid than it needs to work normally. Most mild cases resolve with drinking fluids, but severe cases can strain the heart and kidneys and need prompt medical care.

diseases.name: Delayed ejaculation
diseases.summary: Men with this problem need unusually long stimulation before they reach orgasm and release semen, and some cannot ejaculate at all. It can be present from the start of sexual life or appear later, and it is often linked to medical illness, certain medications, surgery, or emotional and relationship strain. It is worth attention mainly when it persists and causes distress for the man or his partner.

diseases.name: Delayed sleep phase
diseases.summary: A body clock running several hours late makes a person fall asleep and wake well after conventional times, and this pattern persists for months or years. The resulting mismatch often makes school or work mornings very hard. Sleep habit changes, melatonin, and light therapy are commonly used to shift the timing back.

diseases.name: Delirium
diseases.summary: Delirium is an abrupt disturbance of attention and awareness that usually develops within hours to days, often alongside an illness, infection, medication effect, surgery, or substance withdrawal. Its symptoms rise and fall during the day and can resemble dementia, but the underlying trigger is often treatable. Because it can signal a dangerous medical problem, it calls for prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Dementia
diseases.summary: Dementia is an umbrella term for a set of thinking, memory, and social-functioning problems severe enough to disrupt everyday life, and it can arise from several different underlying diseases. Forgetfulness on its own does not confirm it, since many other causes exist, and some forms may be reversible when the root cause is treated. Anyone noticing these changes in themselves or a family member should get a medical evaluation to find the cause.

diseases.name: Dengue fever
diseases.summary: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection found mainly in tropical and subtropical regions. Many infected people feel nothing, while others develop a sudden high fever with body aches and headache that can resemble the flu. A small share progress to a dangerous form involving bleeding and circulatory collapse, which needs emergency treatment.

diseases.name: Depersonalization-derealization disorder
diseases.summary: This is a mental health condition in which a person repeatedly feels detached from their own body or thoughts, or sees their surroundings as unreal, while usually recognizing that these sensations don't match reality. It tends to follow major stress or trauma and can interfere with work, school, and relationships. Counseling is the main treatment, sometimes combined with medication.

diseases.name: Depression (major depressive disorder)
diseases.summary: Depression is a treatable mental health condition that goes well beyond ordinary low spirits, often lasting for weeks and affecting emotions, energy, sleep, and daily functioning. It can affect people of any age or background and frequently recurs over a lifetime. Anyone noticing these changes should contact a doctor or mental health professional, and anyone having thoughts of self-harm should seek immediate help.

diseases.name: Dermatitis
diseases.summary: Dermatitis is a widespread skin condition in which the skin becomes inflamed and irritated, often showing up as itchy, dry patches or rashes. It can take many forms, such as eczema, contact reactions and seborrheic types, each tending to affect different areas of the body. It is not passed from person to person, but it can be quite bothersome and is usually managed with regular moisturizing and topical treatments.

diseases.name: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP)
diseases.summary: A slow-growing skin tumor that starts in the connective tissue of the dermis and usually shows up as a firm, raised patch or bump on the arms, legs, or torso. It can resemble harmless skin lesions, so tissue sampling is typically needed to confirm it. Surgical removal is the main treatment, and the biggest concern is that it may return at the same site.

diseases.name: Dermatographia (Dermatographism)
diseases.summary: This skin reaction appears when the surface is lightly stroked or scraped, producing raised, reddened lines that usually fade within half an hour. It is generally harmless, often linked to outside triggers, and most people need no treatment beyond antihistamines if the marks are bothersome. It is more frequent in younger people and those who already have conditions such as eczema.

diseases.name: Dermatomyositis
diseases.summary: Dermatomyositis is an inflammatory disorder that affects muscles and skin, causing weakness in the shoulders, hips, and neck along with a distinctive rash. It can also involve other organs, and early treatment helps prevent lasting muscle damage.

diseases.name: Desmoid tumors
diseases.summary: A rare, non-cancerous growth made of connective-tissue cells that usually appears in the abdominal wall or limbs, though it can form almost anywhere. It cannot spread elsewhere but can push into nearby tissues, so behavior ranges from slow-growing to aggressive and many need no treatment. Diagnosis requires a biopsy because it can be mistaken for other soft tissue tumors.

diseases.name: Desmoplastic small round cell tumors
diseases.summary: A very rare and fast-growing cancer that usually begins in the lining of the abdomen and pelvis, though it can arise elsewhere. It tends to spread early to nearby organs and bones, and it is most often seen in young males. Treatment usually combines surgery with chemotherapy, radiation, and targeted drugs.

diseases.name: Deviated septum
diseases.summary: A deviated septum is a shift of the thin wall dividing the two nostrils, often present from birth or caused by an injury to the nose. Many people with a mild shift notice nothing, while a larger one can make breathing through one side of the nose harder and contribute to congestion, snoring, or frequent sinus trouble.

diseases.name: Diabetes
diseases.summary: Diabetes is a set of long-term conditions in which the body struggles to regulate blood glucose, leading to excess sugar circulating in the bloodstream. Some forms are lifelong, while prediabetes and gestational diabetes may be reversible or resolve after pregnancy. Many people, particularly those with milder or early forms, have no noticeable signs, so early testing matters.

diseases.name: Diabetes insipidus
diseases.summary: A hormone-related disorder in which the kidneys fail to hold onto water, so affected people pass very large volumes of dilute urine and feel constantly driven to drink. It is unrelated to blood-sugar diabetes and has no cure, but medication can reduce thirst and urine output. Prompt medical evaluation is advised when frequent urination and intense thirst appear together.

diseases.name: Diabetic coma
diseases.summary: A diabetic coma is a life-threatening state of unresponsiveness that arises when blood sugar in a person with diabetes swings to a dangerous extreme. It most often follows a complication like diabetic ketoacidosis or a severely dehydrating high-sugar state, though profoundly low blood sugar can produce the same picture. Because the brain relies on steady glucose and fluid levels, it needs emergency medical care.

diseases.name: Diabetic hypoglycemia
diseases.summary: Low blood sugar in people with diabetes causes a rapid set of body reactions, often from too much insulin, too little food, or extra exercise. It can range from mild shakiness to confusion or loss of consciousness if untreated. Prompt sugar intake usually reverses it, but recurrent or severe episodes need medical review.

diseases.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis
diseases.summary: Diabetic ketoacidosis is a serious complication that mostly affects people with diabetes, when the body lacks enough insulin and begins breaking down fat for fuel. This produces acids called ketones that build up in the blood and can quickly lead to dangerous dehydration and changes in acid-base balance. It requires urgent medical treatment.

diseases.name: Diabetic nephropathy (kidney disease)
diseases.summary: Kidney damage caused by long-standing diabetes gradually wears down the filters that clean waste and excess fluid from the blood. It often produces no noticeable signs early on, and problems tend to surface only as the disease advances. Regular kidney function testing for people with diabetes allows it to be caught and managed before it progresses.

diseases.name: Diabetic neuropathy
diseases.summary: Diabetic neuropathy is nerve damage caused by prolonged high blood sugar, usually starting in the toes and feet and moving upward over time. People often describe tingling, numbness, or burning discomfort, and reduced sensation can make injuries go unnoticed. Seeing a doctor early and keeping blood sugar under control can slow the damage.

diseases.name: Diabetic retinopathy
diseases.summary: Diabetic retinopathy is an eye disease that develops in people with diabetes when high blood sugar gradually damages the small blood vessels of the retina. Early stages often cause no noticeable problems, but as it advances it can distort or block vision. Regular eye exams are important because it can progress without warning.

diseases.name: Diaper rash
diseases.summary: An irritation of the skin under a nappy, most often seen in babies and toddlers, caused by prolonged moisture and contact with waste. It typically looks localized to the covered area and usually improves within days with routine cleaning and protective cream.

diseases.name: Diarrhea
diseases.summary: Diarrhea means stools that are loose, watery, and more frequent than usual, and it is usually brief. When it continues for more than a couple of days, or comes with blood, dehydration, or high fever, it can signal a larger problem that needs medical review.

diseases.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: A fast-growing blood cancer that begins in a type of white blood cell called a B cell, usually showing up as painless lumps in the lymph nodes. It can spread to bone marrow and organs such as the stomach and intestines, brain, bones, or skin, and symptoms depend on where it has taken hold. Although it grows quickly, it often responds well to treatment and can sometimes be cured, especially when caught early.

diseases.name: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG)
diseases.summary: A rare and fast-moving cancer that forms in the central midline of the brain or spinal cord and spreads into surrounding healthy tissue. It is most often found in young children but can occur in adults. Symptoms tend to appear suddenly and worsen quickly, and the disease is difficult to catch early.

diseases.name: DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion syndrome)
diseases.summary: A genetic condition caused by a missing segment of chromosome 22 leads to underdeveloped body systems, most often affecting the heart, immune defenses, palate, and calcium balance. Its signs vary widely in type and severity and can show up at birth or emerge later in childhood or adulthood. Because many organ systems are involved, care usually requires several medical specialties.

diseases.name: Dilated cardiomyopathy
diseases.summary: Dilated cardiomyopathy is a condition in which the heart's main pumping chamber enlarges and weakens, so it cannot pump blood effectively. As a result, fluid can build up and the body receives less oxygen during everyday activity. It is a serious long-term heart disease that often progresses gradually and needs ongoing medical management.

symptoms.name: shortness of breath when lying flat

diseases.name: Diphtheria
diseases.summary: A bacterial infection that mainly affects the throat and nose and spreads through airborne droplets from coughing or sneezing. The toxin it releases can swell the airway and damage the heart and nerves. Routine childhood vaccination has made it very rare in countries that vaccinate widely.

diseases.name: Dislocated shoulder
diseases.summary: A shoulder slips out of its socket when the upper arm bone is forced from the joint, most often during a fall or contact sport. It typically causes sharp pain, visible deformity, and loss of movement, and it needs urgent medical reduction. Most people recover good function within several weeks, though the joint becomes more prone to repeat dislocations afterward.

diseases.name: Dissociative disorders
diseases.summary: This is a group of mental health conditions where a person's sense of self, memory, or awareness of their surroundings becomes disconnected, often as a way of coping with trauma. Symptoms differ by subtype and can include memory gaps or feeling that one's identity is fragmented. Stress tends to make these episodes more noticeable, and talk therapy and medication are commonly used to help people manage them.

diseases.name: Diverticulitis
diseases.summary: Diverticulitis happens when small pouches in the wall of the large intestine become swollen or infected. It most often affects adults past middle age and typically causes lower-left belly pain along with fever or changes in bowel habits. Constant, unexplained belly pain with fever or stool changes calls for prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Dizziness
diseases.summary: Dizziness covers a spectrum of sensations, from light-headedness and wooziness to a spinning feeling known as vertigo. It is a frequent reason adults seek medical help but seldom signals a life-threatening problem. Episodes can last seconds or days and often recur, and older adults face higher risk.

diseases.name: Double uterus
diseases.summary: A condition present from birth in which the uterus forms as two separate organs instead of one, sometimes with a divided vagina as well. Most affected people never notice it, and it is often found during a routine exam or while investigating miscarriages. Pregnancy is often successful, though the condition raises the chance of miscarriage or preterm birth.

diseases.name: Double-outlet right ventricle
diseases.summary: A rare heart defect present from birth in which both major arteries leaving the heart come off the right lower pumping chamber instead of the usual sides. Many affected infants also have a hole between the two lower chambers, and most need surgery, with good long-term outcomes when repaired and followed by a specialist.

diseases.name: Down syndrome
diseases.summary: Down syndrome is a genetic condition in which a cell division error leaves a person with an extra full or partial copy of chromosome 21. That extra genetic material drives lifelong intellectual disability, developmental delays, distinctive physical features, and a higher chance of heart and digestive problems. It is usually identified before or at birth, and early therapy and support can greatly improve daily functioning.

diseases.name: Dressler syndrome
diseases.summary: A condition where the thin sac around the heart becomes inflamed weeks to months after heart muscle injury from a heart attack, heart surgery, or chest trauma, likely due to an immune reaction. It is also called post-cardiac injury syndrome or post-pericardiotomy syndrome. Chest pain that worsens with breathing is the hallmark, and it can mimic a heart attack, so any sudden or ongoing chest pain needs emergency evaluation.

diseases.name: Drug addiction (substance use disorder)
diseases.summary: Drug addiction is a brain-based condition in which a person cannot control their use of a substance, whether illegal, prescribed, or legal like alcohol or nicotine, even when it is clearly causing harm. It often starts casually and escalates over time, with rising tolerance and withdrawal when stopping. Treatment and support from clinicians, peers, or structured programs can help people recover.

diseases.name: Drug allergy
diseases.summary: A drug allergy occurs when the immune system overreacts to a medication, which can be any over-the-counter, prescription, or herbal product. Reactions most often show up as skin changes such as hives or rash, but they can escalate to a life-threatening emergency called anaphylaxis. Anyone with trouble breathing or a sudden collapse after taking a drug needs emergency help right away.

diseases.name: Dry eyes
diseases.summary: A common long-term surface eye problem in which the eyes don't keep enough moisture, so they feel uncomfortable and can look irritated. It often comes from tear film that evaporates too quickly or is poor in quality, and it tends to be worse in dry air, with screen use, or with age. Symptoms are usually manageable with lubricating drops and lifestyle changes.

diseases.name: Dry macular degeneration
diseases.summary: This age-related eye disorder gradually wears down the central region of the retina that handles sharp, straight-ahead sight, so details become fuzzy over time. Edge vision generally survives, which means complete blindness is unlikely, though the loss of central clarity ranges from slight to substantial. Spotting changes early and adjusting daily habits can slow the progression.

diseases.name: Dry mouth
diseases.summary: Dry mouth happens when the salivary glands do not produce enough saliva to keep the mouth moist. It is most often linked to aging, medications, or radiation to the head and neck, and it can affect eating, speech, and dental health. Persistent symptoms warrant a visit to a healthcare professional.

diseases.name: Dry skin
diseases.summary: Dry skin is a very widespread complaint in which the outer layer of skin lacks moisture, leaving it feeling tight, rough, itchy, and flaky. It can be triggered by weather, harsh cleansers, and frequent washing, and most people improve with moisturizers and gentle skin care. Medical attention is worth seeking when the problem persists, becomes painful or inflamed, or breaks open.

diseases.name: Dry socket
diseases.summary: A painful complication that can follow tooth removal, it occurs when the protective clot in the empty socket fails to form or is lost before healing finishes, leaving the bone and nerves exposed. Pain typically starts a day or few after the extraction and can radiate toward the ear, eye, or neck on the same side. Because store-bought pain relievers are often insufficient, a dentist or oral surgeon should be contacted promptly.

diseases.name: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS)
diseases.summary: This cancer is an early, non-invasive growth of abnormal cells confined to a milk duct of the breast, and it often produces no noticeable signs. It is usually discovered on a mammogram rather than by touch. Treatment is generally recommended because it cannot reliably be predicted whether it will progress to an invasive form.

diseases.name: Dumping syndrome
diseases.summary: A condition in which stomach contents pass too quickly into the small intestine, most often after stomach surgery or weight-loss procedures. Symptoms tend to arrive either shortly after a meal or one to three hours later, when blood sugar falls. Diet adjustments are usually the first approach, with a clinician guiding evaluation and treatment.

diseases.name: Dupuytren contracture
diseases.summary: A slowly progressing hand disorder in which tissue in the palm thickens and tightens into cords, gradually pulling one or more fingers toward the palm. It is more common in older men, those of Northern European descent, and people with diabetes, and it has no cure, though treatments can ease symptoms and slow its course.

diseases.name: Dural arteriovenous fistulas
diseases.summary: A dural arteriovenous fistula is an abnormal shortcut linking arteries and veins in the membrane that wraps the brain. It is very uncommon and usually appears in middle age. Many people never notice it, but when symptoms appear they depend on the location and can range from annoying to life-threatening bleeding, so treatment aims to close off the abnormal flow.

diseases.name: Dust mite allergy
diseases.summary: Dust mite allergy is an immune overreaction to proteins found in the waste and body fragments of microscopic house dust mites. When someone inhales these particles, the body can trigger sneezing, nasal congestion, itchy eyes, and sometimes wheezing or breathing difficulty. Symptoms often flare in bedrooms, upholstered furniture, and bedding, and they are usually year-round rather than seasonal.

diseases.name: Dwarfism
diseases.summary: Dwarfism is a group of genetic or medical conditions that leave a person noticeably shorter than average, with adult height at or under about 4 foot 10. Some forms shrink the arms and legs more than the trunk, while others shrink the whole body evenly, and the condition usually appears at birth or in early childhood. Most cases are not inherited from parents, and anyone worried about a child's growth should bring it up with a pediatric clinician.

diseases.name: Dysarthria
diseases.summary: Dysarthria is a speech disorder in which the muscles needed to talk are either weakened or hard to coordinate, so words come out garbled, slow, or hard to follow. It frequently stems from a nervous system condition or facial muscle weakness, and certain medications can trigger it too. A sudden or unexplained change in how someone speaks warrants prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Dyshidrosis
diseases.summary: This is a recurring skin disorder that produces clusters of itchy, fluid-filled bumps on the hands and sometimes the feet. Episodes usually last a few weeks, then the bumps dry out and peel, and flare-ups can continue for months or years. Stress, metal exposure, and eczema-prone skin can make it more likely.

diseases.name: Dyslexia
diseases.summary: Dyslexia is a brain-based difference in processing language that makes it hard to connect sounds with letters and words, which leads to slow or inaccurate reading despite normal intelligence, hearing, and vision. It is lifelong, but structured teaching and early support lead to much better outcomes, and help is worthwhile at any age. Family history raises the chance of having it.

diseases.name: Dysphagia
diseases.summary: Dysphagia is the medical name for difficulty moving food or liquid from the mouth down to the stomach. It often feels like swallowing takes extra work or that food gets caught along the way. Occasional trouble is usually harmless, but persistent difficulty needs evaluation because it can lead to choking, malnutrition, and other complications.

diseases.name: Dystonia
diseases.summary: A neurological condition in which involuntary muscle activity produces repeated, uncontrolled movements or awkward postures. It can stay in one body region, spread to nearby areas, or affect the whole body, and it may interfere with everyday activities. Medication and therapy can ease the effects, though the underlying condition cannot currently be reversed.

diseases.name: E. coli
diseases.summary: A gut infection caused by certain strains of E. coli bacteria, usually picked up from contaminated water or undercooked food, leads to diarrhea that can be watery or bloody along with cramping. Most healthy adults recover on their own within about a week, but young children and older adults face a risk of severe kidney damage.

diseases.name: Ear infection (middle ear)
diseases.summary: A middle-ear infection is an inflammation of the air-filled space behind the eardrum, usually after a cold or blocked Eustachian tube. It is very common in young children and often causes ear pain, fever, and a sense of muffled hearing. Most cases improve on their own or with treatment from a primary care clinician.

diseases.name: Earwax blockage
diseases.summary: Hardened ear wax can accumulate in the ear canal and physically block sound from reaching the eardrum. The main effects are a plugged feeling and reduced hearing, and it is usually easy to resolve with softening drops or gentle removal by a clinician.

diseases.name: Eating disorders
diseases.summary: Eating disorders are mental and physical health conditions marked by distorted thoughts about food, weight and body shape, along with harmful eating habits. The main types are anorexia, bulimia and binge-eating disorder, and they can damage the heart, digestion, bones and teeth. Early treatment improves the chances of recovery.

diseases.name: Ebstein anomaly
diseases.summary: This is a heart problem that exists from birth, where one of the heart's right-sided valves is malformed and sits lower than normal. The faulty valve lets blood leak backward, which strains the heart and can eventually lead to enlargement and heart failure. Some affected people have no symptoms for years, while others have noticeable signs that prompt early medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Ectopic pregnancy
diseases.summary: Ectopic pregnancy happens when a fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, most often in a fallopian tube, and it cannot develop normally. It is a medical emergency because the growing tissue can rupture and cause serious internal bleeding. Early symptoms are often mild and resemble a late period or stomach upset, so prompt evaluation matters.

diseases.name: Ectropion
diseases.summary: A drooping lower eyelid turns outward and no longer sits against the eyeball, so the eye cannot be fully protected or kept moist. The result is often dryness, tearing, and irritation, and the condition becomes more likely with age. Non-surgical measures can ease the discomfort, but a procedure is typically needed to correct the eyelid position.

diseases.name: Edema
diseases.summary: Edema is a buildup of extra fluid in body tissues that causes visible swelling, most often in the legs and feet. It can be triggered by certain medications, pregnancy, or an underlying illness such as heart failure, kidney or liver disease, or poor venous circulation. Treating the underlying cause and easing the swelling are both important, and some breathing or chest symptoms signal a need for urgent care.

diseases.name: Egg allergy
diseases.summary: An immune system overreaction to proteins found in egg whites, most often in young children. Reactions can range from mild skin changes to serious breathing or circulation problems, and some people need to avoid all egg products.

diseases.name: EGPA (formerly Churg-Strauss syndrome)
diseases.summary: EGPA is a rare autoimmune condition in which the immune system inflames small and medium blood vessels while causing a high count of a certain white blood cell. It typically begins with long-standing asthma and sinus problems, then spreads to nerves, skin, the gut, and the heart. Prompt specialist care matters because heart and organ involvement can progress quickly.

diseases.name: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
diseases.summary: A family of hereditary disorders that weaken the body's supportive tissue, most visibly in joints, skin, and blood vessels. Typical cases involve unusually loose joints and delicate skin that bruises and scars easily, while a rare vascular subtype carries a risk of sudden artery or organ rupture. Although it can't be cured, regular monitoring and symptom care can ease daily problems and reduce complications.

diseases.name: Ehrlichiosis and anaplasmosis
diseases.summary: Tick-borne infections caused by bacteria passed through bites from infected ticks, often showing up as a flu-like illness within two weeks of exposure. Prompt treatment with the correct antibiotic typically brings improvement within a few days, but delay can lead to serious complications. Many people who are infected never develop noticeable symptoms.

diseases.name: Eisenmenger syndrome
diseases.summary: A long-standing, uncorrected heart defect present from birth can gradually raise pressure in the lung arteries and damage their walls, leading to a life-threatening condition. Early repair of the original defect generally prevents it, and once established it is managed with regular checkups and medication. Anyone with these symptoms, especially breathlessness or chest pain, should seek medical evaluation promptly.

diseases.name: Elevated blood pressure
diseases.summary: Raised pressure inside the arteries that persists above the normal range, usually causing no obvious signs for years. It is a very frequent long-term circulatory condition that raises the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney damage if left unmanaged. Many people only discover it during routine checks or when a complication appears.

diseases.name: Embolic stroke (brain embolism)
diseases.summary: A blockage in a brain artery caused by material that formed elsewhere and traveled through the bloodstream produces a sudden loss of function that usually appears within minutes. Warning signs often include facial droop, arm weakness, speech trouble, and vision changes, and any suspicion calls for immediate emergency care. Heart rhythm problems such as atrial fibrillation are a frequent source of these travelling clots.

diseases.name: Embryonal tumors
diseases.summary: Embryonal tumors are aggressive brain cancers arising from leftover fetal cells, mostly affecting infants and young children though adults can develop them. They can invade surrounding brain tissue and spread through the spinal fluid, so prompt specialist evaluation matters.

diseases.name: Emphysema
diseases.summary: Emphysema is a long-lasting lung disease in which the tiny air sacs slowly break down, leaving fewer and larger spaces for gas exchange. It is mostly driven by smoking and typically shows up after middle age as breathlessness that worsens over time. Treatment can ease symptoms and slow progression, but the lost lung tissue does not come back.

diseases.name: EncephalitisSymptoms and causes
diseases.summary: Encephalitis is swelling of the brain tissue, most often triggered by a virus. It can change how a person thinks, feels, and moves, and it can progress within hours to days. It is a medical emergency that needs prompt hospital assessment.

diseases.name: Encopresis
diseases.summary: Encopresis is a condition in which a child old enough to be toilet trained repeatedly has bowel movements in clothing or other unintended places. It is most often tied to long-standing constipation, where liquid stool leaks around a backed-up mass of hard stool. Treatment usually focuses on emptying the bowel and rebuilding regular toilet habits.

diseases.name: End-stage kidney disease
diseases.summary: When the kidneys can no longer keep up with the body's filtering and fluid-balance demands, waste and extra water accumulate to dangerous levels. Patients at this stage depend on dialysis or a transplant, or may choose comfort-focused care aimed at quality of life. Early disease often causes no noticeable signs, so symptoms tend to appear only once damage is advanced.

diseases.name: Endocarditis
diseases.summary: A bacterial or fungal infection of the heart's inner lining, most often affecting the valves. Germs that enter the bloodstream can settle on damaged or abnormal valves and cause injury that spreads to other organs. Symptoms often develop gradually and look like a general illness, which can delay diagnosis.

diseases.name: Endometrial cancer
diseases.summary: Endometrial cancer is a malignancy that develops in the inner tissue of the womb. Unusual bleeding is often the first sign, which tends to prompt people to get checked before the disease has spread. When it is caught early, removing the uterus surgically frequently leads to a cure.

diseases.name: Endometriosis
diseases.summary: Endometriosis is a long-term condition in which tissue resembling the uterine lining grows in places outside the uterus, most often in the pelvis. Because this tissue reacts to the menstrual cycle, it commonly causes pain that tends to worsen over time, and some people have no symptoms at all. Care is effective, but the condition is often hard to recognize early because its symptoms overlap with other pelvic and bowel disorders.

diseases.name: Enlarged breasts in men (gynecomastia)
diseases.summary: Gynecomastia is a benign growth of breast gland tissue in males, driven by an imbalance between estrogen and testosterone. It is common during newborn life, puberty, and older age, and often resolves without treatment. Persistent cases can be managed with medication or surgery, and warning signs such as lumps or nipple discharge warrant a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Enlarged heart
diseases.summary: An enlarged heart means the heart's chambers or muscle walls have grown beyond their normal size, usually because they have been working against high blood pressure, faulty valves, or a weakened muscle. As the enlargement advances, the heart often pumps less efficiently, which can cause fluid to back up into the lungs and legs. Many people have no symptoms early on and the condition is found during imaging for another reason.

diseases.name: Enlarged liver
diseases.summary: An enlarged liver, also called hepatomegaly, means the liver is bigger than its normal size and is usually discovered during a physical exam or imaging. It often reflects an underlying problem such as fat buildup, inflammation, congestion, or infiltration by other material. Many people feel no symptoms at first, and the cause determines what follow-up is needed.

diseases.name: Enlarged spleen (splenomegaly)
diseases.summary: An enlarged spleen often produces no noticeable signs and is frequently found during a routine exam. When it does cause problems, they tend to involve discomfort under the left ribs, early fullness when eating, or effects on blood cells such as anemia and easy bruising or bleeding. Many different conditions, from infections to liver disease, cancers, and inherited metabolic disorders, can be behind it, so a doctor usually needs imaging and blood tests to find the cause.

diseases.name: Entropion
diseases.summary: A lid that folds inward lets lashes and skin scrape across the front of the eye, leading to ongoing irritation and possible surface damage.
