It is most often seen in older adults, typically on the lower lid. Treatment usually requires a procedure, while lubricants and protective lenses can ease symptoms in the meantime.

diseases.name: Eosinophilic esophagitisSymptoms and causes
diseases.summary: A long-lasting allergy-related inflammation of the food pipe, in which a particular type of immune cell gathers in the lining and makes it stiff and narrow. The main complaint is trouble getting food down, and food can occasionally become lodged, sometimes requiring urgent removal. It is more often diagnosed in people with other allergic conditions and in men, though it can affect anyone.

diseases.name: Ependymoma
diseases.summary: A tumor arising from the lining cells of the brain's fluid channels or the spinal cord, which can be slow-growing or aggressive. It is most often diagnosed in children, while adults more often develop it in the spinal cord. Symptoms depend on the tumor's location and commonly involve headache, seizures, vision changes, or problems with walking and balance.

diseases.name: Epidermoid cysts
diseases.summary: A harmless, slow-growing lump under the skin, usually on the face, neck, or trunk, that often causes no discomfort. Most are left alone, though removal is an option if one becomes sore, ruptures, or is bothersome. Anyone can get one, but adults past puberty and people who have injured the skin are more prone.

diseases.name: Epidermolysis bullosa
diseases.summary: A hereditary disorder in which the skin and sometimes internal linings form blisters after even slight friction or heat. Most cases appear in infancy or early childhood, though some milder forms surface later. Care centers on protecting the skin and preventing new blisters, since there is no cure.

diseases.name: Epididymitis
diseases.summary: A bacterial infection, often sexually transmitted, inflames the tube behind a testicle that stores and carries sperm, causing scrotal pain and swelling. It is usually treated with antibiotics and symptom relief. Prompt evaluation matters because untreated scrotal pain can occasionally lead to lasting harm.

diseases.name: Epiglottitis
diseases.summary: A swelling of the small flap at the top of the windpipe can quickly block airflow, making it a life-threatening emergency. It was once seen mostly in young children, but routine vaccination has made it rare in that group and it now appears more often in adults. Breathing trouble and difficulty swallowing are the warning signs that need immediate emergency care.

diseases.name: Epilepsy
diseases.summary: Epilepsy is a long-term brain condition marked by repeated seizures, which are bursts of irregular nerve activity. Roughly three million Americans live with it, and it can begin at any age, most often in early childhood or later in life. Seizure symptoms depend on where in the brain they start, ranging from brief staring to full-body convulsions.

diseases.name: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE)
diseases.summary: A rare, slow-or-fast-growing tumor of the blood vessel lining cells, it can appear in the lungs, liver, soft tissue, or bones and is often found by chance on imaging. Symptoms depend on where it sits, and many people have none at all. Its cause is unknown, and treatment depends on tumor location, symptoms, and spread.

diseases.name: Epithelioid sarcoma
diseases.summary: A rare, slow-growing cancer of the connective tissues that often shows up as a firm lump under the skin, most frequently on the hands, fingers, or forearms. It is most often seen in teenagers and younger adults, and it has a tendency to return after treatment. Specialized sarcoma centers are generally recommended for care.

diseases.name: Erectile dysfunction
diseases.summary: Erectile dysfunction is the ongoing difficulty a man has in getting or holding an erection firm enough for sex. Occasional trouble is normal, but persistent cases can point to an underlying physical or emotional cause and are worth raising with a doctor, since treatments are available. It becomes more likely with age, diabetes, heart disease, smoking, and excess weight.

diseases.name: Esophageal cancer
diseases.summary: This cancer begins in the inner lining of the food pipe that carries swallowed food to the stomach, and it often causes no noticeable signs until it has grown considerably. Its biggest risk factors are long-standing acid reflux, tobacco, alcohol, and obesity, and men are affected more often. Treatment usually centers on surgical removal, sometimes combined with chemotherapy, radiation, or newer targeted drugs.

diseases.name: Esophageal spasms
diseases.summary: A muscle in the food pipe between the throat and stomach tightens painfully and involuntarily, which can feel like a crushing pain behind the breastbone that people often confuse with a heart problem. Episodes tend to be occasional and short-lived, though frequent cases can make swallowing difficult and may need medical treatment. Because chest pain of this kind can also signal a heart attack, it should be checked promptly.

diseases.name: Esophageal varices
diseases.summary: Enlarged veins in the food pipe can form when liver scarring or disease slows blood flow through the liver, forcing blood into fragile side vessels. Most people with these veins have no noticeable signs until one bleeds, which can be life-threatening. Bleeding usually shows up as vomiting blood or dark, tarry stools.

diseases.name: Esophagitis
diseases.summary: Inflammation of the esophagus can make swallowing painful or difficult and may cause chest discomfort. It often results from stomach acid flowing backward, though infections, certain medications, and allergies can also be responsible. Untreated, it can damage the esophageal lining and lead to narrowing, weight loss, or dehydration.

diseases.name: Essential tremor
diseases.summary: A slowly progressing neurological disorder that produces rhythmic, involuntary shaking, most often felt in the hands during everyday activities. It tends to run in families and becomes more common with age, particularly after 40. Although it is rarely dangerous, it can worsen over time and is sometimes mistaken for Parkinson's disease.

diseases.name: Esthesioneuroblastoma
diseases.summary: A rare cancer that starts high inside the nose and can extend into nearby sinuses, eyes, and brain. It tends to show up first as a change in smell, bleeding from the nose, or blocked breathing through the nose. Treatment usually combines surgery with radiation and chemotherapy.

diseases.name: Estrogen receptor (ER) positive breast cancer
diseases.summary: This form of breast cancer carries receptors that respond to estrogen, so the hormone can fuel its growth. Many people have no early warning signs, but a new lump, skin or nipple change, or persistent breast pain should prompt a prompt visit to a clinician. Hormone-blocking treatments are a central part of managing it.

diseases.name: Ewing sarcoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer of the bone and nearby soft tissue that mainly strikes children and young adults, typically starting in the leg bones or pelvis. Treatment advances have greatly improved survival, though survivors may face long-term effects that call for ongoing monitoring. Bone-focused complaints such as pain, swelling, or a lump, together with general signs like fever and weight loss, are the usual reasons people seek evaluation.

diseases.name: Exercise headaches
diseases.summary: A headache that starts during or just after physical effort, such as running or lifting. Most cases are harmless primary headaches that resolve on their own within minutes to a couple of days. A first episode still warrants medical evaluation to rule out a serious underlying cause, such as bleeding around the brain.

diseases.name: Exercise-induced asthma
diseases.summary: Exercise-induced asthma is a condition in which the airways tighten during or shortly after physical activity, even when a person has no asthma at rest. Breathing problems typically start within minutes of exertion and usually ease within an hour once activity stops. Doctors commonly manage it with medication taken before exercise and advice on how to warm up and adjust workouts.

diseases.name: Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT)
diseases.summary: This is a slow-growing blood cancer that begins in immune B cells within mucosal linings, most often in the stomach, and is frequently linked to long-standing infection or inflammation. Many affected people have no symptoms early on, and when they do, the signs depend on the organ involved. Care is usually guided by where the tumor sits and whether it is causing problems.

diseases.name: Eye floaters
diseases.summary: Floaters are dark specks or thread-like shapes that drift across the field of view, caused by small clumps forming in the gel inside the eye as it thins with age. They tend to move away when you try to focus on them and show up most against bright plain backgrounds. Most are harmless, but a sudden surge, accompanying light flashes, or a shadow over part of your vision needs urgent eye care because it can signal a retinal tear.

diseases.name: Eye melanoma
diseases.summary: Eye melanoma is a cancer that begins in pigment-producing cells of the eye's middle layer, the uvea, and it often causes no noticeable signs in its early stages. When symptoms do appear, they tend to involve changes in vision or a visible change in the iris or pupil. Because it is usually found during an eye examination or after symptoms emerge, prompt evaluation by an eye doctor matters.

diseases.name: Eyestrain
diseases.summary: Eyestrain happens when the eyes become fatigued from prolonged close work, such as long drives or extended screen time. It typically causes discomfort that eases with rest, though it can occasionally point to an underlying vision problem worth having checked.

diseases.name: Factitious disorder
diseases.summary: This is a psychiatric condition in which a person deliberately fakes, exaggerates, or self-inflicts illness to deceive doctors and others, often without any outside reward. It is considered rare, hard to identify, and can lead to serious injury when the person harms themselves. Professional mental health and medical care is important for safety.

diseases.name: Factor V Leiden
diseases.summary: Factor V Leiden is an inherited genetic change affecting a protein that helps blood clot, which raises the chance of dangerous clots forming in the legs or lungs. Many carriers never have a clot, but those who do typically need blood-thinning medication. Clots can be life-threatening, so symptoms in the leg or chest warrant prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Familial adenomatous polyposis
diseases.summary: This inherited genetic disorder causes hundreds to thousands of growths to form along the large intestine and rectum, usually starting in the teen years and worsening over time. If untreated, it carries a very high chance of bowel cancer at a young age, so early genetic testing and screening matter. Many affected people have no symptoms at first, and signs appear as the growths multiply.

diseases.name: Familial hypercholesterolemia
diseases.summary: This inherited disorder causes very high levels of LDL cholesterol from birth, and many people have no noticeable signs until later in life. Fatty deposits can show up as lumps on tendons or eyelids, and narrowed arteries can eventually cause chest or leg symptoms.

diseases.name: Familial Mediterranean fever
diseases.summary: An inherited inflammatory disorder in which the immune system misfires in repeated bouts, causing short episodes of high temperature along with pain in the belly, chest, or joints. Symptoms usually settle on their own within a few days, but the condition needs long-term medical follow-up because untreated inflammation can damage organs over time.

diseases.name: Farsightedness
diseases.summary: Farsightedness is a very widespread eye condition where faraway things stay sharp while nearby objects look fuzzy. The degree varies, and it is typically present from birth and often runs in families. Glasses, contact lenses, or surgery can correct it.

diseases.name: Fatty liver disease (MASLD)
diseases.summary: A buildup of fat inside the liver, most often linked to excess weight and metabolic conditions like type 2 diabetes. It is the most widespread liver disorder globally. In its milder form it usually causes no noticeable problems, but a more serious inflamed version can progress to scarring of the liver.

diseases.name: Febrile seizure
diseases.summary: A febrile seizure is a convulsion triggered by a rapid rise in body temperature, most often in young children between roughly six months and five years old. It usually happens early in an illness with fever and is typically brief and harmless, though it always warrants a medical check to rule out other causes.

diseases.name: Fecal incontinenceSymptoms and causes
diseases.summary: Fecal incontinence is the inability to control bowel movements, leading to accidental leakage of stool or gas. It ranges from occasional soiling to complete loss of bowel control and often stems from weakened anal muscles, nerve damage, or chronic diarrhea or constipation. It is common, especially in older adults and after childbirth, and is often underreported due to embarrassment.

diseases.name: Female infertility
diseases.summary: Female infertility means being unable to become pregnant after a year of regular unprotected sex, or sooner in women over 35. Most affected women have no obvious warning signs, and when symptoms appear they usually reflect problems with ovulation, the uterus, or the fallopian tubes.

diseases.name: Female sexual dysfunction
diseases.summary: Female sexual dysfunction refers to lasting difficulties with desire, arousal, orgasm, or pain during intercourse that cause distress to a woman or her partner. It can arise at any life stage and is often shaped by a mix of physical, emotional, and relationship factors, so treatment usually combines several approaches.

diseases.name: Fetal alcohol syndrome
diseases.summary: A condition that develops in a baby when the mother drinks alcohol while pregnant, affecting physical growth, facial appearance, and the ability to learn, reason, and manage daily life. The effects are lifelong, though early identification can make a difference in outcomes. No amount of drinking during pregnancy is considered free of risk.

diseases.name: Fetal macrosomia
diseases.summary: Fetal macrosomia means a baby is measurably bigger than expected for its gestational age, either before birth or at delivery. It is usually picked up on routine prenatal measurements or ultrasound rather than through obvious complaints. Many pregnant people notice little beyond the physical effects of a larger baby on the abdomen and surrounding organs.

diseases.name: Fever
diseases.summary: Fever is a temporary rise in body temperature above the normal range, usually a sign that the body is responding to an infection or inflammation. It is a symptom rather than a single disease, and most cases resolve on their own, though high or persistent fevers warrant medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Fibroadenoma
diseases.summary: A fibroadenoma is a benign, solid breast lump that most often appears in younger people and usually produces no discomfort. It typically feels smooth, round, and movable, and it frequently shrinks or disappears on its own over time. Clinicians usually monitor it for changes and only recommend biopsy or removal in certain cases.

diseases.name: Fibrocystic breasts
diseases.summary: Breast tissue can feel lumpy or ropelike and sometimes contains small fluid-filled sacs, which is a normal variation rather than an illness. Discomfort tends to peak before a period and ease once it starts. Most cases need no treatment beyond self-care, but a new or persistent lump or changing pain should be checked by a doctor.

diseases.name: Fibromuscular dysplasia
diseases.summary: A condition where the middle and fibrous layers of medium-sized arteries thicken and narrow, most often affecting vessels supplying the kidneys and brain. Many affected people have no symptoms, and those with symptoms usually notice effects tied to the involved artery, such as high blood pressure or stroke-like signs. It has no cure, but treatment can manage symptoms and reduce complications.

diseases.name: Fibromyalgia
diseases.summary: Fibromyalgia is a long-term condition that causes widespread muscle and bone pain alongside profound tiredness and sleep trouble. It is thought to involve how the nervous system processes pain signals, and it often comes with difficulties in concentration and mood. Diagnosis rests on symptom history and ruling out other causes, since no single test confirms it.

diseases.name: Flatfeet
diseases.summary: Flatfeet is a frequent foot shape in which the inner arch sinks so that much of the sole contacts the ground while standing. It often causes no problems, but it can arise from childhood development, an injury, or later wear on the feet. Pain along the arch or inner ankle is the main reason people seek care.

diseases.name: Floor of the mouth cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that starts in the flat lining cells beneath the tongue, often showing up as a lump or sore that stays put. It can also disturb how the tongue moves and cause pain when swallowing, so anyone with lasting mouth changes should get checked promptly.

diseases.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS)
diseases.summary: This is a kidney disorder in which scarring forms in the tiny filtering units of the kidneys, gradually reducing their ability to clean the blood. Protein leaking into the urine and fluid buildup are the main visible signs. It can progress to kidney failure, so anyone with these changes should see a clinician.

diseases.name: Follicular lymphoma
diseases.summary: This blood cancer is a slow-growing form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that starts in clusters of immune cells within lymph nodes. Many affected people have no noticeable signs for a long time, and it is often discovered only after it has spread to several body areas. Symptoms when they appear tend to be painless lumps plus general body-wide complaints.

diseases.name: Folliculitis
diseases.summary: Folliculitis is an inflammation of hair follicles that usually shows up as small, tender bumps or pustules around hairs, often on areas that get shaved, rubbed, or sweaty. It is most often caused by a bacterial or fungal infection and typically clears up on its own or with simple skin care.

diseases.name: Food allergy
diseases.summary: Food allergy is an overreaction of the immune system to particular foods, and even trace amounts can set it off. Reactions can range from mild skin and stomach symptoms to a dangerous whole-body reaction called anaphylaxis, which needs immediate emergency treatment. Avoiding the trigger food is the main approach, with medicines available to ease symptoms or reduce the impact of accidental exposure.

diseases.name: Food poisoning (foodborne illness)
diseases.summary: A gut infection or toxin picked up from contaminated food or drink. Most cases clear up on their own within a few days, though young children, older adults, pregnant people, and those with weak immune systems can become seriously unwell. Warning signs that need prompt medical attention include persistent vomiting, signs of dehydration, high fever, or any nerve-related changes like vision problems or weakness.

diseases.name: Foot drop
diseases.summary: Foot drop is a sign of an underlying nerve, muscle, or structural problem rather than a condition in itself, and it makes lifting the front of the foot difficult. It can be temporary or lasting, and untreated cases may lead to reduced mobility and ongoing pain. Anyone whose toes keep dragging when walking should see a clinician.

diseases.name: Frontal lobe seizures
diseases.summary: Seizures that start in the front part of the brain can cause unusual movements, vocalizations, and posturing that may look like a psychiatric or sleep problem. They are usually brief, and medication is the first treatment, with surgery or stimulation considered if drugs are not effective. Seeing a clinician is advised for suspected seizure symptoms, while a seizure lasting over five minutes is an emergency.

diseases.name: Frontotemporal dementia
diseases.summary: A group of brain disorders that gradually wear down the front and side regions responsible for personality, conduct, and language. Its earliest signs are often shifts in behavior or speech rather than forgetfulness, and it typically appears in middle age, which can lead to it being mistaken for psychiatric illness or Alzheimer's.

diseases.name: Frostbite
diseases.summary: Frostbite is tissue damage from freezing, most often affecting fingers, toes, ears, cheeks, and the nose. It begins as a mild stage that rewarming usually resolves, but deeper injury can cause lasting harm to skin, muscle, and bone. Anything beyond the mildest stage needs prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Frozen shoulder
diseases.summary: This joint condition causes the tissue around the shoulder to thicken and tighten, leading to pain and stiffness. It tends to build up gradually and usually eases on its own over one to three years. Keeping the arm immobile for long stretches, and certain metabolic or hormonal conditions, raise the chance of getting it.

diseases.name: Fuchs dystrophy
diseases.summary: A slow swelling of the eye's clear front layer leads to hazy sight, especially after waking, along with glare and halos around lights. It usually affects both eyes and tends to worsen over years, often becoming noticeable in middle age. Eye care specialists can manage it, and a transplant may be needed if vision declines a lot.

diseases.name: Functional dyspepsia
diseases.summary: Functional dyspepsia is a long-lasting stomach discomfort with no identifiable structural or medical cause, so it is diagnosed by ruling other problems out. It mirrors ulcer-type symptoms, though no ulcer is found. Symptoms come and go rather than being present constantly.

diseases.name: Functional neurologic disorder/conversion disorder
diseases.summary: Functional neurologic disorder is a condition in which the nervous system works abnormally without a detectable structural lesion, producing real neurological symptoms such as weakness, movement problems, or sensory changes. Symptoms often vary over time and may worsen with stress or fatigue, and diagnosis rests on positive clinical signs rather than the absence of disease. Management typically involves specialist assessment, reassurance, and physiotherapy or psychological therapy.

diseases.name: Galactorrhea
diseases.summary: Milky fluid leaking from the nipples when no baby is being fed is a finding in its own right rather than a standalone illness. It usually points to raised levels of the hormone that drives milk production, and it can be triggered by certain medications, pituitary issues, or breast stimulation. The discharge can affect people of any sex and even infants, and it sometimes resolves without treatment.

diseases.name: Gallbladder cancer
diseases.summary: This cancer starts in the small organ under the liver that stores digestive fluid, and it is uncommon overall. It is often silent early, so it is usually found after it has spread past the organ, when outlook is poorer. Women, older adults, and people with a history of gallstones face higher risk.

diseases.name: Gallstones
diseases.summary: Gallstones are hard deposits that form in the gallbladder from cholesterol or bilirubin. Many people with them have no symptoms, but when a stone blocks the bile ducts it can cause sharp pain in the upper right abdomen, often after fatty meals. Complications such as infection or pancreatitis are possible and need prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Ganglioglioma
diseases.summary: A slow-growing, usually noncancerous growth made of nerve and supporting cells, most often found in the temporal lobe of the brain. It is frequently first noticed because of seizures, and it is seen mainly in children and young adults. Complete surgical removal often leads to a good long-term outlook.

diseases.name: Ganglion cyst
diseases.summary: This is a small fluid-filled bump that usually forms over joints or tendons, most often in the wrist and hand. It tends to change size, sometimes shrinking on its own, and it is typically painless unless it presses on a nearby nerve. It is benign and treated only if it causes trouble.

diseases.name: Gangrene
diseases.summary: Gangrene is the death of body tissue, usually because blood supply has been cut off or severely reduced. It most often affects fingers, toes, feet, or limbs and can spread quickly if untreated. Prompt medical attention is needed because the affected tissue can become infected and threaten life.

diseases.name: Gas and gas pains
diseases.summary: Intestinal gas is air and gases produced during digestion that build up in the stomach and bowel. Most people experience it daily, and it usually causes swelling, discomfort, and release through burping or passing wind.

diseases.name: Gastritis
diseases.summary: Gastritis is swelling of the stomach's inner lining that can start abruptly or build slowly over months or years. Bacterial infection and frequent use of common pain relievers are the usual triggers, and some people never notice any symptoms. Most cases are mild and clear up with treatment, though untreated or long-lasting inflammation can occasionally lead to ulcers.

diseases.name: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
diseases.summary: A long-running condition in which stomach contents, mainly acid, repeatedly move upward into the food pipe and irritate its lining. Many people have occasional reflux, but when it keeps happening it is classed as this disease. Lifestyle adjustments and medication help most people, and surgery is an option for a small number.

diseases.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
diseases.summary: Bleeding somewhere along the digestive tract can show up as blood in vomit or stool, or as dark, tar-like stool, and it is not always visible to the naked eye. How much it affects a person depends on how fast it is happening and where it starts. Doctors can usually find the source with imaging or an endoscopic exam.

diseases.name: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST)
diseases.summary: A slow-growing cancer arising from specialized cells in the wall of the digestive tract, most often found in the stomach or small bowel. Many affected people have no symptoms early on, and when signs do appear they tend to be vague digestive complaints. It is most often diagnosed in adults and is very unusual in children.

diseases.name: Gastroparesis
diseases.summary: Gastroparesis is a long-term condition in which the stomach's muscles move food through too slowly, so it empties poorly and digestion suffers. It is often unexplained, though it can follow diabetes, surgery, or a viral illness. Although there is no cure, medication and dietary changes can often ease the discomfort.

diseases.name: Gaucher disease
diseases.summary: A rare inherited disorder in which a fatty substance accumulates in organs such as the spleen, liver, and bones, gradually damaging them. Its most common form, type 1, is seen more often in people of Ashkenazi Jewish descent and can show up at any age, though it usually surfaces in childhood or the teen years. Rarer forms also affect the brain and breathing.

diseases.name: Gender dysphoria
diseases.summary: This condition involves significant unease arising from a mismatch between a person's internal sense of gender and the sex recorded for them at birth. It is distinct from simply identifying with a gender or from not conforming to typical gender roles. Signs can begin in childhood, emerge at puberty, or appear later in life, and they may fade and return over time, sometimes surfacing as anxiety, low mood, or problems at school or socially.

diseases.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
diseases.summary: Generalized anxiety disorder involves persistent, hard-to-control worry about many areas of life, out of step with what is actually happening. It often brings restlessness, tiredness, and physical tension, and it can be managed well with talk therapy, medication, and lifestyle changes.

diseases.name: Genital herpes
diseases.summary: Genital herpes is a widespread infection caused by the herpes simplex virus, passed mainly through skin contact during intimate activity. Many carriers feel nothing at all, yet they can still transmit it. Although it cannot be cured, antiviral medication eases outbreaks and lowers the chance of passing it to others.

diseases.name: Genital warts
diseases.summary: A very widespread viral infection passed through sexual contact, caused by certain strains of human papillomavirus. It produces soft, flesh-toned growths in the genital or nearby areas, which can be tiny and hard to notice or grow into a cauliflower-like cluster. Most sexually active people will be exposed at some point, and vaccination lowers the chance of catching the strains that cause these growths.

diseases.name: Geographic atrophy
diseases.summary: A progressive eye disorder that develops in people who already have age-related macular degeneration, where light-sensing cells in the central back of the eye die off and create expanding patches. Vision in the center gradually fades while the outer field typically remains intact. It mostly affects older adults and has no cure, though some newer drugs can slow its course.

diseases.name: Geographic tongue
diseases.summary: A harmless, non-contagious inflammation of the tongue's surface in which small bumps temporarily disappear, leaving shifting smooth, reddish areas. Many affected people feel nothing at all, while others notice mild soreness or sensitivity when eating spicy, acidic, or salty foods. It tends to come and go over days to years and usually resolves without treatment.

diseases.name: Germ cell tumors
diseases.summary: This is a group of uncommon, mostly young-onset growths that start in reproductive cells and usually appear in the testicles or ovaries, though they can rarely form elsewhere in the body. Their symptoms largely reflect pressure on nearby tissue, with a testicular lump being a hallmark sign. Many are not cancerous, and treatment can involve surgery, chemotherapy, or radiation.

diseases.name: Gestational diabetes
diseases.summary: Gestational diabetes is a form of high blood sugar first recognized during pregnancy, usually in the second or third trimester, that typically resolves after delivery. Most affected people feel few or no symptoms, so it is often found through routine screening. When symptoms do occur, they tend to be mild and similar to those of normal pregnancy.

diseases.name: Giant cell arteritis
diseases.summary: This is a disorder in which the walls of certain blood vessels become inflamed, most often those running across the temples on the sides of the head. It mainly affects adults over fifty and can threaten eyesight if left untreated. Prompt steroid treatment usually controls it, but symptoms can flare again, so ongoing follow-up with a clinician is needed.

diseases.name: Giardia infection (giardiasis)
diseases.summary: Giardiasis is an intestinal infection caused by a microscopic parasite that is picked up through contaminated water, food, or contact with infected people or animals. It typically produces watery, greasy-looking diarrhea along with bloating, gas, and cramping, and symptoms can linger for weeks. Most people recover fully, though the illness can lead to dehydration and weight loss if it persists.

diseases.name: Gilbert syndrome
diseases.summary: This is a harmless, inherited condition in which the liver processes a waste pigment less efficiently than usual, so levels rise mildly from time to time. Most people never notice it, but those who do may see brief yellowing that tends to flare with fasting, stress, illness, or dehydration. It generally needs reassurance rather than treatment.

diseases.name: Gingivitis
diseases.summary: Gum inflammation that is very widespread and usually reversible with better daily mouth care. Left alone it can progress to a more serious gum disease that threatens teeth, so an early dental visit matters. Warning signs are tender, reddish gums that bleed easily during brushing or flossing.

diseases.name: Glaucoma
diseases.summary: Glaucoma is a group of eye disorders in which pressure or poor drainage inside the eye gradually injures the optic nerve, which can eventually lead to lost vision. Many types cause no noticeable warning in the early stages, so routine eye checks are how it is usually caught. Acute angle-closure is a sudden, painful form that needs emergency eye care right away.

diseases.name: Glioblastoma
diseases.summary: This is a fast-growing malignant tumor arising from supportive cells in the brain or spinal cord, and it is the most frequent aggressive primary brain cancer in adults. Its symptoms depend on which area of the brain is affected and often include headaches, changes in thinking or personality, seizures, and problems with movement, speech, or vision. Surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy can slow its progression and extend life, but they cannot cure it.

diseases.name: Glioma
diseases.summary: Gliomas are tumors that develop from the brain's support cells, and they can also appear in the spinal cord. Some grow slowly, while others are aggressive and spread into surrounding tissue. The symptoms people notice depend on which area is pressed or damaged, and often include headaches, seizures, and changes in thinking, vision, or speech.

diseases.name: Glomerulonephritis
diseases.summary: Glomerulonephritis is a condition in which the kidney's tiny filtering units become inflamed and damaged, so they cannot clean the blood properly. It can start suddenly or develop slowly over time, and it may occur alone or alongside disease affecting other organs. Because it can progress to lasting kidney harm, prompt medical evaluation is advised.

diseases.name: Goiter
diseases.summary: A goiter is an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid, the butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck. Many goiters cause no discomfort, but a large one can press on the windpipe and food tube, making swallowing or breathing harder. Iodine shortage, autoimmune thyroid disease, and nodules are common reasons it develops.

diseases.name: Golfer's elbow (Medial epicondylitis)
diseases.summary: An inflammation of the tendons on the inner elbow, where forearm muscles anchor to bone, causes ache and tenderness there that can travel toward the wrist. Repetitive gripping and wrist motions, not only sports, tend to bring it on, and it usually settles with rest and adjusted activity. Warning signs such as a hot, swollen elbow with fever, or an elbow that cannot bend, need prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Gonorrhea
diseases.summary: Gonorrhea is a bacterial infection passed mainly through genital, oral, or anal sex, and it often causes no noticeable signs. When symptoms do appear, they usually involve the genitals or urinary tract, though the rectum, throat, eyes, and joints can also be affected. Prompt testing and treatment are important because untreated infection can spread to partners and cause complications.

diseases.name: Gout
diseases.summary: A very common inflammatory arthritis caused by excess uric acid crystals settling in joints, typically producing abrupt, painful flares that peak within hours. Attacks often strike at night and usually affect the big toe first, though other joints can be involved. Prompt medical evaluation is advised for sudden severe joint pain, and infection must be ruled out if fever accompanies a hot, swollen joint.

diseases.name: Granuloma annulare
diseases.summary: This is a harmless skin disorder in which firm, raised spots arrange themselves into circles, most often on the fingers, toes, and lower limbs of younger adults. It usually causes little pain and cannot pass between people, though it often recurs and can persist for years without treatment. Because it is occasionally linked to diabetes or thyroid problems, a doctor should evaluate it if it lingers beyond a few weeks.

diseases.name: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
diseases.summary: This is a rare autoimmune disorder in which small blood vessels become inflamed, most often affecting the sinuses, airways, lungs, and kidneys, though any organ can be involved. It typically begins with cold-like or general illness signs and can progress quickly to organ damage if not treated. It usually appears between ages 40 and 65, and early diagnosis and treatment greatly improve outcomes.

diseases.name: Granulosa cell tumor
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon, slow-growing cancer of the ovary's support cells. Many are caught before they spread, so outlook is often good when detected early. Its signs come from the tumor's mass and from hormones it produces, which can disrupt periods and breast tissue.

diseases.name: Graves' disease
diseases.summary: This autoimmune disorder overstimulates the thyroid, so the gland pumps out more hormone than the body needs and speeds up many systems. Because that hormone reaches nearly every organ, the effects can extend to the eyes and skin as well as the heart and digestion. It is seen more often in women and in adults over 30.

diseases.name: Group B strep disease
diseases.summary: Group B streptococcus is a bacterium that usually lives harmlessly in the gut and genital tract but can invade the bloodstream and cause serious infections of the lungs, urinary tract, skin, joints, and brain. It is most dangerous for newborns, pregnant people, older adults, and people with diabetes or weakened immune systems. Because these infections can progress quickly to sepsis, new fever or unusual drowsiness in a newborn needs immediate medical attention.

diseases.name: Growing pains
diseases.summary: Growing pains are a common, harmless cause of aching in the legs in young children, usually between about ages 3 and 12. The discomfort tends to appear later in the day or overnight, and children are typically fine by morning with normal activity. Doctors generally diagnose it by ruling out joint, muscle, or other problems, since the exam is normal.

diseases.name: Growth plate fractures
diseases.summary: A break that runs through the soft, actively growing tissue at the end of a child's long bone. Because this area controls future bone length and straightness, the injury needs prompt medical assessment even when it looks minor. Most cases heal well when treated correctly, though the bone can grow unevenly if the injury is missed or handled poorly.

diseases.name: Guillain-Barre syndrome
diseases.summary: A rare immune-mediated disorder in which the body's defenses damage the nerves outside the brain and spinal cord, interrupting signals to muscles. It typically starts with tingling and weakness in the lower limbs that can climb upward and sometimes reach the face and breathing muscles. Because it can worsen quickly, it is treated as a hospital-level emergency, and most people recover, though slowly.

diseases.name: H1N1 flu (swine flu)
diseases.summary: Swine flu is an influenza A infection caused by the H1N1 virus, which first spread widely among people in 2009 and now circulates as part of routine seasonal flu. Most otherwise healthy people recover on their own, but it can become dangerous for young children, older adults, pregnant people, and those with long-term illnesses.

diseases.name: Hair loss
diseases.summary: Hair thinning or bald patches can develop gradually from genetics and aging or come on suddenly from stress, medical conditions, or hair-pulling styles. Most types are not dangerous, but sudden or patchy loss should be checked by a doctor because it can point to an underlying problem.

diseases.name: Hairy cell leukemia
diseases.summary: This blood cancer involves an overproduction of abnormal B lymphocytes that take on a fuzzy, hair-like look under the microscope. It often progresses slowly and may go unnoticed until a routine blood test reveals it. It is most often diagnosed in older men, and treatment is typically given only when symptoms appear or blood counts drop.

diseases.name: Hammertoe and mallet toe
diseases.summary: This foot problem makes one or more toes buckle at a joint, so they stay bent instead of lying flat. Tight or ill-fitting shoes are a common trigger, while injury, diabetes, arthritis, and family history can also play a part. Changing footwear or using inserts often eases discomfort, and surgery is considered when those steps fail.

diseases.name: Hamstring injury
diseases.summary: A pulled or torn muscle at the back of the thigh usually causes a sudden, sharp jolt of pain, often with a popping feeling, followed by swelling and bruising within hours. Most mild cases settle with rest, ice and pain relief, but being unable to put weight on the leg or walk more than a few steps warrants prompt medical assessment. Athletes who sprint, stop suddenly or stretch extremely are the most frequently affected.

diseases.name: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease
diseases.summary: A viral infection, most often in young children, that causes fever and a sore mouth followed by a rash with blister-like spots on the hands, feet, and sometimes the buttocks. It spreads easily through close contact and respiratory droplets, and usually resolves on its own within about a week or two. Care focuses on comfort, hydration, and watching for dehydration.

diseases.name: Hangovers
diseases.summary: A hangover is a cluster of unpleasant effects that follow heavy drinking, typically peaking the morning after. It usually resolves by itself within a day, though repeated episodes can signal a drinking problem worth discussing with a clinician.

diseases.name: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
diseases.summary: A rare, serious lung infection caused by inhaling particles from rodent droppings or urine. It starts with flu-like illness and can progress within days to fluid in the lungs and breathing failure. Prompt hospital evaluation is needed because the condition can worsen quickly.

diseases.name: Hashimoto's disease
diseases.summary: Hashimoto's disease is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system gradually attacks the thyroid gland, reducing its hormone output. Because the thyroid regulates metabolism, the resulting underactivity tends to produce slowly developing, general symptoms. It is typically managed with lifelong daily thyroid hormone replacement.

diseases.name: Hay fever
diseases.summary: Hay fever is an immune overreaction to harmless airborne substances such as pollen, dust mites, or pet dander, producing cold-like nasal and eye symptoms without any infection. Symptoms can be seasonal or year-round, and they often respond well to avoidance measures and medication. People with asthma, eczema, or a family history of allergies are more likely to develop it.

diseases.name: Head and neck cancers
diseases.summary: This is an umbrella group of cancers that develop in the upper airway, mouth, nasal passages, and salivary glands, most often in the surface cells lining those areas. Warning signs depend on the exact location, but a lasting mouth sore, a neck lump, or pain on swallowing are among the most typical. Smoking, heavy drinking, and certain viral infections increase the chance of developing these cancers, and treatment is planned around the tumor's site, size, and cell type.

diseases.name: Head lice
diseases.summary: A tiny insect that lives on the scalp and feeds on small amounts of blood, spreading mainly through close head-to-head contact. The most noticeable sign is an itchy scalp, and people often spot the insects or their attached eggs in the hair near the scalp. Treatment usually involves lice-specific products and fine-toothed combing.

diseases.name: Headaches in children
diseases.summary: Pain in the head is one of the most frequent complaints in school-age children and teens, and most episodes come from tension-type pain or migraine rather than a serious illness. Many children also feel sick to their stomach, are bothered by bright light, or feel tired along with the pain. Persistent, worsening, or unusual headaches still warrant a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Hearing loss
diseases.summary: Hearing that declines gradually is widespread, especially among older adults, and is often linked to aging or long-term exposure to loud sound. It usually cannot be reversed, but hearing aids and other tools can make sounds easier to follow. A sudden drop in hearing, especially in one ear, needs prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Heart arrhythmia
diseases.summary: Heart rhythm disorders cause the heart to beat too fast, too slow, or in an uneven pattern, and some are harmless while others are dangerous. Many people notice a racing or fluttering sensation in the chest, but some have no symptoms at all and the problem is found during a routine checkup. Anyone with chest pain, trouble breathing, or fainting needs emergency care.

diseases.name: Heart attack
diseases.summary: A heart attack occurs when the heart muscle is starved of oxygen-rich blood, most often because a coronary artery suddenly becomes blocked, and tissue begins to die if flow is not restored quickly. It often shows up as pressure or discomfort in the chest that can radiate into the arm, jaw, or back, frequently with breathlessness, sweating, or nausea. Because heart muscle is lost within minutes to hours, anyone suspecting one needs emergency care immediately.

diseases.name: Heart disease
diseases.summary: Heart disease is an umbrella term for several problems affecting the heart, including narrowed coronary arteries, irregular rhythms, congenital defects, muscle disorders, and valve issues. Many forms can be prevented or managed through lifestyle habits and medical care. Warning signs vary by type, but chest discomfort, breathlessness, and fainting are the most important to act on quickly.

diseases.name: Heart failure
diseases.summary: The heart's pumping ability weakens, so blood and fluid back up into the lungs and lower body. This commonly leads to breathlessness, tiredness, and swelling in the legs, and it can become life-threatening when it progresses. Treatment and lifestyle changes can ease symptoms and support a better quality of life.

diseases.name: Heart murmurs
diseases.summary: A heart murmur is an additional sound picked up with a stethoscope, produced when blood flows turbulently through or across a heart valve or chamber. Many murmurs are harmless and cause no complaints, while others can signal valve disease or a structural problem that places extra strain on the heart. A clinician usually sorts out which type is present, often with an ultrasound of the heart.

diseases.name: Heart palpitations
diseases.summary: Heart palpitations are sensations of a racing, pounding, fluttering, or irregular heartbeat that people notice in the chest or neck. They are usually harmless and often triggered by caffeine, stress, or fatigue, but they can occasionally signal a rhythm problem that needs evaluation.

diseases.name: Heart valve disease
diseases.summary: Many people with this condition have no noticeable signs for years, and symptoms that do appear often reflect strain on the heart and reduced circulation. The condition arises when a heart valve fails to open fully or to shut tightly, which disturbs normal blood flow. Medical evaluation is advised for anyone noticing these warning signs, and treatment depends on the affected valve and how advanced the problem is.

diseases.name: Heartburn
diseases.summary: Heartburn is a burning discomfort behind the breastbone caused by stomach acid rising into the gullet, often after meals or when lying down. It is very common and usually manageable with lifestyle changes or over-the-counter medicines, though persistent symptoms should be checked by a doctor.

diseases.name: Heat exhaustion
diseases.summary: Heat exhaustion is the middle stage of heat-related illness, occurring when the body becomes too hot, often after hard exercise or time spent in warm, humid conditions. It is treatable if caught early, but it can progress to a dangerous heatstroke without prompt cooling and rest.

diseases.name: Heat rash
diseases.summary: Heat rash is a skin irritation that forms when sweat gets trapped under the skin because the sweat ducts are blocked, typically in hot or humid conditions. It usually appears as clusters of tiny bumps or blisters and tends to fade on its own once the skin cools and stays dry. It is seen most often in infants and in people who sweat heavily or spend long periods in warm places.

diseases.name: Heatstroke
diseases.summary: Heatstroke is the most severe form of heat-related illness, where the body's internal temperature climbs dangerously high, usually from hot surroundings or long periods of hard exercise in the heat. Without rapid treatment it can injure the brain, heart, kidneys, and muscles, and the risk of lasting harm or death rises with every delay.

diseases.name: Heavy menstrual bleeding
diseases.summary: Periods that bring on far more blood than usual, or that drag on for many days, can make daily life hard and leave a person worn out. It happens most often when an egg isn't released in a cycle, which lowers progesterone, or when the uterus has growths such as fibroids or polyps. Anyone whose bleeding soaks through protection every hour or who notices bleeding between periods should contact a clinician.

diseases.name: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection
diseases.summary: A bacterial infection that colonizes the stomach lining and can irritate it over time. Many people carry it without noticing anything, while others develop upper digestive discomfort, and in some cases ulcers that can bleed.

diseases.name: Hemangioblastoma
diseases.summary: A hemangioblastoma is a slow-growing, noncancerous tumor of the blood-vessel-forming cells in the brain, spinal cord, or retina. Its symptoms depend on where it develops and whether the tumor or its fluid-filled cysts press on nearby nerve tissue. It is most often linked to the inherited von Hippel-Lindau disease, though many cases occur with no known cause.

diseases.name: Hemangioma
diseases.summary: A benign vascular birthmark that usually shows up in the first weeks of life and is typically harmless. Most of these marks fade on their own over the first decade, so treatment is needed only when they interfere with vision, breathing, or other vital functions, or sit in a cosmetically sensitive spot.

diseases.name: Hemifacial spasm
diseases.summary: A nerve-related movement disorder in which twitching or involuntary contractions affect the muscles on one side of the face, typically starting around the eye. The episodes can spread over time and are not dangerous, though they can be bothersome and socially awkward. A blood vessel pressing on the facial nerve is the usual underlying cause.

symptoms.name: spasms on both sides of face

diseases.name: Hemochromatosis
diseases.summary: Hemochromatosis is an inherited disorder in which the gut absorbs more iron than the body needs, and the surplus accumulates in organs such as the liver, heart, and pancreas. Many people never notice symptoms, and when they do, the early signs are vague and easily mistaken for other conditions. Left untreated, the iron buildup can progress to liver disease, heart problems, and diabetes.

diseases.name: Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS)
diseases.summary: This is a serious blood-clotting disorder in which tiny vessels become inflamed and clots form throughout the body, often injuring the kidneys. It most often follows a gut infection with a particular strain of E. coli and strikes mainly young children. With prompt treatment, most people, especially children, recover fully.

diseases.name: Hemophilia
diseases.summary: Hemophilia is an inherited condition in which the blood cannot form clots well because of a shortage of specific clotting proteins. Bleeding can be prolonged after injuries or procedures, and the most dangerous complication is bleeding inside the body, especially into the brain. It is treated mainly by replacing the missing clotting factor, with newer non-factor therapies also available.

diseases.name: Hemorrhoids
diseases.summary: Hemorrhoids are clusters of enlarged blood vessels in the anal canal and lower rectum that can sit inside or just under the skin near the anus. They are often linked to straining, pregnancy, and aging, and most cases improve with self-care. Bleeding or persistent symptoms still warrant a medical check to rule out more serious causes.

diseases.name: Henoch-Schonlein purpura
diseases.summary: An immune-driven inflammation of tiny blood vessels that mostly affects children and often follows an infection. It typically causes a purple rash on the legs and buttocks along with joint pain, stomach pain, and sometimes kidney involvement. Most cases resolve on their own, but kidney and bowel complications need medical assessment.

diseases.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
diseases.summary: A condition in which a failing liver lets toxins, especially ammonia, build up in the blood and disturb brain function. It can progress from attention and sleep problems to confusion and coma if not treated promptly. It is most often linked to advanced liver scarring, though acute liver failure, portal blood flow bypassing the liver, alcohol use, and certain medicines can also trigger it.

diseases.name: Hepatitis A
diseases.summary: This liver infection spreads mainly through contaminated food or water and close contact with an infected person. Many people who catch it have no symptoms, and those who do usually recover fully within weeks to months. Prevention relies on handwashing and vaccination.

diseases.name: Hepatitis B
diseases.summary: A viral infection of the liver that most adults clear fully, though in some people it lingers for years and can lead to scarring, liver failure, or cancer. Early signs often appear weeks to months after exposure, and some people, especially young children, have no noticeable symptoms. A vaccine offers reliable prevention, and prompt treatment after exposure can lower the chance of infection.

diseases.name: Hepatitis C
diseases.summary: Hepatitis C is a long-lasting viral infection that inflames and can gradually scar the liver, and it spreads through contact with infected blood. Many people carry it for years without noticing anything, so screening is recommended for most adults. Modern antiviral drugs cure the infection in most cases.

diseases.name: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
diseases.summary: This cancer starts in the liver's main cell type and most often develops in people already living with long-term liver scarring from hepatitis B or C. It usually causes no early warning signs, so it is often found through screening or only after it has advanced. People with a known risk who notice unexplained changes should be seen by a clinician promptly.

diseases.name: Hepatopulmonary syndrome
diseases.summary: Liver disease that has become advanced can cause tiny lung blood vessels to widen, so less oxygen passes from the lungs into the blood. Breathlessness is typically the first sign, often worse upright and easing when lying down. Liver transplantation is the only treatment that reverses the lung problem, while oxygen can partly help in the meantime.

diseases.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
diseases.summary: A genetic disorder that runs in families, where abnormal direct connections form between arteries and veins in places like the skin, nose, gut, lungs, brain, and liver. These fragile connections can grow over time and bleed, and the degree of illness varies widely even among relatives. Frequent nosebleeds and small red spots on the skin are typical early signs.

diseases.name: Herniated disk
diseases.summary: A slipped or ruptured spinal disk occurs when the soft inner core of a cushion between vertebrae pushes through a tear in its tougher outer shell. Most often in the lower back and less often in the neck, it tends to irritate a nearby nerve, producing pain, tingling or weakness usually on one side of the body. Many people with this problem have no symptoms at all.

diseases.name: Hiatal hernia
diseases.summary: A hiatal hernia happens when part of the stomach pushes upward through the muscular opening in the diaphragm into the chest. Small ones often go unnoticed, while larger ones can let stomach contents rise into the food pipe and cause reflux-type discomfort. Most people are managed with lifestyle changes or medication, and surgery is reserved for very large cases.

diseases.name: Hiccups
diseases.summary: Hiccups are involuntary contractions of the muscle under the lungs that briefly snap the voice box shut, producing a distinctive sound. Most episodes fade within minutes and are often set off by large meals, fizzy or alcoholic drinks, or sudden strong emotion. Episodes lasting longer than two days, or ones that interfere with eating, sleep, or breathing, call for a medical visit.

diseases.name: Hidradenitis suppurativa
diseases.summary: A long-lasting skin disorder that forms pus-filled bumps in folds and friction-prone areas, usually beginning in early adulthood. Over time the bumps can return, connect into underground channels, and leave scars. Seeing a skin specialist early helps control flares and limit lasting damage.

diseases.name: High blood pressure (hypertension)
diseases.summary: Raised blood pressure usually causes no noticeable signs for years, which is why it is often found during routine checks. When it is very high or has caused damage, it can bring on headaches, vision changes, chest discomfort, or shortness of breath. Because it quietly strains the heart, vessels, and kidneys, regular measurement is the main way to catch it early.

diseases.name: High blood pressure in children
diseases.summary: Childhood hypertension means blood pressure readings stay above the normal range for a child's age, sex, and height. It is often found incidentally during routine checkups because it frequently causes no obvious signs. When symptoms do occur, they tend to be vague, and severe cases can produce headaches or vision changes.

diseases.name: High cholesterol
diseases.summary: Elevated fat-like particles in the bloodstream can gradually build up inside arteries, narrowing them and raising the chance of heart attack or stroke. The condition usually produces no warning signs, so a blood test is the only reliable way to detect it. Diet, activity, weight, smoking, and alcohol all influence it, and it can also run in families.

diseases.name: Hilar cholangiocarcinoma
diseases.summary: This cancer begins in the cells lining the point where the two main channels leaving the liver merge, interrupting the flow of digestive fluid. Because it often grows quietly, early signs are subtle, and blockage usually shows up as yellowing, itching, or changes in urine and stool color. It is the most common form of bile duct cancer yet still uncommon overall.

diseases.name: Hip dysplasia
diseases.summary: Hip dysplasia is a condition in which the hip socket does not fully cover the ball of the thighbone, so the joint can partly or fully slip out of place. It is usually present from birth, and early detection often allows a simple brace to correct it. If it goes unnoticed, it can later cause wear, cartilage injury, and groin pain in adolescence or adulthood.

diseases.name: Hip fracture
diseases.summary: A hip fracture is a break in the upper end of the thigh bone, usually after a fall, and it most often affects older adults with weaker bones. People typically feel intense pain in the groin or hip that makes it very hard to bear weight or walk. The leg often looks shorter or turned outward, and this needs urgent medical assessment.

diseases.name: Hip labral tear
diseases.summary: A hip labral tear is an injury to the ring of cartilage that lines the rim of the hip socket. It often causes pain in the groin or front of the hip, along with catching, clicking, or a sense of instability, and is frequently linked to repetitive hip motion or structural hip shape differences.

diseases.name: Hirschsprung's disease
diseases.summary: Hirschsprung's disease is a birth defect in which nerve cells are missing from the lower part of the bowel, so stool cannot move through normally. Infants usually show signs in the first days or weeks of life, with failure to pass the first stool and swelling of the belly being typical. Without treatment it can lead to a dangerous bowel infection, so it needs prompt surgical care.

diseases.name: Hirsutism
diseases.summary: Hirsutism is excess coarse, dark hair growth in areas where hair is typically minimal or absent in women, such as the face, chest, abdomen, and back. It is usually caused by higher-than-normal levels of androgens or increased sensitivity of hair follicles to them. The condition is common and is often linked to hormonal disorders such as polycystic ovary syndrome.

diseases.name: Histoplasmosis
diseases.summary: A fungal lung infection caught by breathing in spores that grow in soil enriched with bird or bat droppings. Many people have no symptoms or only a flu-like illness that clears on its own, while a minority develop a more serious spread to other organs.

diseases.name: HIV/AIDS
diseases.summary: HIV is a virus that gradually weakens the immune system, and without treatment it can progress to AIDS. Early on, many people feel flu-like, and later the body struggles to fight off infections. Modern medicine keeps the virus under control in most people, so the infection rarely advances to AIDS.

diseases.name: Hives and angioedema
diseases.summary: Hives are itchy, raised welts on the skin that are usually brief and harmless, while angioedema is a deeper swelling that often shows up around the face and lips. Both are usually treated with antihistamines and tend to resolve on their own, though swelling of the throat or tongue can block the airway and needs emergency care.

diseases.name: Hoarding disorder
diseases.summary: This mental health condition causes a person to hold onto belongings compulsively, even when they have little value, until living areas fill up and become hard to move through or use. People often feel strong attachment to their things and may not recognize the situation as a problem. It typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood and tends to worsen with age.

diseases.name: Hodgkin lymphoma (Hodgkin disease)
diseases.summary: A cancer of the lymph system's white blood cells that often shows up first as painless swelling in the neck, armpits, or groin. It mainly affects young adults and people over 65, and it responds well to treatment, with many cases curable.

diseases.name: Horner syndrome
diseases.summary: Horner syndrome is a nerve disruption on one side of the face caused by an interruption in the sympathetic nerve pathway to the eye. It typically shows up as drooping of the upper eyelid together with a smaller pupil on the affected side. Its signs can point to problems in the neck, chest, or brain that need prompt investigation.

diseases.name: Hot flashes
diseases.summary: Hot flashes are sudden waves of heat that spread over the upper body and face, often with reddening of the skin and sweating. They are most often linked to hormonal shifts, especially during menopause or perimenopause. They are common, usually harmless, and can be eased with lifestyle changes or treatment when they are disruptive.

diseases.name: HPV infection
diseases.summary: Human papillomavirus is a very widespread virus spread through skin-to-skin and sexual contact. Most people who carry it never notice any signs and clear it on their own, often within a couple of years. When symptoms do occur, they are usually wart-like growths on the skin or genitals, and in rare cases changes in the voice or throat.

diseases.name: Huntington's disease
diseases.summary: A hereditary brain disorder that gradually impairs movement, thinking, and emotional health, most often becoming noticeable in middle adulthood. Each child of an affected parent has an even chance of inheriting the responsible gene. Medications can ease some symptoms, but they cannot stop the progressive decline.

diseases.name: Hurthle cell cancer
diseases.summary: A Hurthle cell cancer is a less common, cell-type variant of follicular thyroid cancer that arises from the thyroid gland in the front of the neck. It often shows up as a lump in the neck that may grow and can sometimes spread to nearby lymph nodes or the lungs.

diseases.name: Hydrocele
diseases.summary: A hydrocele is a fluid-filled enlargement around a testicle that makes the scrotum look swollen. It is usually present from birth and frequently disappears during infancy, while in older males it can follow an injury, inflammation, or infection. It is typically painless and harmless, but a medical check is still needed to rule out more serious causes.

diseases.name: Hydrocephalus
diseases.summary: Hydrocephalus is a condition where excess fluid collects in the brain's internal chambers, enlarging them and raising pressure that can injure brain tissue. Its signs differ with age, ranging from a swollen head in babies to memory, walking, and bladder problems in older adults. Some infant symptoms, such as seizures or repeated vomiting, require emergency care.

diseases.name: Hydronephrosis
diseases.summary: A condition where urine backs up into one or both kidneys because it cannot drain properly, usually from a blockage in the urinary tract or a birth difference. Many people have no noticeable signs, but when they do, pain, urinary changes, and general illness are the typical complaints. Long-standing cases can damage the kidney, so timely evaluation matters.

diseases.name: Hypercalcemia
diseases.summary: Excess calcium in the blood often arises when the parathyroid glands overproduce their hormone, though cancer, some medications, and high calcium or vitamin D supplements can also be responsible. Many people have no noticeable signs when the elevation is mild, while more significant cases can affect the kidneys, digestion, bones, muscles, brain, and heart. Seeing a doctor promptly is advisable if thirst, frequent urination, or stomach pain develops.

diseases.name: Hypereosinophilic syndrome
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon blood disorder in which a persistent surplus of one kind of immune cell injures tissues such as the skin, lungs, gut, heart, or nerves. Which symptoms appear depends on which organs are affected. Treatment can target an underlying trigger when one exists and may also use medicines that bring the cell count down.

diseases.name: Hyperglycemia in diabetes
diseases.summary: When blood sugar runs higher than target in someone with diabetes, the body tries to flush out the extra glucose through urine, which leads to thirst and frequent bathroom trips. Over time, the excess sugar can also cause tiredness and blurred vision. Very high levels need prompt medical attention because they can lead to dangerous complications.

diseases.name: Hyperhidrosis
diseases.summary: Hyperhidrosis is a condition in which a person sweats far more than their surroundings, activity, or emotions would explain, sometimes enough to soak clothing or drip from the hands. It often disrupts daily life and can lead to embarrassment or social withdrawal. Treatment typically starts with stronger antiperspirants and can progress to medications, therapies, or surgery when needed.

diseases.name: Hyperoxaluria and oxalosis
diseases.summary: A condition where the urine carries too much of a naturally occurring chemical, usually from a gene change, an intestinal disorder, or a high-oxalate diet, and it often first shows up as a kidney stone. If the kidneys decline and oxalate builds up in the blood, it can deposit in blood vessels, bones, and organs, a state called oxalosis. Early detection and prompt treatment are important for protecting kidney health.

diseases.name: Hyperparathyroidism
diseases.summary: Hyperparathyroidism happens when one or more parathyroid glands make too much parathyroid hormone, which raises calcium in the blood and can weaken bones and strain the kidneys. Many people have few or no symptoms at first and the condition is often found on routine blood tests. When symptoms do appear, they tend to be vague and involve the bones, kidneys, digestive system, and mood.

diseases.name: Hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid)
diseases.summary: An overactive thyroid makes more hormone than the body needs, which speeds up metabolism and can cause unplanned weight loss, a racing or irregular heartbeat, and jitteriness. Symptoms can be easy to miss or mistake for other problems, especially in older adults. Treatment options include medications, radioactive iodine, or surgery, and some cases resolve on their own.

diseases.name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
diseases.summary: A genetic thickening of the heart muscle, most often in the wall between the heart's chambers, can make it harder for the heart to pump. Many carriers never notice anything, while a minority develop breathing trouble, chest discomfort, or fainting, and some are at risk of dangerous rhythm problems. Because it runs in families, relatives are typically advised to get screened.

diseases.name: Hypoglycemia
diseases.summary: Low blood sugar can cause a range of symptoms, from shakiness and sweating to confusion and, when severe, fainting or seizures. It is most often linked to diabetes treatment, though it can also occur in people without diabetes due to certain medicines, skipped meals, heavy drinking, or other medical conditions. Prompt intake of fast-acting sugar is the usual first step, and medical help is needed if symptoms persist or recur.

diseases.name: Hyponatremia
diseases.summary: Hyponatremia means the sodium concentration in the blood has dropped below normal, usually because the blood has been diluted by excess water or by an underlying illness. As water shifts into cells, they can swell, which may affect the brain and other organs. Mild cases may only need reduced fluid intake, while severe cases can require hospital treatment with intravenous salt solutions.

diseases.name: Hypoparathyroidism
diseases.summary: Hypoparathyroidism happens when the parathyroid glands make too little hormone, so the body holds too little calcium and too much phosphate in the blood. Most complaints come from nerves and muscles firing abnormally because calcium is low. It is uncommon, and it is usually managed with calcium and vitamin D supplements.

diseases.name: Hypopituitarism
diseases.summary: Hypopituitarism happens when the pituitary gland in the brain fails to produce enough of one or more of its hormones, which can disrupt growth, reproduction, thyroid function, stress response, and fluid balance. Symptoms often build slowly over months or years, though they can appear abruptly, and depend on which hormones are lacking. Treatment usually involves lifelong hormone replacement, and sudden symptoms with headache or vision changes need urgent care.

diseases.name: Hypoplastic left heart syndrome
diseases.summary: A heart defect present from birth leaves the left ventricle underdeveloped, so it cannot move enough blood, and the right side has to supply both the lungs and the body. Newborns with this problem typically become critically ill within the first days of life, and early recognition and treatment have substantially improved survival.

diseases.name: Hypospadias
diseases.summary: A birth difference in which the urethral opening sits on the underside of the penis rather than at its tip, usually noticed right after delivery. It is common, does not usually make caring for a baby difficult, and surgical repair typically restores normal appearance and urination, with fertility generally preserved.

diseases.name: Hypothermia
diseases.summary: When the body cools faster than it can generate warmth, the core temperature falls well below normal and organs start to slow down. Shaking is often the first sign, and it can progress to muddled thinking, poor coordination, and unconsciousness. Because affected people often fail to recognize their own decline, this needs prompt emergency help.

diseases.name: Hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid)
diseases.summary: This condition slows the body's metabolism because the small gland at the front of the neck produces too little of its key hormone. Symptoms often creep in over years and are easy to mistake for ordinary aging or tiredness. A simple blood test confirms it, and daily hormone replacement tablets generally bring it under control.

diseases.name: Idiopathic hypersomnia
diseases.summary: This is a lasting sleep disorder in which people feel excessively drowsy through the day even after long nights of sleep. Getting up is hard, and people may feel disoriented afterward, while naps rarely bring real rest. The cause is unknown, it usually begins in youth, and sudden urges to sleep can be dangerous during activities like driving.

diseases.name: IgA nephropathy (Berger disease)
diseases.summary: This kidney disorder occurs when an immune protein accumulates in the kidney filters and triggers ongoing irritation that slowly reduces their filtering ability. Many people have few or no signs for years, and it is often found incidentally through urine testing. Progression varies widely, and while there is no cure, treatments and blood pressure control can slow it down.

diseases.name: Illness anxiety disorder
diseases.summary: A long-lasting condition where a person becomes fixated on the belief that they have, or will develop, a serious disease, often after noticing ordinary body sensations or minor changes. The fear persists even when medical checks find nothing serious, and it can strongly disrupt daily life. Counseling and sometimes medication can ease it.

diseases.name: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
diseases.summary: A blood disorder in which the immune system destroys platelets, leaving the body with too few to clot properly. It typically shows up as bruises and small reddish-purple spots on the skin, along with bleeding from the gums, nose, or other places. It is more often seen in young women and can last for years in adults, while children often recover on their own.

diseases.name: Impacted wisdom teeth
diseases.summary: Wisdom teeth that get stuck under the gum line, often because there is no room for them to come through, frequently cause no trouble at all. When they do, the trouble tends to involve the gums and jaw, and they can also lead to decay or damage to neighboring teeth. Pain or problems usually lead to removal, though some dentists suggest removing them preventively.

diseases.name: Impetigo
diseases.summary: A contagious bacterial infection of the outer skin layers that mainly affects young children and spreads easily through touch or shared items. It typically appears as sores around the nose, mouth, or on exposed limbs, and it usually clears with prescribed antibiotics, though it still needs a medical assessment to start treatment.

diseases.name: Incompetent cervix
diseases.summary: A weakened cervix can open too early during pregnancy, which may lead to late loss or preterm delivery. Often there are no warning signs, but some people notice pressure, cramps, or light bleeding, usually before the 24th week. Treatments such as a stitch placed around the cervix, medication, and ultrasound monitoring are used when the problem is identified.

diseases.name: Indigestion
diseases.summary: Indigestion is discomfort or pain in the upper belly that can feel like burning, fullness, or bloating, and it often has no identifiable underlying cause. It tends to come and go and is frequently managed through diet changes, lifestyle adjustments, and sometimes medication. Most mild cases are harmless, but persistent symptoms or warning signs such as weight loss, black stools, or chest pain need prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Infant jaundice
diseases.summary: Yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes in a newborn, caused by a buildup of bilirubin in the blood as the infant's liver is still maturing. It is very common in the first week or two of life and usually resolves on its own, but a doctor should check it promptly to rule out a more serious cause.

diseases.name: Infant reflux
diseases.summary: Spitting up after feeds is very common in babies and usually harmless when the infant is content and gaining weight. It tends to fade by around 18 months. Specific warning signs, such as poor weight gain, forceful vomiting, or blood or green fluid, call for prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Infectious diseases
diseases.summary: Infectious diseases are illnesses caused by microbes such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites that invade the body. They can pass between people, animals, food, water, or the environment. The symptoms depend heavily on which organism is involved and which body system it affects.

diseases.name: Infertility
diseases.summary: Infertility is the inability to conceive after a year or more of regular unprotected intercourse, and it can stem from one partner, both, or a combination of factors. Many people find that medical treatments improve their chances of having a child. Most cases show no signs apart from not becoming pregnant, though some people have menstrual irregularities or hormone-related changes.

diseases.name: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)
diseases.summary: Inflammatory bowel disease is a long-term condition in which the digestive tract becomes chronically inflamed. Its symptoms depend on which part of the gut is involved and how intense the inflammation is. With ongoing specialist care and consistent treatment, many people can keep symptoms under control for extended periods.

diseases.name: Inflammatory breast cancer
diseases.summary: This is an aggressive form of breast cancer that tends to swell the breast and change the skin's color and texture rather than forming a noticeable lump. It typically progresses over weeks to months and is often mistaken for a breast infection, so persistent changes warrant prompt medical evaluation with a tissue sample.

diseases.name: Influenza (flu)
diseases.summary: Influenza is a virus that infects the nose, throat, and lungs and usually spreads during winter months in each hemisphere. Most people recover at home, but it can occasionally lead to serious complications, especially in those with underlying health problems. Symptoms tend to appear quickly, a day or few after exposure.

diseases.name: Ingrown hair
diseases.summary: A hair that was cut or pulled out regrows and bends back into the skin, leading to small tender lumps that can sting or itch. It is most often seen in people with tightly coiled hair who shave closely. Usually it clears up by itself, but medical advice is worth seeking if it lingers or keeps coming back.

diseases.name: Ingrown toenails
diseases.summary: A nail that grows into the surrounding skin, usually at the edge of a big toe, causes pain, tenderness, and swelling there. Pressure from footwear or improper trimming often triggers it, and it can become infected if left alone.
