diseases.summary: A stomach and intestinal illness caused by a highly contagious virus that spreads through contaminated food, water, surfaces, and close contact. It usually comes on suddenly and clears up on its own within a few days, though dehydration is the main risk, especially for young children and older adults.

diseases.name: Obesity
diseases.summary: Obesity is a long-term condition in which a person carries enough excess body fat to threaten their health, typically judged by body mass index or waist size. It raises the likelihood of heart disease, diabetes, and several other chronic illnesses, but even a small drop in weight can meaningfully lower that risk. Diet and activity changes, prescription medications, and surgical options are all available treatments.

diseases.name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)
diseases.summary: This condition involves unwanted, intrusive thoughts or urges that trigger repeated ritual behaviors meant to ease anxiety, though the relief is usually short-lived. The patterns often revolve around themes like contamination, checking, or orderliness, and they can consume substantial time and disrupt daily life. It typically starts in adolescence or early adulthood, tends to fluctuate with stress, and responds well to treatment.

diseases.name: Obstructive sleep apneaSymptoms and causes
diseases.summary: A sleep-related breathing disorder in which the upper airway repeatedly narrows or collapses overnight, briefly cutting off airflow and fragmenting sleep. Bed partners often notice loud snoring and pauses in breathing, while the person usually wakes unrested and drowsy during the day. Left untreated, it can strain the heart and blood pressure over time.

diseases.name: Occupational asthma
diseases.summary: Occupational asthma is a form of asthma brought on by breathing in fumes, dust, gases, or other irritants encountered at work, which sets off airway inflammation and narrowing. Symptoms often appear during or after a work shift and may ease on days away from the job, though they can become lasting if exposure continues. Avoiding the workplace trigger and using medication are central to managing it, since untreated cases can permanently damage the lungs.

diseases.name: Ocular rosacea
diseases.summary: This eye condition is a flare of inflammation that can cause redness, stinging, and itching, and it often shows up in people who also have a facial skin condition that makes them flush easily. It typically appears between ages 30 and 50 and cannot be fully cured, but medication and careful eye hygiene can keep it under control. Eye symptoms sometimes come before any skin changes, so a person may need periodic eye checks if they already have facial rosacea.

diseases.name: Oligodendroglioma
diseases.summary: A slow-growing tumor that arises from the supportive cells of the brain or spinal cord, most often in the brain. Because it grows gradually, it can go unnoticed for years, and its effects depend on where it sits. Seizures are usually the first sign, often followed by headaches, changes in thinking or speech, and numbness or weakness on one side.

diseases.name: Oppositional defiant disorder (ODD)
diseases.summary: A pattern of persistent anger, argumentativeness, and deliberate defiance toward parents and other authority figures, sometimes accompanied by spiteful acts, that usually appears in early childhood and disrupts home life, friendships, and school. Because these behaviors can resemble ordinary willfulness, a professional evaluation is generally needed to distinguish them. Treatment focuses on parenting and behavior skills, with additional support if related conditions are present.

diseases.name: Optic glioma
diseases.summary: A slow-growing tumor along the nerve pathway linking the eyes to the brain, most often seen in young children and frequently linked to neurofibromatosis type 1. It typically shows up first as changes in vision, and sometimes as headache or nausea when pressure builds. Adults who develop it tend to have faster-moving symptoms and need prompt evaluation.

diseases.name: Optic neuritis
diseases.summary: Optic neuritis is inflammation of the optic nerve that usually causes sudden, painful loss or blurring of vision in one eye. It is often linked to autoimmune or demyelinating conditions, and vision commonly improves over weeks, though a doctor should evaluate it promptly.

diseases.name: Oral lichen planus
diseases.summary: A long-term inflammation of the mouth's lining in which the body's defenses mistakenly target the soft tissues. It takes two main forms: a lacy white-patch type that is usually harmless, and a red, sore type that can cause burning and needs ongoing monitoring because of a small added risk of mouth cancer. It is not contagious and is most often found in middle-aged women.

diseases.name: Oral thrush
diseases.summary: A yeast-type infection can overgrow in the mouth and leave pale, raised film-like areas on the tongue or inner cheeks. It is usually mild in otherwise healthy people but tends to be more stubborn and serious in infants, older adults, and people with weakened immunity. Anyone who notices these patches should have a dentist or doctor check them.

diseases.name: Orchitis
diseases.summary: Orchitis is inflammation of one or both testicles, most often caused by an infection such as a sexually transmitted infection or mumps, and it frequently occurs together with infection of the nearby sperm-carrying tube. It usually brings on testicle pain and swelling that can appear quickly, sometimes with fever, an upset stomach, or a general sense of being unwell. Because similar pain can come from a twisted spermatic cord, prompt medical assessment is advised.

diseases.name: Orthostatic hypotension (postural hypotension)
diseases.summary: Orthostatic hypotension is a drop in blood pressure that happens when a person stands up, causing reduced blood flow to the brain. It often leads to lightheadedness or faintness that eases when lying down or sitting. Many cases are linked to dehydration, certain medications, or nervous system problems.

diseases.name: Osteoarthritis
diseases.summary: Osteoarthritis is a long-term condition in which the cushioning cartilage in joints gradually wears down, causing pain and stiffness, mostly in weight-bearing and hand joints. It develops slowly and tends to worsen over years, though symptoms can often be eased with exercise, weight control, and medication. It is typically managed with routine care rather than emergency treatment.

diseases.name: Osteochondritis dissecans
diseases.summary: This is a joint problem in which a small piece of bone and its overlying cartilage separate from the surrounding joint surface. It mostly affects growing children and teenagers who play sports involving jumping, running, or quick turns, and the knee is the joint most often involved. Symptoms tend to worsen gradually and can include pain, catching, or a joint that feels like it is locking.

diseases.name: Osteomyelitis
diseases.summary: A bone infection that can affect one or more segments of a bone, usually reaching it through the bloodstream, nearby infected tissue, or an opening created by injury. It is more likely in people with diabetes, circulation problems, smoking habits, or who have undergone surgery or dialysis, and it is often treated with surgical removal of damaged bone followed by intravenous antibiotics.

diseases.name: Osteoporosis
diseases.summary: Osteoporosis is a gradual thinning of the skeleton in which the body removes old bone faster than it can rebuild it. Many people have no warning signs for years, and the condition often becomes apparent only after a bone breaks or the spine begins to compress.

diseases.name: Osteosarcoma
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins in the bone-forming cells, most often in the long bones of the legs, and it is most often diagnosed in adolescents and young adults. It is uncommon overall, but among primary bone cancers it is the most frequent in young people. Its early signs are easily confused with sports injuries or growing pains, so persistent bone symptoms deserve a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Ovarian cancer
diseases.summary: A cancer that starts in the ovaries and can spread into nearby tissue. It often causes no early warning signs, and when symptoms appear they tend to resemble more ordinary digestive or urinary complaints. Treatment generally combines surgery with chemotherapy.

diseases.name: Ovarian cysts
diseases.summary: Fluid-filled sacs on or within a woman's ovary are very widespread and usually cause no trouble, often disappearing by themselves over several months. Occasionally a larger one leads to a dull or sharp ache low in the belly on one side, or pressure and bloating, and in uncommon cases it can twist or rupture, which is a medical concern.

diseases.name: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
diseases.summary: A complication of fertility medication in which the ovaries overreact to hormone injections and swell up. Fluid can leak from the ovaries into the belly and sometimes the chest, which causes bloating, weight gain, and lower urine output. Most cases are mild and resolve on their own, but severe cases can become dangerous quickly.

diseases.name: Overactive bladder
diseases.summary: Overactive bladder causes sudden, hard-to-control urges to urinate, often leading to frequent trips to the toilet by day and night and sometimes involuntary leakage. It can lead people to withdraw socially, but it is typically manageable through behavioral changes and other treatments. Seeing a clinician is worthwhile when symptoms are bothersome or interfere with daily life.

diseases.name: Paget's disease of bone
diseases.summary: A long-lasting condition where bone is broken down and rebuilt too quickly, producing bone that is larger, softer, and more fragile than normal. Many people have no noticeable signs and it is found by chance, but when symptoms occur they usually involve aching bones and visible changes in bone shape. It mainly affects older adults and is typically managed with medication.

diseases.name: Paget's disease of the breast
diseases.summary: Paget's disease of the breast is an uncommon cancer that starts in the ducts and spreads to the skin of the nipple and areola, often alongside a tumor deeper in the breast. Its early signs look like a persistent skin condition on the nipple that does not heal or respond to usual creams, so it needs prompt medical assessment. It can affect men as well as women.

diseases.name: Painful intercourse in women
diseases.summary: Pain during or around sex in women can come from physical, medical, or emotional causes, and it is far more often reported by women than by others. It can be felt at the vaginal opening, inside the vagina, or deeper in the pelvis, and it often affects relationships and self-image. Seeing a clinician is worthwhile, since treating the underlying cause frequently resolves or reduces it.

diseases.name: Pancolitis
diseases.summary: Pancolitis is a form of ulcerative colitis in which the inflammation spreads across the whole large intestine, though the same term can occasionally describe colon-wide inflammation from other causes such as Crohn's disease or certain infections. The disease alternates between flare-ups and quieter periods, and its severity ranges from mild to severe. Symptoms are mainly digestive, with bloody diarrhea and cramping being the most typical.

diseases.name: Pancreatic cancer
diseases.summary: Pancreatic cancer usually begins in the ducts of this digestive gland and often stays silent until it has progressed. Its warning signs can include abdominal discomfort, unexplained weight loss, and yellowing of the skin or eyes. Risk rises with smoking, long-standing diabetes or inflammation of the pancreas, obesity, and a family history of the disease.

diseases.name: Pancreatic cysts
diseases.summary: Pancreatic cysts are fluid-filled sacs that form in or on the pancreas, an organ behind the stomach that produces digestive enzymes and insulin. Many are found incidentally on imaging done for another reason and cause no symptoms, while others may produce abdominal discomfort or, less often, signs of pancreatitis or obstruction.

diseases.name: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors
diseases.summary: This condition is an uncommon cancer arising from the hormone-making cells of the pancreas, sometimes called islet cell cancer. Many such tumors cause no noticeable problems at first, and some produce excess hormones that trigger a wide range of effects. Anyone with ongoing or worrying symptoms should arrange a medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Pancreatitis
diseases.summary: Inflammation of the pancreas, the gland behind the stomach that aids digestion and blood sugar control, can strike suddenly or develop into a long-lasting condition. Gallstones blocking the bile duct are a frequent trigger, and heavy alcohol use and smoking also raise the odds. The main warning sign is abdominal pain that can spread to the back, often worsening after meals.

diseases.name: Panic attacks and panic disorder
diseases.summary: Panic disorder involves repeated, sudden surges of intense fear that arrive without a real threat and bring strong bodily reactions. A single episode is often a one-time event linked to a stressful period, but recurring attacks and ongoing worry about the next one point to the disorder. The episodes are not physically dangerous, yet they can disrupt daily life and respond well to treatment.

diseases.name: Paraganglioma
diseases.summary: This is a rare tumor that develops from specialized nerve-linked cells scattered through the body, usually in the head, neck, abdomen, or pelvis. Most cases are harmless, though a minority behave aggressively, and some run in families because of inherited gene changes. Symptoms depend on location: tumors in the head and neck can press on nearby structures, while hormone-producing tumors cause episodes of high blood pressure and a racing heartbeat.

diseases.name: Paraneoplastic syndromes of the nervous system
diseases.summary: A group of uncommon disorders where the immune system, reacting to a tumor, mistakenly harms parts of the brain, spinal cord, nerves, or muscles. Symptoms can appear quickly and often show up before the underlying cancer is found. Early medical evaluation matters, since treating the cancer and calming the immune response can limit lasting nerve damage.

diseases.name: Parkinson's disease
diseases.summary: Parkinson's is a long-term brain condition that affects how the body moves and gradually progresses. It usually begins with subtle changes on one side, often a small shake, and tends to spread to both sides over time. Although it can't be cured, medications and sometimes brain surgery can ease the symptoms.

diseases.name: Parotid tumors
diseases.summary: Parotid tumors are abnormal cell growths in the pair of salivary glands located in front of each ear, and most are not cancerous. They typically show up as swelling in the face or jaw, sometimes with trouble swallowing or changes in facial movement. Older adults and people with prior head and neck radiation are at higher risk, and a doctor specializing in ear, nose and throat problems usually evaluates them.

diseases.name: Parvovirus infection
diseases.summary: Parvovirus B19 is a small virus that often causes a mild, childhood illness marked by a bright facial flush. In adults it more often brings on joint aches and tiredness. Most people recover fully without treatment, though the infection can be more serious for pregnant people and for those with certain blood disorders.

diseases.name: Patellar tendinitis
diseases.summary: Patellar tendinitis is an overuse injury where the tendon that links the kneecap to the shinbone becomes irritated and sore, usually from repeated jumping or running. Pain typically sits just below the kneecap and worsens with activity and load, often easing with rest in the early stages. Left untreated, it can become persistent and limit sport or daily movement.

diseases.name: Patellofemoral pain syndrome
diseases.summary: This knee condition causes an aching pain at the front of the knee, centered on the kneecap, and it tends to flare during activities that load the knee. It is especially seen in teenagers, young adults, and active people who run or jump, and it often responds well to simple self-care, though physical therapy sometimes helps. Symptoms usually creep in gradually and can involve one or both knees.

diseases.name: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)
diseases.summary: A heart defect present from birth leaves a vessel-connecting channel that should have closed after delivery still open. Small openings often cause no problems, while large ones can strain the heart and lead to breathing trouble and poor growth in infants. Doctors may monitor small cases and treat larger ones with medication or a closure procedure.

diseases.name: Patent foramen ovale
diseases.summary: A patent foramen ovale is a small leftover opening between the heart's two upper chambers that normally closes shortly after birth but stays partly open in about a quarter of adults. Most people with it never notice any problem. In a minority it can let blood clots or bubbles pass to the arterial side, which may cause stroke-like episodes or breathing trouble when upright.

diseases.name: Peanut allergy
diseases.summary: A peanut allergy happens when the immune system overreacts to peanut protein, usually within minutes of eating or touching it. Reactions range from mild skin or stomach symptoms to a dangerous whole-body reaction called anaphylaxis, which needs emergency treatment. Anyone with a known reaction should check in with a doctor, even if past reactions seemed minor.

diseases.name: Pectus excavatum
diseases.summary: A chest wall difference in which the breastbone is pushed inward, leaving a dip in the front of the chest. Many people have only a cosmetic dip, while others feel heart or breathing effects, especially during growth spurts. Evaluation by a clinician is warranted if symptoms appear or the dip deepens.

diseases.name: Pediatric brain tumors
diseases.summary: Brain growths in children can affect nearby brain function and produce a range of symptoms, with headaches, nausea, and vomiting among the most typical. The specific signs depend on where the growth sits and how fast it enlarges, and tumors vary from slow-growing and harmless to fast-growing and cancerous. Because these symptoms overlap with many other conditions, a child with persistent or worrying signs should be evaluated by a doctor promptly.

diseases.name: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea
diseases.summary: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea happens when a child's airway narrows or closes during sleep, so breathing repeatedly pauses and restarts through the night. It often shows up as loud snoring and restless sleep, and it can also affect daytime behavior, attention and school performance. Enlarged tonsils and adenoids are the most common underlying cause, and early evaluation matters because untreated cases can affect growth, learning and heart health.

diseases.name: Pediatric white blood cell disorders
aliases: White blood cell disorders in children
diseases.summary: In these conditions, a child's blood carries an abnormal number of the immune cells that defend against germs, either below or above the typical range. Low counts usually leave children prone to repeated infections, while high counts often point to an active infection or an allergic, autoimmune, or cancer-related process.

diseases.name: Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
diseases.summary: An infection of the upper female reproductive organs, usually spreading upward from the vagina or cervix through sexually transmitted or other bacteria. It often causes lower belly discomfort, unusual discharge, and pain during sex, and can cause lasting damage to fertility if not treated promptly.

diseases.name: Pelvic organ prolapse
diseases.summary: Pelvic organ prolapse happens when the supportive muscles and tissues of the pelvic floor weaken, letting organs such as the bladder, uterus or rectum slip down into the vaginal area. Many people have no symptoms, while others notice a bulge, pressure, or bladder and bowel changes. It is often managed without surgery, though surgery can be an option.

diseases.name: Pemphigus
diseases.summary: Pemphigus is a small group of uncommon conditions that cause fluid-filled bubbles on the skin and on moist linings such as the inside of the mouth. It usually shows up in middle age or later, and people of certain ancestries face a higher chance. Early detection tends to make it more manageable, typically with long-term medication, while untreated sores may linger or become infected.

diseases.name: Penicillin allergy
diseases.summary: A penicillin allergy is an immune reaction to penicillin-type antibiotics, in which the body treats the drug as a threat. Reactions range from a mild skin reaction to a life-threatening whole-body response, and the most serious ones can begin within minutes of a dose. Many people who carry the label were never truly allergic, and testing can often clarify it.

diseases.name: Peptic ulcer
diseases.summary: An open sore forms on the lining of the stomach or the first part of the small intestine, often caused by a bacterial infection or regular use of anti-inflammatory painkillers. Many people never notice it, while others feel a burning or gnawing ache in the upper belly that can shift with meals. Dark or bloody stools and vomiting blood are signs that medical attention is needed quickly.

diseases.name: Pericardial effusion
diseases.summary: Pericardial effusion is a buildup of extra fluid in the sac surrounding the heart. When the fluid grows large or builds up quickly, it can squeeze the heart and impair its ability to fill and pump blood. Many cases are mild and cause few symptoms, while larger or rapidly forming effusions can be dangerous and need prompt medical evaluation.

diseases.name: Pericarditis
diseases.summary: Inflammation of the thin sac around the heart typically produces a sharp, stabbing chest discomfort that changes with breathing, coughing, or posture. Many cases are mild and resolve on their own, but chest pain always warrants prompt medical evaluation because it overlaps with heart attack and lung problems. Treatment ranges from medication for more serious cases to rarely needed surgery.

diseases.name: Perimenopause
diseases.summary: Perimenopause is the transitional stretch that leads up to a woman's final period, when hormone levels swing unpredictably and monthly cycles become erratic. It usually begins in the forties but can start earlier or later, and it ends once a full year passes without bleeding. Many women notice changes in their cycles, body temperature regulation, sleep, mood, and vaginal or urinary comfort.

diseases.name: Periodontitis
diseases.summary: Periodontitis is a advanced infection of the gums that gradually breaks down the tissue and bone holding teeth in place. It is widespread but largely avoidable through daily cleaning and regular dental visits. Catching it early gives the best chance of stopping the damage.

diseases.name: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
diseases.summary: A heart-muscle weakening that arises around pregnancy or in the months after delivery, leaving the heart unable to pump enough blood and leading to heart failure. Many affected people improve with medication, though some need a transplant if the heart stays severely weak. Early recognition matters because symptoms can worsen quickly.

diseases.name: Peripheral artery disease (PAD)
diseases.summary: Narrowed arteries that limit blood flow to the legs or arms can cause pain while walking and other symptoms, often in the calves. Many people have few or no symptoms at first. Seeing a doctor for a checkup is advised when leg or arm pain or related signs appear.

diseases.name: Peripheral nerve injuries
diseases.summary: Damage to the body's nerves outside the brain and spinal cord can disrupt movement, sensation, and automatic functions like sweating and digestion. Symptoms vary widely depending on which nerve fiber types are affected and how serious the injury is. Prompt medical evaluation matters because early treatment can limit lasting harm.

diseases.name: Peripheral nerve tumors
diseases.summary: Nerve sheath growths that arise in or beside peripheral nerves are usually harmless, though their position determines what a person feels. Symptoms come from the tumor pressing on or irritating the nerve and nearby structures, so they can range from a visible lump to numbness or loss of function. Those with genetic conditions such as neurofibromatosis or schwannomatosis, or prior radiation exposure, face higher risk, and a fast-growing lump warrants prompt medical review.

diseases.name: Peripheral neuropathy
diseases.summary: Nerve damage outside the brain and spinal cord can cause numbness, tingling, and pain, most often in the feet and hands. It can also disrupt balance, muscle strength, sweating, digestion, and bladder control. Early evaluation improves the chances of treating the cause and limiting lasting harm.

diseases.name: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: A fast-moving cancer that begins in mature T lymphocytes, a kind of infection-fighting white blood cell, and usually shows up first in lymph nodes before it can reach other organs. It is a family of distinct subtypes rather than a single disease, and the exact signs can differ depending on which subtype is present.

diseases.name: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI)
diseases.summary: Infection can take hold around an artificial joint such as a hip, knee, shoulder, or elbow, either shortly after the operation or years later. Treatment usually pairs drug therapy with another operation, and delays raise the chance of serious harm. Anyone with a recent joint replacement who notices drainage, worsening pain, or fever should contact their surgeon promptly.

diseases.name: Peritoneal carcinomatosis
diseases.summary: This is a late-stage situation in which cancer from an organ such as the colon, stomach, or ovaries has spread to the lining of the abdominal cavity. Typical complaints involve a swollen, bloated belly, discomfort, appetite loss, and unexplained weight loss. Treatment may combine chemotherapy, surgery, or heated drug delivery directly into the abdomen, and prompt medical evaluation is essential.

diseases.name: Peritonitis
diseases.summary: The lining of the abdominal cavity becomes infected or inflamed, most often from bacteria. It can arise from liver or kidney disease, a perforated organ, or peritoneal dialysis. Without prompt treatment with antibiotics, and sometimes surgery, it can spread through the bloodstream and become life-threatening.

diseases.name: Persistent depressive disorder
diseases.summary: A long-lasting, low-grade form of depression that tends to start in childhood, adolescence, or early adulthood and can persist for years. Its emotional and practical effects often reach into relationships, schoolwork, and job performance, and it can be harder to shake than a typical depressive episode. Talk therapy and medication are commonly used together to manage it.

diseases.name: Persistent post-concussive symptoms (Post-concussion syndrome)
diseases.summary: Some people continue to have problems for months after a mild head injury, well beyond the usual recovery period. The mix of symptoms varies widely from person to person and often includes headaches, dizziness, and difficulty thinking clearly. Treatment aims to ease these symptoms and help people get back to their daily routines.

diseases.name: Personality disorders
diseases.summary: A group of long-standing conditions in which a person's inner expectations and behavior toward others stay rigid across situations, often causing trouble in relationships, work, and daily life. Many people with these conditions do not realize their way of thinking is the source of the problem, and they may blame others for difficulties. Because they are grouped into three clusters with different features, symptoms can look quite different from one type to another.

diseases.name: Pet allergy
diseases.summary: Pet allergy is an immune reaction to proteins found in animal dander, saliva, or urine, most often from cats and dogs. It mainly affects the nose, eyes, and airways, and can also cause skin itching or hives in some people. Symptoms usually appear soon after contact with the animal and can be worse in people who also have asthma.

diseases.name: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
diseases.summary: A rare inherited disorder in which benign growths form along the digestive tract, most often in the small intestine, stomach, and colon. Affected people also develop darkened patches on the lips, inside the mouth, and on the hands and feet, and face a substantially raised lifetime risk of several cancers, so ongoing screening matters.

diseases.name: Peyronie's disease
diseases.summary: A condition in which a firm, scar-like band develops beneath the skin of the penis, leading to bending, discomfort, and sometimes a shorter length. It is not a cancer and usually does not resolve on its own, though early treatment can help prevent worsening and ease symptoms. Anyone whose symptoms appear or bother them or a partner should see a clinician.

diseases.name: Phenylketonuria (PKU)
diseases.summary: PKU is a rare genetic condition in which the body cannot properly process phenylalanine, an amino acid found mainly in protein-rich foods, so it accumulates to harmful levels. Newborns usually show no signs at first, but untreated cases tend to produce problems with the nervous system, skin, and development within months. A lifelong low-phenylalanine diet, started early, prevents most serious complications.

diseases.name: Pheochromocytoma
diseases.summary: A pheochromocytoma is an uncommon, usually noncancerous growth on one of the adrenal glands that releases hormones and drives episodes of very high blood pressure. Many affected people notice episodes of pounding heartbeat, sweating, and headache, while some have no symptoms at all and discover the tumor by chance. Because blood pressure can return to normal between episodes, the condition is easy to miss without specific testing.

diseases.name: Pilocytic astrocytoma
diseases.summary: This is a slow-growing, usually noncancerous brain tumor that starts in star-shaped support cells and is mostly found in children and young people. It tends to form in the back of the brain that governs coordination, though it can also appear along the optic pathways, brainstem, or spinal cord. Symptoms vary with location and often reflect raised pressure in the skull or disrupted nerve function.

diseases.name: Pilonidal cyst
diseases.summary: A pilonidal cyst is a small pocket that forms in the skin just above the buttock cleft, near the base of the spine, and often holds trapped hair and debris. Many people never notice one, but when it becomes infected it can cause significant pain, swelling, and drainage. Doctors typically treat infected cases by draining them, and sometimes a surgical procedure is required.

diseases.name: Pinched nerve
diseases.summary: Pressure on a nerve from nearby bone, cartilage, muscle, or tendon can cause pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness, and the exact symptoms depend on which nerve is involved. Most cases improve within days to weeks with rest and over-the-counter pain relief, though some need surgery. Medical review is advised if symptoms persist for several days despite self-care.

diseases.name: Pineal gland tumor
diseases.summary: A rare growth in the middle of the brain, near the small gland that regulates sleep, can press on nearby tissue and block the normal flow of fluid. Its effects depend on its size, how fast it grows, and where it sits. Most cases appear in children and young adults, and tumor types range from slow-growing to aggressive.

diseases.name: Pineoblastoma
diseases.summary: This is a very rare cancer that begins in the pineal gland, a small structure near the center of the brain that produces melatonin. It grows quickly, can spread through the brain and its surrounding fluid, and is most often diagnosed in young children. Early signs tend to involve headaches, low energy, and changes in vision or eye movement.

diseases.name: Pink eye (conjunctivitis)
diseases.summary: This is an eye condition where the clear lining over the white of the eye and inside the eyelid swells and turns red or pink. It is most often triggered by a virus, though bacteria, allergies, and blocked tear ducts in infants can also cause it. It is usually irritating but rarely damages vision, and it can spread easily when infection is the cause.

diseases.name: Pinworm infection
diseases.summary: A small roundworm infection of the intestines, most often seen in children, that causes itching around the anus, especially at night. It spreads easily through contact with eggs on hands, bedding, and surfaces, and is usually treated with a single over-the-counter medicine.

diseases.name: Pituitary tumors and adenomas
diseases.summary: Pituitary tumors are usually harmless growths in the small gland at the base of the brain that controls hormones. Many cause no problems and are found by chance, while larger ones can press on nearby structures or upset hormone levels. The specific symptoms depend on which hormone, if any, the tumor overproduces.

diseases.name: Pityriasis rosea
diseases.summary: A self-limiting skin eruption that usually begins with one larger patch, followed within days to weeks by many smaller oval, scaly patches that spread across the trunk and limbs. It typically clears on its own over several weeks and is most often seen in young adults and teenagers. Symptoms are generally mild, with itching being the main complaint.

diseases.name: Placenta accreta
diseases.summary: Placenta accreta is a pregnancy complication in which the placenta grows abnormally deep into the uterine wall, so it does not separate normally after birth. It is most often noticed through bleeding during pregnancy or at delivery, and it can lead to dangerous hemorrhage that needs urgent obstetric care.

diseases.name: Placenta previa
diseases.summary: Placenta previa is a pregnancy condition in which the placenta sits low in the uterus, partially or fully covering the cervical opening. It typically shows up as painless vaginal bleeding in the later part of pregnancy and can become dangerous if left unrecognized.

diseases.name: Placental abruption
diseases.summary: Placental abruption is a serious pregnancy complication in which the placenta separates partly or fully from the uterine wall before delivery, cutting off oxygen and nutrients to the baby. It most often appears in the third trimester and can threaten both mother and fetus, so prompt medical evaluation is essential.

diseases.name: Plague
diseases.summary: Plague is a rare but serious infection spread mainly by flea bites from infected rodents, and it can progress quickly if not treated. It shows up in three forms, with symptoms depending on whether the bacteria settle in the lymph nodes, the bloodstream, or the lungs. Prompt antibiotic treatment is essential, and a sudden high fever in someone who has been in an affected area needs urgent medical attention.

diseases.name: Plantar fasciitis
diseases.summary: A common, self-limiting inflammation of the thick tissue along the sole that links the heel to the toes, typically felt as a stabbing heel ache that is worst with the first steps after waking. It becomes more likely with running, excess weight, unusual foot shape, and worn footwear, and it is most often seen in adults aged 40 to 60. Symptoms usually respond to rest and supportive care, though persistent cases warrant a clinical review.

diseases.name: Plantar warts
diseases.summary: A benign skin growth on the sole of the foot, typically caused by a common viral infection that enters through small breaks in the skin. Many cases resolve on their own, particularly in children, though they can be painful when pressed and may need treatment if they persist or spread.

diseases.name: Plasmacytoma
diseases.summary: This is a rare cancer in which antibody-producing immune cells multiply into a single mass, most often within a bone and less often in soft tissue such as the head and neck. Its symptoms depend on where the mass sits, with bone pain and swelling typical of bone involvement and nasal or throat problems typical of soft tissue involvement. Treatment can often eliminate it, but it may return or progress to multiple myeloma, so long-term monitoring is important.

diseases.name: Pleurisy
diseases.summary: Pleurisy is swelling of the membranes that cover the lungs and line the chest wall, producing discomfort that flares with each breath. The pain often eases when breathing is paused, and fluid buildup, partial lung collapse, or infection can accompany it. Respiratory infections, certain autoimmune and blood disorders, and some medications or drugs can trigger it.

diseases.name: Plexiform neurofibroma
diseases.summary: This is a noncancerous nerve-sheath tumor that spreads in a tangled, network-like pattern along several nerve bundles and can extend into skin, fat, bone and muscle. It is strongly tied to neurofibromatosis type 1, appears most often in childhood and adolescence, and usually grows slowly. Its effects depend on where it sits and how much it presses on surrounding structures.

diseases.name: Pneumonia
diseases.summary: Pneumonia is a lung infection that causes the tiny breathing spaces to fill with fluid or pus, making it harder to breathe. Its severity varies widely, from a mild cold-like illness to a dangerous one, with the greatest risk for infants, older adults, and people with weakened immunity or chronic lung or heart disease. Prompt medical assessment matters, especially when fever persists or breathing becomes difficult.

diseases.name: Pneumonitis
diseases.summary: Pneumonitis is inflammation of the lung tissue that is not caused by germs. It happens when the immune system overreacts to an irritant that is inhaled, such as dust, mold, or bird material, or sometimes a drug. Breathing difficulty and a persistent dry cough are typical, and treatment focuses on removing the trigger and calming the inflammation.

diseases.name: Pneumothorax
diseases.summary: A lung collapses when air seeps into the space between the lung and the chest wall, pressing it inward. It can affect all or part of a lung and sometimes happens after an injury, a medical procedure, or lung disease, though it can also occur without a clear reason. Sudden chest pain and breathlessness are the typical warning signs, and severe cases can be life-threatening.

diseases.name: POEMS syndrome
diseases.summary: A rare blood-related disorder in which abnormal plasma cells release a protein that injures nerves and affects several organ systems, with the name standing for its key features. It typically shows up gradually over weeks to months, mostly in people past middle age, and although it has no cure, treatment has become much more effective and early recognition matters a great deal.

diseases.name: Poison ivy rash
diseases.summary: A itchy, blistering skin reaction that follows contact with the oily sap of poison ivy, poison oak, or poison sumac. It typically shows up one to two days after exposure, can persist for a few weeks, and is usually manageable at home, though it needs medical care if it spreads widely, affects the face or genitals, or comes with breathing trouble.

diseases.name: Polio
diseases.summary: Polio is a viral infection that mostly strikes the nerves of the spinal cord and brainstem, and most infected people have no symptoms at all. In a small share of cases it causes flu-like illness, and in rare cases it progresses to muscle weakness, paralysis, or breathing trouble. Vaccination is the main protection, and people who have had polio before should report any new or worsening symptoms to a doctor.

diseases.name: Polycystic kidney disease
diseases.summary: This inherited disorder causes many fluid-filled sacs to form mainly in the kidneys, which gradually enlarge and lose function over time. Many people carry it for years without noticing, and it can also affect the liver and pancreas and lead to high blood pressure or kidney failure.

diseases.name: Polycythemia vera
diseases.summary: A slow blood disorder in which the bone marrow makes too many red blood cells, thickening the blood and raising the risk of clots. Many patients feel tired, have headaches, or itch, and some notice an enlarged belly from an enlarged spleen. Doctors usually find it on routine blood counts and treat it to lower the risk of clots and bleeding.

diseases.name: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS)
diseases.summary: This is a common hormonal disorder in people with ovaries that often appears around the first period, though it can also emerge years later. It is tied to excess androgen activity and trouble with how the body handles insulin, and it commonly disrupts menstrual cycles and fertility. Symptoms range from barely noticeable to significant, and early evaluation can help lower the chance of later metabolic problems.

diseases.name: Polyhydramnios
diseases.summary: Polyhydramnios is a pregnancy condition in which there is too much fluid around the developing baby. It affects roughly 1 to 2 percent of pregnancies and is usually mild, often picked up in the second or third trimester. Mild cases often resolve without intervention, while severe cases may need closer monitoring or treatment.

diseases.name: Polymorphous light eruption
diseases.summary: An itchy skin reaction that shows up on areas exposed to sunlight, usually hours to a day or two after time outdoors. It is most often seen in young adults, especially women, and tends to clear on its own over several days to a couple of weeks. Sun-protected skin is typically unaffected.

diseases.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
diseases.summary: An inflammatory condition causing sudden-onset aching and stiffness in the shoulders, neck, upper arms, and hips, mainly in people over 50. Symptoms are typically worst after rest, such as on waking. It often comes with general signs of illness and responds well to corticosteroid treatment.

diseases.name: Polymyositis
diseases.summary: This is a long-term condition where the body's immune defenses mistakenly target and inflame the muscles used for movement, leading to gradual, symmetrical weakness. It is uncommon, usually appears in middle age, and is more frequently diagnosed in women. Although it has no cure, medication and physical therapy can help restore strength and function.

diseases.name: Popliteal artery aneurysm
diseases.summary: A bulge in the artery behind the knee can go unnoticed for a long time, or it may first show up as calf discomfort during walking. Its main danger is forming a clot that cuts off circulation to the lower leg, which is a medical emergency. It is uncommon and tends to occur in older men, especially those who also have an aneurysm in the body's main abdominal artery.

diseases.name: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome
diseases.summary: A condition where the calf muscle presses on the main artery behind the knee, restricting blood flow to the lower leg and foot. It is uncommon and mostly seen in young, physically active people, especially men. Exercise-related calf pain that eases with rest is the typical clue that prompts an evaluation.

diseases.name: Porphyria
diseases.summary: Porphyria is a small group of inherited conditions in which the body builds up chemicals that normally help make a component of red blood cells. Acute forms tend to strike the nerves and digestive system in sudden episodes, while cutaneous forms cause pain and damage when skin is exposed to sunlight. Many symptoms overlap with more common illnesses, so prompt medical evaluation is recommended.

diseases.name: Portal hypertension
diseases.summary: Portal hypertension is a pressure buildup in the veins that carry blood from the gut toward the liver, typically caused by liver scarring that makes it hard for blood to pass through. Early on it often causes no noticeable signs, and problems usually appear only after complications such as internal bleeding or fluid collecting in the abdomen. Catching and treating the underlying cause early can sometimes allow improvement.

diseases.name: Post-polio syndrome
diseases.summary: A late-onset condition affecting some people who recovered from paralytic polio decades earlier. It tends to bring back weakness and tiredness in muscles that had previously regained function, usually after many years of stability. Care focuses on pacing activity, rehabilitation, and monitoring for complications, since no cure exists.

diseases.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)
diseases.summary: PTSD can develop after someone lives through or sees a deeply frightening event, and its signs can show up within a few months or, less often, years later. Most people recover from the initial shock with time and self-care, but symptoms that persist for over a month and disrupt work, relationships, or daily routines call for professional evaluation. Early treatment tends to ease symptoms and improve day-to-day functioning.

diseases.name: Post-vasectomy pain syndrome
diseases.summary: Post-vasectomy pain syndrome is a long-lasting ache or tenderness in the testicles or scrotum that persists beyond three months after a vasectomy. It can range from a faint, dull discomfort to sharp pain that disrupts daily activities or sexual activity. Because its cause is unknown and no clear risk factors have been identified, anyone who has had the procedure may be affected.

diseases.name: Posterior cortical atrophy
diseases.summary: This is a rare-to-uncommon brain disorder in which nerve cells at the back of the brain gradually degenerate, undermining the ability to interpret what the eyes see and to judge space. Most cases stem from Alzheimer's disease, though other degenerative conditions can cause it too. Memory and thinking tend to decline as the condition advances.

diseases.name: Posterior vaginal prolapse (rectocele)
diseases.summary: A rectocele occurs when the thin partition between the back of the vagina and the rectum loosens, allowing the rectum to press forward into the vaginal canal. Small cases often go unnoticed, while larger ones can make passing stool harder and leave a feeling of pressure. Management usually begins with non-surgical measures, with surgery reserved for cases that significantly disrupt daily life.

diseases.name: Postherpetic neuralgia
diseases.summary: Nerve pain that lingers after a shingles outbreak has cleared is the core problem here. It typically sits on the same patch of skin where the rash appeared and can persist for months. It is most often seen in older adults, and while there is no cure, treatments can help and many people improve over time.

diseases.name: Postpartum depression
diseases.summary: A form of depression that emerges after childbirth and lasts far longer and feels more intense than the brief emotional dip many new parents experience. It can affect fathers as well as mothers, and it may start during pregnancy or up to a year after delivery. Because it can disrupt caring for a baby and handling daily life, it calls for prompt evaluation by a clinician.

diseases.name: Postpartum preeclampsia
diseases.summary: Postpartum preeclampsia is a pregnancy-related blood pressure disorder that appears after delivery, usually within the first couple of days but sometimes up to six weeks later. It can affect the brain, liver, kidneys, and other organs, so it needs prompt medical assessment.

diseases.name: Pouchitis
diseases.summary: Pouchitis is an inflammatory reaction in the reservoir that surgeons build from the small intestine after colon removal, most often in people whose surgery was done for ulcerative colitis. It occurs in roughly half of those who have this procedure. Irritation of the pouch tends to produce bowel symptoms such as loose stools and abdominal discomfort, and it typically responds to medical treatment once a doctor confirms it.

diseases.name: Prader-Willi syndrome
diseases.summary: A rare inherited disorder affecting chromosome 15 that changes how the body handles appetite, growth, muscle tone and learning across a lifetime. Babies often feel floppy and feed poorly, while older children and adults struggle with constant hunger and weight gain. A team of specialists is usually needed to manage it well.

diseases.name: Precocious puberty
diseases.summary: Precocious puberty means a child's body starts developing into an adult body earlier than expected for their age. It can bring growth spurts, body hair, and other physical changes, and while the cause is often unknown, some cases are linked to underlying medical problems. Treatment usually involves medication to slow the process down.

diseases.name: Prediabetes
diseases.summary: Prediabetes is a stage where the body's cells respond poorly to insulin, so blood sugar runs higher than normal but not yet high enough to count as diabetes. It usually causes no obvious signs, and the main warning sign that is sometimes visible is darker patches of skin in body folds. Those risks climb with excess body fat, a large waist, inactivity, and family history.

diseases.name: Preeclampsia
diseases.summary: A pregnancy complication that usually begins after the 20th week, marked by raised blood pressure along with signs that another organ, often the kidneys or liver, is being strained. It can also appear shortly after delivery. Because it can worsen quickly and put both mother and baby at risk, prompt medical evaluation is essential.

diseases.name: Premature birth
diseases.summary: A baby arriving before 37 weeks of pregnancy is considered premature, and the earlier the arrival, the greater the chance of health complications. Newborns in this situation often need specialized hospital care to help with breathing, feeding, and keeping warm. Carrying multiples, short gaps between pregnancies, and certain medical conditions can raise the likelihood.

diseases.name: Premature ejaculation
diseases.summary: Ejaculating sooner than desired during sexual activity is a widespread and treatable concern that many men face at some point. Occasional early climax is normal, and it becomes a medical concern when it happens most of the time and causes distress or avoidance of intimacy. Anxiety about performance, stress, and difficulty keeping an erection can all contribute, and medication, counseling, and delay techniques often help.

diseases.name: Premature ventricular contractions (PVCs)
diseases.summary: Premature ventricular contractions are extra heartbeats that start in the lower chambers of the heart and arrive earlier than the next expected beat. Most people are unaware of them, though some notice a skipped or pounding sensation in the chest. They are usually harmless, but frequent episodes or those with other heart disease can need evaluation.

diseases.name: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)
diseases.summary: A recurring set of physical and emotional changes that appear in the days before a period and typically ease once bleeding starts. The intensity varies widely, and for a minority of people the emotional symptoms are severe enough to disrupt daily life.

diseases.name: Presbyopia
diseases.summary: Presbyopia is an age-linked decline in the eyes' capacity to bring nearby objects into focus, and most people notice it somewhere past their fortieth birthday. It typically shows up as trouble reading small print or doing close work, which can be addressed with reading glasses or other corrective options.

diseases.name: Prescription drug abuse
diseases.summary: Taking a prescription medicine in a way the prescriber did not intend, such as using someone else's pills, exceeding the dose, or crushing tablets to snort or inject, can turn into a repeated pattern despite clear harm. It affects people of every age and is most common among teens and young adults, usually involving painkillers, anxiety or sleep medicines, or stimulants. Addressing it early with a health care provider can help prevent it from becoming a full addiction.

diseases.name: Preterm labor
diseases.summary: Early labor before the 37th week of pregnancy can lead to a baby being delivered prematurely, and the earlier that happens, the more health problems the baby may face. The cause is often unclear, though certain medical and pregnancy-related factors raise the odds. Anyone with possible early warning signs should contact their clinician promptly so it can be confirmed or ruled out.

diseases.name: Priapism
diseases.summary: Priapism is a prolonged, painful erection of the penis that continues for hours without sexual stimulation or desire. It is a urological emergency because prolonged blood trapping can damage penile tissue and cause lasting erectile dysfunction. Prompt medical treatment is needed to relieve the blood buildup.

diseases.name: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC)
diseases.summary: A long-term liver condition in which the immune system slowly destroys the small bile ducts, so bile backs up and gradually scars the liver. Many people feel no symptoms at diagnosis, but tiredness and itching usually show up as the damage progresses. It is most often seen in middle-aged and older women, especially in North America and Northern Europe.

diseases.name: Primary immunodeficiency
diseases.summary: This is a group of inherited conditions in which parts of the immune system are missing or do not work properly, leaving the body poorly equipped to fight germs. People often have infections that come back, last longer than usual, or are caused by unusual organisms. Signs often start in infancy or childhood, although milder forms may not be recognized until adulthood.

diseases.name: Primary lateral sclerosis (PLS)
diseases.summary: Primary lateral sclerosis is an uncommon disorder in which the nerves that carry movement signals from the brain slowly deteriorate, leading to gradual stiffness and weakness, most often starting in the legs. It is closely related to ALS but tends to progress more slowly and is usually not life-threatening. Symptoms build over years and can eventually affect speech, swallowing, and the hands.

diseases.name: Primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma
diseases.summary: This is an aggressive form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that starts in immune B-cells in the central chest and forms a bulky tumor there. The growing tumor can press on nearby airways, the esophagus, and the major vessel returning blood from the upper body to the heart, causing breathing, swallowing, and swelling problems along with general signs such as fever and sweating. It is most often found in people during their thirties and forties.

diseases.name: Primary ovarian insufficiency
diseases.summary: This hormonal condition means the ovaries begin to underperform before age 40, producing less estrogen and releasing eggs irregularly, which often makes conceiving difficult. Its signs overlap with menopause, but affected people may still have periods for years and can sometimes become pregnant. Hormone treatment can restore estrogen and help guard against bone thinning and heart disease.

diseases.name: Primary progressive aphasia
diseases.summary: This is a rare, slowly progressing brain disorder in which language abilities decline, usually beginning before age 65, and it belongs to the frontotemporal dementia family. Over time people may struggle to find words, understand speech or writing, or form sentences, though many keep up daily self-care for years. Most affected people eventually develop dementia.

diseases.name: Primary progressive apraxia of speech (PPAOS)
diseases.summary: This is a slowly progressing brain disorder in which the brain struggles to plan and coordinate the movements needed for speech, even though the mouth muscles themselves are not weak. Speech gradually becomes slower, harder to form, and less understandable, and in time some people lose the ability to talk. It begins in adulthood, usually after age 40, and most often after 65.

diseases.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)
diseases.summary: A long-term liver disorder in which the small tubes that drain bile become inflamed, scarred, and narrowed, gradually impairing liver function. Many people feel no symptoms at first, and it is closely tied to inflammatory bowel disease. Liver transplant is the only cure for advanced cases.

diseases.name: Proctitis
diseases.summary: Proctitis is swelling and irritation of the lining of the rectum, the last part of the large bowel. It can be caused by inflammatory bowel disease, sexually transmitted infections, or radiation therapy. Typical complaints are discomfort in the back passage, bleeding, and a constant need to go without much result.

diseases.name: Progeria
diseases.summary: Progeria is a very rare inherited condition that makes children age far faster than normal, with signs appearing in the first couple of years of life. Babies typically look healthy at birth, then gradually show slowed growth, loss of body fat and hair, and changes to the skin. Heart and blood vessel disease is the main threat, and most affected children do not survive past their mid-teens; treatment today focuses on easing symptoms.

diseases.name: Progressive supranuclear palsy
diseases.summary: This is a rare, progressively worsening brain disorder that damages nerve cells controlling movement, balance, eye motion, and swallowing, and it resembles Parkinson's disease. It typically begins in a person's sixties or seventies, and no cure exists, so care centers on easing symptoms and preventing complications such as pneumonia.

diseases.name: Prolactinoma
diseases.summary: A prolactinoma is a noncancerous tumor of the pituitary gland, a small structure at the base of the brain, that releases too much prolactin, the hormone that signals the breasts to make milk. The excess hormone disrupts sex hormone balance, so many symptoms involve menstrual, sexual, or breast changes. As the tumor grows, it can press on nearby nerves and cause headaches or vision problems.

diseases.name: Prostate cancer
diseases.summary: Prostate cancer is a malignant growth that begins in the prostate gland, a small male reproductive organ, when cells develop changes that let them multiply uncontrollably. It is one of the more frequently diagnosed cancers in men, and it is often treatable when found early. Early disease frequently causes no noticeable problems, so screening is commonly recommended for men at higher risk.

diseases.name: Prostate cancer recurrence
diseases.summary: When prostate cancer returns after initial treatment, the first clue is usually a climbing PSA level in blood work, often before any scan can show it. Many people have no noticeable symptoms at this stage, and later signs such as bone pain or unexplained weight loss tend to appear only once the disease has grown. Anyone who has been treated for prostate cancer and notices worrying changes should contact their care team promptly.

diseases.name: Prostatitis
diseases.summary: An infection or long-lasting inflammation of the prostate gland can make urination painful or difficult and cause discomfort in the pelvis, groin, or genitals. Some cases are caused by bacteria, while others have no detectable infection. Because several other conditions can produce similar symptoms, a prompt medical evaluation is important.

diseases.name: Pseudobulbar affect
diseases.summary: A neurological condition causes sudden bouts of laughing or crying that a person cannot control and that often do not match the moment or their actual mood. It most often arises after brain injury or in people with certain progressive brain or nerve diseases. It is frequently confused with depression or bipolar disorder, so a specialist evaluation is important.

diseases.name: Pseudocholinesterase deficiency
diseases.summary: Pseudocholinesterase deficiency is an inherited shortage or dysfunction of a blood enzyme that normally clears certain muscle-relaxing anesthetic drugs. Most people who carry it never notice any problem. It usually comes to light after surgery, when a standard relaxant lingers far longer than expected and leaves the patient weak and struggling to breathe.

diseases.name: Pseudogout
diseases.summary: Pseudogout is a form of inflammatory joint disease in which calcium-containing crystals build up inside joints, producing sudden flares of swelling and pain. The condition becomes more likely with advancing age and after joint trauma or surgery, and its flares can persist for days to weeks. Because the presentation can look like gout, a medical evaluation is advisable when a joint suddenly becomes hot, swollen and hard to use.

diseases.name: Pseudomembranous colitis
diseases.summary: This is an inflammation of the large bowel that usually follows a course of antibiotics, when a toxin-producing bacterium overgrows and damages the colon lining. It can range from mild, short-lived symptoms to a serious, fast-moving illness. Prompt medical evaluation is important because complications such as dehydration and bowel dilation can develop quickly.

diseases.name: Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension)
diseases.summary: This is a condition where fluid pressure inside the skull rises without an identifiable cause, mostly affecting younger women with higher body weight. Its main effects come from pressure on the optic nerve and from headaches that are often worse in the morning or when lying down. Vision problems are the main reason for urgent evaluation, since untreated pressure can lead to permanent vision loss.

diseases.name: Psoriasis
diseases.summary: A long-lasting skin condition in which skin cells renew far too quickly, producing thick, scaly, itchy patches that tend to flare and then calm down over time. It has no cure, but treatments and lifestyle strategies can keep it under control, and it often begins in childhood or runs in families.

diseases.name: Psoriatic arthritis
diseases.summary: Psoriatic arthritis is an inflammatory joint disease that affects some people who have psoriasis, a chronic skin condition. It typically causes painful, swollen joints and can also involve tendons, nails, and the spine. Symptoms often flare and remit, and early treatment helps limit lasting joint damage.

diseases.name: Pubic lice (crabs)
diseases.summary: Pubic lice are tiny parasitic insects that live in coarse body hair, most often in the genital area, and spread mainly through close sexual contact. The main complaint is itching that tends to be worse at night, often with small bluish spots or visible lice and nits on the skin or hair. The infestation is usually easy to treat with topical medicine.

diseases.name: Pulmonary atresia
diseases.summary: A heart defect present from birth in which the valve sending blood from the heart to the lungs fails to form properly, so the connection is blocked. Babies depend on temporary vessels that normally close after delivery, and the condition is usually detected in the first days of life and requires urgent surgical and medication treatment.

diseases.name: Pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect
diseases.summary: A heart defect present at birth in which the pulmonary valve fails to form, blocking blood flow from the right ventricle to the lungs, together with a hole between the heart's two pumping chambers. Without treatment, oxygen levels fall progressively, so surgical or catheter repair is needed, and symptoms usually show up in the first days or weeks of life.

diseases.name: Pulmonary edema
diseases.summary: Fluid builds up in the air sacs of the lungs, making it hard to move air and exchange oxygen. This usually results from the heart failing to pump effectively, though other injuries or exposures can cause it. It can escalate quickly and needs prompt medical attention.

diseases.name: Pulmonary embolism
diseases.summary: A lung blockage happens when a clot travels, most often from a leg vein, and lodges in a lung artery, cutting off blood supply to part of the lung. It can be fatal, but quick treatment markedly improves the outlook. Any sudden breathing trouble, chest discomfort, or fainting warrants immediate emergency evaluation.

diseases.name: Pulmonary fibrosis
diseases.summary: A progressive lung condition in which the delicate air spaces become stiff and scarred, making it harder to draw in enough oxygen. It tends to worsen over time, though the pace varies widely between individuals, and it is most often seen in middle-aged and older adults.

diseases.name: Pulmonary hypertension
diseases.summary: Pulmonary hypertension is a form of high blood pressure inside the lungs' arteries, caused by vessels becoming stiff, narrowed, or lost, which forces the heart's right side to work harder. It tends to progress slowly and can eventually weaken the heart, though treatments can ease symptoms and extend life. Early signs are easy to miss and often resemble other conditions, so a medical evaluation is important.

diseases.name: Pulmonary valve disease
diseases.summary: A problem with the pulmonary valve, the gate between the right lower heart chamber and the lung artery, can narrow it, let blood leak backward, or leave it unformed from birth. These changes disrupt how blood reaches the lungs and may be noticed in infancy or only later in life. Chest discomfort, breathlessness, tiredness, and fainting are the main warning signs that call for a medical check.

diseases.name: Pulmonary valve stenosis
diseases.summary: A narrowing of the pulmonary valve, which controls blood flow from the heart to the lungs, usually present from birth. Mild cases often cause no problems, while more significant narrowing makes the heart work harder and can reduce how much a person can exert themselves. Severity and symptoms vary widely between individuals.

diseases.name: Pyloric stenosis
diseases.summary: This is a blockage at the outlet of the stomach caused by thickening of the ring-shaped muscle that normally lets food pass into the small intestine. It is an uncommon condition that appears in young infants, usually within the first several weeks of life. Untreated, it can lead to dehydration and poor weight gain, and it is typically corrected with surgery.

diseases.name: Pyoderma gangrenosum
diseases.summary: This is an uncommon skin condition believed to involve an overactive immune response, where a small lump can quickly evolve into a large, tender open wound, usually on the lower limbs. It is more often seen alongside certain bowel, joint, and blood disorders. Treatment typically brings it under control, but healing often leaves marks and new wounds can appear elsewhere.

diseases.name: Rabies
diseases.summary: Rabies is a viral illness usually passed on by an animal's saliva, most often through a bite. It begins with flu-like complaints and can progress to inflammation of the brain, bringing confusion, agitation, and trouble swallowing. Once nerve symptoms appear it is nearly always fatal, so any possible exposure needs urgent medical care.

diseases.name: Radiation enteritis
diseases.summary: Radiation enteritis is irritation and swelling of the bowel that can follow radiation treatment aimed at the abdomen or pelvis. Its digestive symptoms usually fade within weeks of finishing treatment, but in some people they linger or appear months or years later. Long-lasting cases can lead to anemia or a blocked bowel.

diseases.name: Radiation sickness
diseases.summary: Radiation sickness is harm to the body from taking in a large amount of radiation, usually over a short period. How bad it gets depends on the dose absorbed and which body parts were exposed. Early signs often show up within hours to days and can be followed by a quiet stretch before more serious problems appear.

diseases.name: Ramsay Hunt syndrome
diseases.summary: Ramsay Hunt syndrome happens when the chickenpox virus reactivates in a facial nerve ganglion, causing inflammation of that nerve. It typically brings ear pain and a blistering rash along with weakness on one side of the face. Early antiviral treatment improves the chances of recovering facial movement and hearing.

diseases.name: Raynaud's disease
diseases.summary: Raynaud's is a condition where extremities such as the fingers and toes temporarily lose circulation when chilled or emotionally stressed, causing color shifts, numbness, and tingling. It shows up more often in women and in people living in cold regions, and while it is usually not disabling, it can reduce comfort and daily quality of life.

diseases.name: Reactive arthritis
diseases.summary: Reactive arthritis is an inflammatory joint condition that tends to appear a few weeks after an infection in the gut or urinary or genital tract. It usually involves swelling in the large joints of the legs, often together with eye irritation and skin or urinary changes. Most people recover within several months, though some have symptoms that linger or come back.

diseases.name: Reactive attachment disorder
diseases.summary: Reactive attachment disorder is a rare condition in young children whose early caregiving was severely disrupted, often through neglect or repeated changes in caregivers. Affected children tend to hold back from forming close emotional bonds and often do not look to adults for comfort when distressed. A child psychologist or psychiatrist usually makes the diagnosis after a full developmental assessment.

diseases.name: Rectal cancer
diseases.summary: Rectal cancer begins as abnormal cell growth in the final part of the large intestine, just before the anal opening. It often causes no noticeable signs at first, and when symptoms do appear they are usually linked to bowel changes or bleeding, so anyone with worrying symptoms should see a doctor for evaluation.

diseases.name: Rectal prolapse
diseases.summary: A condition in which the lower part of the bowel slides down and pushes out through the anal opening, often triggered by straining. It is usually uncomfortable rather than an immediate danger, but it generally needs a surgical fix rather than medicine alone. Older adults and women are affected more often, and long-term constipation is a common contributor.

diseases.name: Rectovaginal fistula
diseases.summary: A passage between the rear bowel and the vagina lets gas or stool escape through the vaginal opening. It often follows childbirth injury, inflammatory bowel disease, pelvic radiation or cancer, pelvic surgery, or diverticulitis. Small ones may cause little trouble, while larger ones can cause leakage and hygiene problems, and most need surgical repair.

diseases.name: Recurrent bladder cancer
diseases.summary: When bladder cancer returns, it most often does so within two years of treatment, though it can appear much later. It may reappear inside the bladder, where it is often fully removable, or spread elsewhere in the body, where a cure is usually not possible but treatment can prolong life. Symptoms depend on the location, with urinary changes being typical for bladder recurrence and general or bone-related complaints suggesting spread.

diseases.name: Recurrent breast cancer
diseases.summary: Breast cancer that returns after initial treatment, either in the breast or chest wall, in nearby lymph nodes, or in distant organs such as bone, liver, or lungs. Where it reappears shapes the signs a patient notices, and local or regional returns may be curable, while distant spread is usually managed rather than cured. Regular follow-up exams help catch a return early.

diseases.name: REM sleep behavior disorder
aliases: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
diseases.summary: A sleep condition in which a person acts out dreams during the sleep stage when the body is normally kept still, leading to shouting, limb jerks, and sometimes injury to themselves or a bed partner. It often starts gradually, tends to worsen over time, and can be an early sign of certain brain disorders affecting movement and memory.

diseases.name: Renal artery stenosis
diseases.summary: Narrowing of the arteries feeding the kidneys reduces blood supply to them, which can impair their filtering and fluid removal and push blood pressure upward. It often causes no noticeable signs until it is well advanced, and is frequently found incidentally or when blood pressure is unusually hard to control. Risk is closely tied to general vascular disease factors such as age, smoking, high cholesterol, and diabetes.

diseases.name: Residual limb pain
diseases.summary: Pain can persist in the stump left behind after a limb is removed, and it affects a large share of people who have had an amputation. It often starts within days of surgery, though it can also appear years later. Some people improve without treatment, while others need medical management.

diseases.name: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
diseases.summary: RSV is a very widespread airborne virus that usually causes a mild, cold-like illness in older children and adults. In infants, older adults, and people with heart or lung conditions, it can inflame the small airways and make breathing difficult, sometimes requiring hospital care.

diseases.name: Restless legs syndrome
diseases.summary: RLS is a nervous-system condition that produces a strong, hard-to-resist need to move the legs, usually because of an uneasy or achy sensation inside them. Symptoms tend to show up in the evening or overnight during rest, and moving brings temporary relief. It often disrupts sleep and daytime functioning.

diseases.name: Retinal detachment
diseases.summary: A sudden separation of the light-sensing back layer of the eye can cause permanent vision loss if it is not treated quickly. Early warning signs often include new floating specks, light flashes, and a dark curtain in the side vision. Anyone with these changes should be examined by an eye specialist without delay.

diseases.name: Retinal diseases
diseases.summary: Problems affecting the inner rear lining of the eye can blur, distort, or dim eyesight, and some lead to permanent loss if they go untreated. Abrupt changes such as drifting specks, brief light streaks, or sudden dimming call for prompt attention. Early assessment by an eye specialist gives the best chance to protect or recover vision.

diseases.name: Retinoblastoma
diseases.summary: A cancer that begins in the light-sensitive tissue at the back of the eye, mostly affecting very young children, usually found before age two. It typically involves one eye but can involve both, and most children can be treated without losing the eye. The outlook is generally very favorable.

diseases.name: Retractile testicle
diseases.summary: A testicle that slides between the scrotum and the groin, and can often be coaxed back into the scrotum by hand, is usually harmless. In most boys the movement stops on its own around puberty, leaving the testicle settled in the scrotum for good. Occasionally it stays up in the groin, which is a different situation that still calls for a check-up.

diseases.name: Retrograde ejaculation
diseases.summary: A man has an orgasm but little or no semen comes out, because it flows backward into the bladder instead of exiting through the penis. This is usually linked to nerve or bladder-neck problems, certain medications, diabetes, or prior prostate or bladder surgery. It is typically harmless on its own, but it is worth a doctor's review to find the cause.

diseases.name: Retroperitoneal sarcoma
diseases.summary: A rare cancer of the soft connective tissue in the abdominal space behind the organs, it often grows large before it causes noticeable problems. Its signs depend on where the mass presses, such as swelling in the legs, back or belly discomfort, or early fullness. Surgical removal is the main treatment when the tumor can be fully taken out, with radiation or drugs used in some cases.

diseases.name: Rett syndrome
diseases.summary: Rett syndrome is a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder that almost always affects girls and usually appears after a period of apparently normal early development. It typically causes gradual loss of hand skills and spoken language, along with repetitive hand movements, breathing irregularities, and seizures. Care is multidisciplinary and focuses on managing symptoms and supporting movement, communication, and nutrition.

diseases.name: Reye's syndrome
diseases.summary: Reye's syndrome is a rare but dangerous illness that causes swelling in the liver and brain, mainly in children and teenagers recovering from a viral infection. It typically appears a few days after flu or chickenpox and has been associated with aspirin use during those illnesses. Because it can progress to seizures and unconsciousness, it requires prompt emergency medical attention.

diseases.name: Rhabdomyosarcoma
diseases.summary: A rare soft tissue cancer arising in muscle-forming cells that can start nearly anywhere in the body, most often in children and teenagers. Outlook depends on age, tumor location and size, and whether it has spread. Early signs are usually a lump or swelling, and the symptoms that appear depend on where the tumor grows.

diseases.name: Rheumatic fever
diseases.summary: This inflammatory illness can follow an untreated throat infection caused by group A streptococcus, typically appearing a few weeks later. It can affect the joints, skin, heart, and brain, and in some cases leaves lasting heart damage. Prompt antibiotic treatment of strep infections is the main way to prevent it.

diseases.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
diseases.summary: Long-term autoimmune inflammatory disorder in which the immune system attacks the lining of the joints, causing pain, warmth and swelling that often appear on both sides of the body. Without good treatment it can erode bone and deform joints, and it can also affect skin, eyes, lungs, heart and blood vessels. Symptoms tend to come and go in flares and quiet periods, and early diagnosis makes a real difference in outcomes.

diseases.name: Rickets
diseases.summary: This is a bone disorder in children, usually caused by a lack of vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate, that stops bones from mineralizing properly as they grow. The softened bones can bend and deform, most often in the legs, wrists, and spine. Growth delay and muscle weakness are also typical.

diseases.name: Right-sided heart failure
diseases.summary: Right-sided heart failure occurs when the heart's lower right pumping chamber weakens, so blood and fluid back up into the abdomen and lower limbs. Early treatment can ease symptoms and extend life, but the condition can become dangerous and occasionally requires advanced devices or transplantation.

diseases.name: Ringworm (body)
diseases.summary: A common fungal skin infection that affects the trunk, arms, or legs despite its name, which has nothing to do with worms. It usually shows up as a round, itchy patch that gradually expands while its center starts to fade. Most cases clear up well with antifungal creams or tablets.

diseases.name: Ringworm (scalp)
diseases.summary: Scalp ringworm is a fungal infection of the hair-bearing skin of the head, caused by dermatophytes.
